rows.requirement_summary: Within Effective_Period (both ends included, an unspecified end open), Present_Value is the current value of the best-priority Exception_Schedule element in effect today whose current value is not NULL (priority 1 best, the lower array index breaking a tie); an element is in effect when its inline calendar entry matches today or the Calendar it references is TRUE today, resolved once per pass through the database. Failing that, today's Weekly_Schedule element if its current value is not NULL; failing that, Schedule_Default, which may be NULL. A list's current value is that of its latest time-value at or before the current time (seconds and hundredths included, entry order irrelevant), and none before the first. Outside Effective_Period nothing is calculated or written and Present_Value keeps its last value. Entering the period, the first pass after start-up included, writes the value to the references even when unchanged; afterwards only a change is written, or the current value after a change of the references or the priority (BACNET-12-SCHEDULE-WRITES). Present_Value is calculated even without references, and Out_Of_Service suspends it, a client's written value taking its place (BACNET-12-SCHEDULE-WRITES). Time-values and Schedule_Default hold primitive datatypes only. The server evaluates every 60 seconds from one Device clock frame, and evaluates a Schedule at once after a write to it commits.

notes: Refs #1028. Before, evaluate applied every exception whatever its period, ignored Calendar references and Effective_Period, treated a NULL time-value as a value, and returned an Octet String of the raw time-value bytes, which commandable targets refused.

Local choices: the weekday used for Weekly_Schedule and matching is computed from the local date, so an inconsistent weekday octet in the clock cannot split the two; a Calendar reference to a missing object or a non-Calendar is never in effect; the setters refuse non-specific or repeated times (DUPLICATE_ENTRY, as 12.24.7 and 12.24.8 ask of written days), non-primitive values and out-of-range priorities and entries.

Network writes of Weekly_Schedule, Exception_Schedule and Effective_Period, with the immediate evaluation after them, are BACNET-12-SCHEDULE-WRITES (#1057), and the CONFIGURATION_ERROR evaluation of 12.24.13 is BACNET-12-SCHEDULE-RELIABILITY (#1056).

Present_Value writes while Out_Of_Service and their write-through to the references (12.24.14) are BACNET-12-SCHEDULE-WRITES (#1055). Not covered: remote references; and evaluation finer than the 60-second pass (a scheduled time takes effect at the next pass, not exactly at its time).
evidence: #1028. Within `Effective_Period` (ends included, unspecified ends open) Present_Value is the best-priority special event in effect today whose current value is not NULL (inline calendar entry matching, or the referenced Calendar TRUE; the lower array index breaks a tie), else today's weekly entry if not NULL, else `Schedule_Default`.

A list's current value is its latest time-value at or before now. Outside the period nothing is calculated or written. Entering it (start-up included) writes even an unchanged value. Time-values are typed, so Present_Value and the target writes carry the scheduled datatype, at `Priority_For_Writing` (locally settable, default 16); NULL relinquishes.

Breaking: before, every exception applied whatever its period, Calendar references and `Effective_Period` were ignored, NULL counted as a value, and Present_Value was an Octet String of the raw bytes.

Evidence: `crates/bacnet-objects/src/schedule/evaluation_tests.rs`, `crates/bacnet-server/src/schedule_tests.rs`, `crates/bacnet-endpoint/src/source_reporter_schedule_tests.rs`. rows.requirement_summary: WriteProperty, WritePropertyMultiple and write_local accept Weekly_Schedule, Exception_Schedule and Effective_Period whole, and one element of either array by index. The value is decoded with the shared constructed codecs and checked by the functions the local setters use: a non-specific time or an event priority outside 1 to 16 is VALUE_OUT_OF_RANGE, a time repeated within one list DUPLICATE_ENTRY, an element of another datatype INVALID_DATA_TYPE, a malformed element INVALID_DATA_ENCODING, and a refusal leaves the property unchanged. Weekly_Schedule stays seven elements (a whole write of another count is VALUE_OUT_OF_RANGE, index 0 WRITE_ACCESS_DENIED); writing Exception_Schedule index 0 resizes it, appended elements being special events without time-values, up to 1,024 events (NO_SPACE_TO_WRITE_PROPERTY). Once a write to a Schedule commits, the server runs that Schedule's evaluation at once under the same database guard, through the tick's code, and fans COV out for the targets it writes. While Out_Of_Service is TRUE, Present_Value takes any primitive value, NULL included (INVALID_DATA_TYPE otherwise; WRITE_ACCESS_DENIED in service), and every accepted value goes to the references at Priority_For_Writing, a NULL relinquishing, in that same pass, ahead of any calculated value and without needing a clock. Out of service neither the tick nor a content write replaces it; back in service the calculation takes over at once. List_Of_Object_Property_References (whole, as a read returns it) and Priority_For_Writing (an Unsigned from 1 to 16, VALUE_OUT_OF_RANGE otherwise) are writable the same three ways (#1088): a list member naming any Device but the server's own is OPTIONAL_FUNCTIONALITY_NOT_SUPPORTED (12.24.10), while one naming the server's own Device is stored, and reads back, as the local reference it stands for (#1122), a member of another datatype INVALID_DATA_TYPE, a malformed one INVALID_DATA_ENCODING, more than 1,024 members NO_SPACE_TO_WRITE_PROPERTY, and a refusal changes nothing. After a change the pass it triggers sends the current Present_Value to the new list at the new priority, if the Schedule is writing at all (in service, only inside Effective_Period; out of service, at once), and relinquishes with a NULL at the old priority every slot the Schedule holds that the change leaves behind: each dropped reference, or every reference when the priority moves. The Schedule holds slots from a write of a non-NULL value until it leaves Effective_Period. AddListElement and RemoveListElement edit the list and hand the result to the same whole-list write (#1121), so an accepted edit triggers the same pass: a member already held, or repeated in the request, changes nothing and is no failure; a member the list lacks is LIST_ELEMENT_NOT_FOUND; an element that does not decode as a reference INVALID_DATA_TYPE; a member past the 1,024 cap NO_SPACE_TO_ADD_LIST_ELEMENT and one in another device OPTIONAL_FUNCTIONALITY_NOT_SUPPORTED, each ChangeList-Error naming the request element; and a refused request changes nothing.

notes: Refs #1057. Before, all three properties answered WRITE_ACCESS_DENIED. The server hands the three properties to the object as raw bytes (index 0 of the arrays stays an Unsigned), and the object also takes the List of ApplicationData a read returns, so a read value writes back unchanged.

Local choices: the INVALID_DATA_TYPE / INVALID_DATA_ENCODING split follows the Date_List precedent, keyed on the element's first tag; an event priority outside 1 to 16 decodes, since the shared codec checks only structure, and is VALUE_OUT_OF_RANGE as from add_exception, per the 15.9.1.3 split and the Date_List precedent (#1087; it was INVALID_DATA_ENCODING before); an appended Exception_Schedule element has a wholly unspecified date and priority 16, which never supplies a value; the 1,024-event cap matches Date_List and now applies to add_exception too; any committed write to a Schedule, not only to these properties, triggers the immediate evaluation, which writes only a changed value or on entering Effective_Period.

DATATYPE_NOT_SUPPORTED is never returned: every primitive datatype is accepted and a mixed configuration is reported through Reliability (BACNET-12-SCHEDULE-RELIABILITY), so a client can move a Schedule to another datatype one property at a time.

#1055: before, Present_Value answered WRITE_ACCESS_DENIED in every state. Local choices: every accepted Present_Value write is sent on, even of the value already held, and several before one pass send the last; the value goes out whatever Effective_Period or a later Out_Of_Service says, so a WritePropertyMultiple that writes it and then returns the object to service delivers it ahead of the calculation; the return to service writes the calculated value only when it differs from Present_Value, which by then matches what the targets were last sent. A value written on the object directly, outside the server's write paths, goes out at the next tick through BACnetObject::take_owed_schedule_writes (take_simulated_schedule_write until #1088).

#1088: before, List_Of_Object_Property_References and Priority_For_Writing answered WRITE_ACCESS_DENIED; Table 12-28 leaves their writability to the implementation. The server hands the list to the object as raw bytes, an empty list included.

Local choices: a member naming a Device was refused even when it named this device, since the object stores and serves local references only (#1122 accepts that case); relinquishing what a change leaves behind keeps no command at a priority no writer owns any more, and limiting it to slots the Schedule still holds keeps an out-of-season Schedule from clearing the command of the seasonal Schedule that 12.24.6 lets share its references and priority; a NULL Present_Value holds no slot, having relinquished already; every accepted write counts as a change, so the current value is sent again even when nothing changed; add_object_property_reference now returns Result for the same 1,024 cap. Not covered: references in other devices (refused).

#1121: before, AddListElement and RemoveListElement of the list answered WRITE_ACCESS_DENIED. The handler decodes the elements with a reference codec, edits the stored list (whole-element comparison, all or nothing) and writes it back through the Schedule's whole-list write, which now names the member it refuses (Error::Structured with FirstFailedElementNumber), so the relinquish and owed-write rules and the refusals are the WriteProperty ones; WriteProperty and WritePropertyMultiple keep the plain class and code on the wire.

Local choices: an element that does not decode is INVALID_DATA_TYPE for both services, as for every list codec (BACNET-15-LIST-ELEMENT-SEMANTICS), though the whole-list write tells a foreign datatype from a malformed member; a remote member is never stored, so removing one is LIST_ELEMENT_NOT_FOUND; a pure-duplicate add still writes the list back, and the pass resends the current value, harmlessly.

#1122: 12.24.10 only lets a Schedule limited to its own device refuse references to objects outside it. The Schedule object cannot tell which Device holds it, so the server, which selects the local Device under the write's database guard, drops a Device identifier naming that Device from each member before the object decodes the value (WriteProperty, WritePropertyMultiple, write_local and both list services); teaching the object the identifier would have needed a new BACnetObject hook and keeping every Schedule in step with the Device set.

A Device at the wildcard instance names no device and is never local. A read returns the stored local form, so a member written with and without the identifier is one member to the list services. Direct callers of ScheduleObject::write_property still get every Device member refused. Staging's Target_References gets the same rewrite since #1136 (BACNET-12-STAGING-TARGET-REFERENCES).
evidence: #1057. WP, WPM and `write_local` accept `Weekly_Schedule`, `Exception_Schedule` and `Effective_Period` whole, and one array element by index, decoded with the shared constructed codecs and checked by the setters' own functions: a non-specific time or an event priority outside 1 to 16 is VALUE_OUT_OF_RANGE (the codec decodes any Unsigned priority, #1087), a repeated time in one list DUPLICATE_ENTRY, an element of another datatype INVALID_DATA_TYPE, a malformed one INVALID_DATA_ENCODING, and a refusal changes nothing.

`Weekly_Schedule` stays seven days (other counts VALUE_OUT_OF_RANGE, index 0 WRITE_ACCESS_DENIED); `Exception_Schedule` index 0 resizes it with empty events, up to 1,024 (NO_SPACE_TO_WRITE_PROPERTY, `add_exception` too). A committed write to a Schedule runs its evaluation at once through the tick's code, with COV for the targets. DATATYPE_NOT_SUPPORTED is never returned; mixed datatypes show in Reliability.

#1055: while `Out_Of_Service` is TRUE, Present_Value takes any primitive value, NULL included (INVALID_DATA_TYPE otherwise; WRITE_ACCESS_DENIED in service), and every accepted write goes to the references at `Priority_For_Writing` in that same pass, NULL relinquishing, ahead of any calculated value and without a clock; neither the tick nor a content write replaces it, and the return to service hands back to the calculation at once.

Evidence: `crates/bacnet-objects/src/schedule/write_tests.rs`, `crates/bacnet-objects/src/schedule/out_of_service_tests.rs`, `crates/bacnet-server/src/server/schedule_write_tests.rs`, `crates/bacnet-server/src/schedule_tests.rs`. Not covered: network writes of the references and `Priority_For_Writing`.

rows.requirement_summary: A Staging object's Target_References is a BACnetARRAY of BACnetDeviceObjectReference, written whole or one element by index over WriteProperty, WritePropertyMultiple and write_local, with its length fixed after construction. The object commands only targets inside its own device, so a written element naming any other Device is PROPERTY / OPTIONAL_FUNCTIONALITY_NOT_SUPPORTED and the array and its targets stay as they were. An element whose Device member names the server's own Device is a reference into this device: the server stores it, and a read returns it, in the local form without the Device member, and the current stage is re-applied at once, so a new target is commanded at Priority_For_Writing (#1136).
notes: Refs #1136. Before, every element carrying a Device identifier was refused, even one naming this device, which 12.62.14 does not permit: like 12.24.10 for the Schedule, it lets a property limited to its own device refuse only references outside it.

The rewrite is the Schedule's (BACNET-12-SCHEDULE-WRITES), generalized in local_references.rs over both reference types: the server, which selects the local Device under the write's database guard, drops a Device member naming that Device from each element before the object decodes the value.

A Device at the wildcard instance names no device and is never local. StagingObject written directly, or configured through StagingConfig, still refuses every Device member, since it cannot tell which Device holds it. Target_References is an array, so the list services do not apply. Not covered: targets in other devices (refused; the object issues no remote writes).

rows.standard_anchor: Clause 12.24.13 Reliability, 12.24.12 Status_Flags and 12.24.14 Out_Of_Service (printed311-312/PDF313-314); output rule in 12.24.4 (printed309/PDF311); reference writes in 12.24.10 (printed311/PDF313)
rows.requirement_summary: Reliability is CONFIGURATION_ERROR while the non-NULL values in Weekly_Schedule, Exception_Schedule and Schedule_Default are not all of one datatype, or while a referenced property refused the last value of the schedule's datatype written to it with INVALID_DATA_TYPE or DATATYPE_NOT_SUPPORTED (#1086), and NO_FAULT_DETECTED again once neither holds; Status_Flags FAULT follows it. The check runs on every change to those properties, from the local setters or a network write, on the return to service, and in the fault detector's pass. The object clears only a fault it raised: a Reliability applied through set_reliability_internal, or simulated while Out_Of_Service is TRUE, is left alone. A misconfigured Schedule keeps evaluating and writing its references. Present_Value is outside the check: a value written while Out_Of_Service counts for nothing, and a simulated Reliability doesn't hold its write to the references back. The schedule pass reports every target write through BACnetObject::complete_schedule_write, one ScheduleTargetOutcome per reference: a refusal raises the reference half, a later accepted write to that target or its removal from the list clears it, and a NULL, a value of another datatype or any other failure counts for nothing.

notes: Refs #1056. Before, nothing evaluated a Schedule's Reliability. Datatypes compare by PropertyValue variant, so Real, Unsigned and Enumerated differ. Writes continue under CONFIGURATION_ERROR because 12.24.4 sends every change to the references and keeps going past a failing member, while 12.24.13 only reports the condition; the multi-state objects treat their CONFIGURATION_ERROR as report-only too.

#1086: the second condition of 12.24.13, that every referenced property accept the datatype, is judged from the writes (the issue's option B) rather than checked beforehand: the objects publish no datatype per property, so an eager check would have to guess from a target's current value or probe it with a write.

The cost is that the fault shows at the first write rather than at configuration time; 12.24.13 already lets a remote member's fault wait for a write. Local choices: only a refusal of a value whose datatype the schedule itself holds counts, so a NULL, or an out-of-service value of another datatype, raises nothing; any other failure leaves a member's standing as it was; the flag combines with the contents check under the one ownership rule, so a Reliability set by the application or a client simulation is never cleared by it.

rows.standard_anchor: Clause 6.2

notes: Reserved-bit negative tests remain required: reserved control bits still only log a warning. #1141 covers malformed address lengths. The NPDU codec holds DLEN and SLEN to NpduAddress::MAX_MAC_LEN, 18 octets, the same bound as BACnetAddress::MAX_MAC_LEN (#1124).

Table 6-2 (Clause 6.2.2.2) needs at most 7 octets for any standard data link, and the longest MAC this stack serves is the 18-octet B/IPv6 form. decode_npdu refuses a longer length with NpduDecodeError::AddressTooLong before reading the address octets, whether or not they are present, and reports the NPDU's DNET when it has one.

For an over-long DADR it also reports the SNET/SADR behind it, read past the DLEN octets the frame announces, when a complete and valid one is there (#1158), so the router can address its reject; encode_npdu refuses a longer address with Error::Encoding (the limit was 255).

The non-router NetworkLayer drops such an NPDU before APDU or control admission and counts it in address_length_drops(); a non-router sends no reject. The router side is under BACNET-6-ROUTER-MESSAGES. Tests feed hand-built wire bytes for each address field: 19 and 255 are refused, 1, 6 and 18 decode and re-encode unchanged.
evidence: NPDU codec and network layer paths exist.

rows.standard_anchor: Clauses 6.4-6.6
rows.requirement_summary: Router discovery, route tables, network messages, reject reasons, busy/available messages, and broadcast forwarding behavior.
notes: Needs in-memory or Docker multi-network conformance evidence.

#1141: an NPDU whose DLEN or SLEN is past NpduAddress::MAX_MAC_LEN (18) is neither forwarded nor delivered locally, and BACnetRouter::address_length_drops() counts it. When it names a specific DNET, the router rejects it with Reject-Message-To-Network reason 6 (ADDRESSING_ERROR, Clause 6.4.4, which covers an invalid DADR or SADR length) for that DNET, addressed like its other rejects (#1158, below).

A global broadcast draws no reject, as elsewhere in this router, and an NPDU without a DNET has no network to name, so both are only dropped. In-memory loopback tests cover both address fields: the reject, the 18-octet boundary forwarded intact through a learned route, and the silent drops, each fenced by the next frame on every port and the local queue.

#1158: every reject the router originates (reason 1 for an unknown or unreachable DNET, 2 for a busy one, 3 for an unknown message type, 6 for an over-long address) goes through one helper, send_reject in router/reject.rs.

Per Clause 6.4.4 a reject is meant for whoever first sent the refused message, which that message's source fields identify. When the refused NPDU carries SNET/SADR, the reject names that node as its DNET/DADR with hop count 255 and goes back out the arrival port as a unicast to the link sender, the router that relayed the NPDU; without SNET/SADR it stays a local unicast to the sender.

For reason 6, decode_npdu reports the SNET/SADR behind an over-long DADR. When the SADR is the over-long field, or nothing usable follows the DADR, the originator cannot be addressed, and the reject falls back to a local unicast to the link sender, the only node that can be told.

A received reject is relayed by its DNET/DADR through the normal forwarding path (Clauses 6.5 and 6.6.3.5): stripped and unicast to the DADR when the DNET is directly connected, otherwise passed to the next hop with one hop spent.

One with no DNET, the global DNET, the arrival network or an unrouted DNET stops at this router, and nothing answers a reject. Before #1158 the relay took the received reject's SNET/SADR for the originator.

Loopback tests compare every reject byte for byte, relayed and local, for each call site that originates one, plus the reason-6 fallback, the relay, and a two-router chain that carries a reject from the far router back to the device.

notes: Split child of BACNET-12-OBJECT-MODEL (#980). Breaking pre-1.0 retype, on the wire and in the Rust API: Landing_Call_Control was a raw Enumerated and Landing_Calls an Unsigned count, and the unused public BACnetAssignedLandingCalls is removed (#1052 brings the name back with its Clause 21 shape for the Lift's Assigned_Landing_Calls).

Local policies: before any write Landing_Call_Control reads a placeholder of floor 0 with direction UNKNOWN, because the datatype has no empty form; the application owns Landing_Calls through set_landing_calls, and a Landing_Call_Control write doesn't add to it, since only the supervisory controller knows when a call becomes active or is served; following the Clause 15.9.1.3 error table, a well-formed member that exceeds its type (floor-number or destination above 255, a direction of 2^32 or more) is VALUE_OUT_OF_RANGE, like a direction above 65535, while a malformed member anywhere in the value takes precedence as INVALID_DATA_ENCODING; the codec reports the former as a local Error::OutOfRange (not a Protocol error, which would read as a remote Error-PDU) and the object maps it to PROPERTY / VALUE_OUT_OF_RANGE.

The object accepts the write either as one ApplicationData or as the service decoder's one-element-per-member List, as the Loop reference properties do. Not covered here: the object's property set, which BACNET-12-ELEVATOR-GROUP-PROPERTY-SET covers (#997: Machine_Room_ID added, Group_ID held to Unsigned8, and Status_Flags, Out_Of_Service and Reliability removed), the footnote that limits Group_Mode and both landing-call properties to groups of lifts, and any dispatching behavior.
evidence: Split child of `BACNET-12-OBJECT-MODEL` (#980). `Landing_Call_Control` holds one `BACnetLandingCallStatus` (floor [0], direction [1] or destination [2], optional floor-text [3], unframed) and `Landing_Calls` a `BACnetLIST` of them, replacing a raw Enumerated and an Unsigned count (breaking on the wire; the unused public `BACnetAssignedLandingCalls` is removed).

`Landing_Call_Control` stays writable (12.58.10) and refuses non-constructed values with INVALID_DATA_TYPE, undecodable or trailing bytes with INVALID_DATA_ENCODING, and a well-formed call whose floor-number or destination exceeds 255 or whose direction is reserved or above 65535 with VALUE_OUT_OF_RANGE (Clause 15.9.1.3), atomically, over WP and WPM.

`Landing_Calls` is read-only and application-owned (`set_landing_calls`); a control write doesn't add to it. Before any write the control reads floor 0 / UNKNOWN. Evidence: `crates/bacnet-encoding/src/constructed/tests/landing_call_status.rs`, `crates/bacnet-objects/src/elevator/tests/landing_calls.rs`, `crates/bacnet-server/src/handlers/tests/elevator_landing_calls.rs`. Not covered: the object's property set (`BACNET-12-ELEVATOR-GROUP-PROPERTY-SET`, #997), the lift-group presence footnote, and dispatching.

rows.standard_anchor: Clause 12.58 and Table 12-76; Clause 15.5 ReadProperty, Clause 15.7 ReadPropertyMultiple and Clause 15.9.1.3 WriteProperty errors
rows.requirement_summary: The Elevator Group serves the rows Table 12-76 defines. Machine_Room_ID is a required BACnetObjectIdentifier naming the Positive Integer Value object that holds the number of the group's machine room, or instance 4194303 when the room has no number; it is readable, and a network write is refused with PROPERTY / WRITE_ACCESS_DENIED. Group_ID is a required Unsigned8, and a write above 255 is refused with PROPERTY / VALUE_OUT_OF_RANGE without changing the stored value. Group_Members is a BACnetARRAY of BACnetObjectIdentifier: read without an index it is the whole array, at index 0 the member count, at index n the n-th member, and past the last member PROPERTY / INVALID_ARRAY_INDEX; it is read-only over the network. Status_Flags, Out_Of_Service and Reliability are not Table 12-76 rows, so they are absent from Property_List, the property metadata, RPM ALL and OPTIONAL, and the PICS rows, and ReadProperty, ReadPropertyMultiple and WriteProperty on any of them fail with PROPERTY / UNKNOWN_PROPERTY.
notes: Split child of BACNET-12-OBJECT-MODEL (#997). Breaking pre-1.0 removal: Elevator Group used to serve Status_Flags, Out_Of_Service and Reliability through the shared common read arms, all three listed as required, with a routed Out_Of_Service write; now they are unknown properties.

The object has no COV support, event state or intrinsic reporting, and the server's COV flag capture, event-notification payloads, GetAlarmSummary, GetEventInformation and GetEnrollmentSummary already treat an object without these properties as absent, so none needs an Elevator Group case.

Local policies: the application sets Machine_Room_ID through set_machine_room_id, which refuses a reference to any object type other than Positive Integer Value with VALUE_OUT_OF_RANGE, as set_landing_calls does for a reserved direction; Group_ID stays network-writable, since an R row leaves writability to the implementation, and is stored as a u8, so neither the constructor (which starts it at 0) nor any local path can hold a larger value.

Group_Members used to answer every array index with the whole list (#1034); it now goes through the shared BACnetARRAY reader the Lift's arrays use, and stays application-owned through add_member. This row covers the served property set only.

It makes no claim that the Machine_Room_ID object exists in the device, nor for the footnote that limits Group_Mode and both landing-call properties to groups of lifts, the audit, tag and profile rows, or any dispatching behavior.
evidence: Split child of `BACNET-12-OBJECT-MODEL` (#997). Elevator Group serves only Table 12-76 rows. `Machine_Room_ID` (required `BACnetObjectIdentifier`) names the Positive Integer Value object holding the machine room's number, or instance 4194303 when there is none; it reads over RP and RPM, refuses WP with WRITE_ACCESS_DENIED, and the application sets it with `set_machine_room_id`, which refuses any other object type with VALUE_OUT_OF_RANGE.

`Group_ID` (required Unsigned8) stays writable, is stored as `u8`, and refuses a write above 255 with VALUE_OUT_OF_RANGE without mutation. `Status_Flags`, `Out_Of_Service` and `Reliability` are absent from `Property_List`, the metadata, RPM `ALL`/`OPTIONAL` and PICS, and RP, RPM and WP on them return PROPERTY / UNKNOWN_PROPERTY (breaking: they used to read fixed or stored values and `Out_Of_Service` took writes).

The object has no COV, event state or intrinsic reporting, and COV, event-notification and alarm/event summary consumers already treat these properties as absent. Evidence: `crates/bacnet-objects/src/elevator/{metadata.rs,tests/group_properties.rs}`, `crates/bacnet-server/src/handlers/tests/{elevator_properties.rs,read_rpm/elevator.rs,property_metadata/elevator.rs}`, `crates/bacnet-server/src/pics/property_metadata_tests/elevator.rs`. Scope: the served property set only; no claim that the `Machine_Room_ID` object exists, nor for the lift-group presence footnote, the audit, tag and profile rows, or dispatching.

rows.standard_anchor: Clause 12.59 and Table 12-77; Clause 21 BACnetLiftCarDirection; Clause 23.1 Table 23-1; Clause 15.9.1.3
rows.requirement_summary: The Lift object's Car_Moving_Direction is a BACnetLiftCarDirection. Its named values UNKNOWN (0), NONE (1), STOPPED (2), UP (3), DOWN (4) and UP_AND_DOWN (5), and the proprietary range 1024..=65535 that Table 23-1 opens for this enumeration, are accepted on write and read back unchanged. A reserved value (6..=1023) or one above 65535 is refused with PROPERTY / VALUE_OUT_OF_RANGE, and a value that isn't Enumerated with PROPERTY / INVALID_DATA_TYPE, both without changing the stored value. A new Lift reads STOPPED.
notes: Split child of BACNET-12-OBJECT-MODEL (#998). The write check used to admit only 0..=3, numbered as if 1 were STOPPED and 3 DOWN, so DOWN, UP_AND_DOWN and every proprietary value were refused, and a new Lift read NONE (1) where STOPPED was meant.

The value is now stored as the LiftCarDirection newtype, as #932 did for the other enumerated fields, and the domain check is the one the Escalator enumerations and the landing-call direction share. The Car_Moving_Direction description lists UNKNOWN, STOPPED, UP and DOWN as the values the property takes; the write check follows the datatype and also accepts NONE and UP_AND_DOWN, leaving that choice to the application.

Car_Moving_Direction stays writable in service and out of service, as before. The Lift's other Table 12-77 rows and datatypes are BACNET-12-LIFT-PROPERTY-SET (#1021). Car_Assigned_Direction, which shares the datatype and domain check, is BACNET-12-LIFT-PROPERTY-SET (#1052). Not covered here: intrinsic reporting.
evidence: Split child of `BACNET-12-OBJECT-MODEL` (#998). `Car_Moving_Direction` is stored as `LiftCarDirection` (#932 pattern) and accepts the six named values 0..=5 and proprietary 1024..=65535; reserved 6..=1023 and values above 65535 fail with VALUE_OUT_OF_RANGE and non-Enumerated values with INVALID_DATA_TYPE, atomically, over the object API and WP.

The old check admitted only 0..=3, numbered as if 1 were STOPPED, so DOWN, UP_AND_DOWN and proprietary values were refused and a new Lift read NONE (1); it now reads STOPPED (2). The property description lists four of the six named values; the check follows the datatype and leaves the choice to the application.

Evidence: `crates/bacnet-objects/src/elevator/tests/lift_car_moving_direction.rs`, `crates/bacnet-server/src/handlers/tests/{elevator_properties.rs,read_rpm/elevator.rs}`. The Lift's other Table 12-77 rows and datatypes are `BACNET-12-LIFT-PROPERTY-SET` (#1021). Not covered: `Car_Assigned_Direction` and intrinsic reporting.

rows.standard_anchor: Clause 12.59 and Table 12-77, including Out_Of_Service, Energy_Meter and Energy_Meter_Ref; Clause 12.1.5.1; Clause 21 BACnetDoorStatus, BACnetLandingDoorStatus, BACnetAssignedLandingCalls, BACnetLiftCarCallList, BACnetLiftCarDirection, BACnetLiftCarDoorCommand, BACnetLiftCarMode, BACnetLiftCarDriveStatus, BACnetLiftFault, BACnetEngineeringUnits and BACnetDeviceObjectReference; Clause 23.1; Clause 15.5 ReadProperty, Clause 15.7 ReadPropertyMultiple and Clause 15.9.1.3 WriteProperty errors
rows.requirement_summary: The Lift serves only rows Table 12-77 defines, each with its table datatype. The required Elevator_Group (BACnetObjectIdentifier, Elevator Group instance 4194303 when no group lists the lift), Group_ID and Installation_ID (Unsigned8), Passenger_Alarm (BOOLEAN) and Fault_Signals (BACnetLIST of BACnetLiftFault) are present. Car_Position is an Unsigned8, and a write above 255 is refused with PROPERTY / VALUE_OUT_OF_RANGE without changing the stored value. Car_Load is a REAL, served together with Car_Load_Units as the table's presence footnote requires. Car_Door_Status is a BACnetARRAY of BACnetDoorStatus and Landing_Door_Status a BACnetARRAY of BACnetLandingDoorStatus, both with one element per car door, and Floor_Text is a BACnetARRAY of CharacterString; all three take an array index. While Out_Of_Service is TRUE, Car_Door_Status and Landing_Door_Status take WriteProperty of the whole array or one element, as item (c) of the Out_Of_Service description requires; the size stays the car door count, so a write of index 0 is refused with PROPERTY / WRITE_ACCESS_DENIED, a whole array of another size with VALUE_OUT_OF_RANGE and an index past the last door with INVALID_ARRAY_INDEX. A door status outside BACnetDoorStatus or a floor number above 255 is VALUE_OUT_OF_RANGE, a value of the wrong datatype INVALID_DATA_TYPE and an undecodable landing-doors frame INVALID_DATA_ENCODING, none changing either array; in service both refuse writes with WRITE_ACCESS_DENIED. The optional Assigned_Landing_Calls (BACnetARRAY of BACnetAssignedLandingCalls), Making_Car_Call (BACnetARRAY of Unsigned8), Registered_Car_Call (BACnetARRAY of BACnetLiftCarCallList) and Car_Door_Command (BACnetARRAY of BACnetLiftCarDoorCommand) are per-door arrays of the same size as Car_Door_Status, and Car_Assigned_Direction (BACnetLiftCarDirection), Car_Door_Zone (BOOLEAN), Car_Mode (BACnetLiftCarMode), Next_Stopping_Floor (Unsigned8) and Car_Drive_Status (BACnetLiftCarDriveStatus) are single values. All nine refuse writes in service with WRITE_ACCESS_DENIED and take them while Out_Of_Service is TRUE, as items (c) and (d) of the Out_Of_Service description require, under the same array rules as the door arrays; a floor number above 255, a direction, mode or drive status outside its named values and the Clause 23.1 proprietary range, or a door command other than NONE, OPEN or CLOSE is VALUE_OUT_OF_RANGE, a value of the wrong datatype INVALID_DATA_TYPE and an undecodable landing-calls or floor-numbers frame INVALID_DATA_ENCODING, none changing the property. Fault_Signals takes named faults and the Clause 23.1 proprietary range without repeats. Energy_Meter_Ref is a BACnetDeviceObjectReference, read-only over the network, and while it names an instance other than 4194303 Energy_Meter reads 0.0 and refuses any other value with VALUE_OUT_OF_RANGE. Tracking_Value and Floor_Number are not Table 12-77 rows, so they are absent from Property_List, the property metadata, RPM ALL and OPTIONAL and the PICS rows, and ReadProperty, ReadPropertyMultiple and WriteProperty on them fail with PROPERTY / UNKNOWN_PROPERTY.
notes: Split child of BACNET-12-OBJECT-MODEL (#1021). Breaking pre-1.0 wire changes: Car_Position stored any Unsigned, Car_Load was an Unsigned percentage capped at 100, Car_Door_Status an empty list of Unsigned and Landing_Door_Status an Unsigned floor count; Tracking_Value and Floor_Number (an alias of it) were served and Tracking_Value took writes; the five required rows and Car_Load_Units were missing.

Rows are listed in table order. Local policies: the table gives no row a W code, so writability is the implementation's choice. Elevator_Group, Group_ID and Installation_ID (shared with the Escalator through one membership model), Car_Load_Units, Energy_Meter_Ref and Floor_Text are read-only over the network; the application sets the first five with LiftObject setters, which refuse an Elevator_Group of another object type or units above 65535 with VALUE_OUT_OF_RANGE and no change.

Car_Door_Status and Landing_Door_Status are application-owned in service, set with set_car_door_status and set_landing_door_status, which refuse a door status outside BACnetDoorStatus or a Landing_Door_Status whose size differs from Car_Door_Status; set_car_door_status sets the car door count and resizes Landing_Door_Status to match.

While Out_Of_Service is TRUE both also take simulation writes (#1035, metadata WhenOutOfService, PICS writable); the array size isn't network-writable (Clause 12.1.5.1 leaves that to the implementation), as for the Staging arrays, so the two arrays always have the same size.

An element arrives as one Enumerated or one landing-doors frame, and a one-door car's whole array as that bare element; the landing-door codec reports a well-formed floor number above 255 or door status above 32 bits as a local Error::OutOfRange, which the object maps to VALUE_OUT_OF_RANGE, as the landing-call codec does.

Car_Position, Car_Moving_Direction, Car_Load, Passenger_Alarm, Energy_Meter and Fault_Signals take writes in service and out of service, like the Escalator status family. Energy_Meter_Ref (#1036, shared with the Escalator in energy_meter.rs) has the O code and no write requirement and records how the installation is metered, so it is application-owned: set_energy_meter_ref takes an Accumulator, Pulse Converter, Analog Input, Analog Value, Large Analog Value, Integer Value, Positive Integer Value or proprietary object type (128-1023, vendor meters), local or with a Device identifier, and refuses other object types or a non-Device device with VALUE_OUT_OF_RANGE (the clause names no types; this is the set whose Present_Value is a measured number in engineering units).

A reference to instance 4194303 clears it. Setting a reference zeroes Energy_Meter, and a write of anything but 0.0 is refused while it is set. A new Lift has one car door with status UNKNOWN and no landing doors reported, Car_Load 0.0 in PERCENT, Passenger_Alarm FALSE, no faults and an uninitialized Energy_Meter_Ref (Accumulator 4194303, no device).

The call, door-command and car-state rows (#1052) follow the door arrays: application-owned in service through LiftObject setters, which refuse a size other than Car_Door_Status's or a value outside the row's range with VALUE_OUT_OF_RANGE, simulation writes only while Out_Of_Service is TRUE (metadata WhenOutOfService, PICS writable), and the per-door arrays resized with the door count (a new door has no assigned or registered calls, a Making_Car_Call of 0, which the Making_Car_Call description gives for a door with no call yet, and a Car_Door_Command of NONE).

Making_Car_Call and Car_Door_Command describe a write as a passenger request, but the table gives them no W code, so in-service writes stay refused and the application applies requests itself; reverting a command to NONE once it has run is the application's, through set_car_door_command.

The landing-calls and floor-numbers codecs report a well-formed floor number above 255 or direction above 32 bits as Error::OutOfRange, mapped to VALUE_OUT_OF_RANGE, as the landing-door codec does, and share its floor-pair helper.

Directions, modes and drive statuses follow their datatypes (named values plus 1024..=65535) rather than the narrower value lists some descriptions give, as Car_Moving_Direction does; BACnetLiftCarDoorCommand has no Table 23-1 entry, so only its three named values are in range.

A new Lift reads UNKNOWN for Car_Assigned_Direction, Car_Mode and Car_Drive_Status, FALSE for Car_Door_Zone and 1, its car position, for Next_Stopping_Floor. Not covered: the unserved optional rows (Car_Door_Text and the deck rows), the Status_Flags OVERRIDDEN flag for Making_Car_Call, Car_Door_Command and Car_Mode, the Floor_Text size rule, Elevator_Group consistency with the group's Group_Members, that Energy_Meter_Ref names an object that exists, intrinsic reporting, and dispatching.
evidence: Split child of `BACNET-12-OBJECT-MODEL` (#1021). The Lift serves only Table 12-77 rows, in table order, each with its table datatype. It gains the required `Elevator_Group` (Elevator Group instance 4194303 until set), `Group_ID` and `Installation_ID` (Unsigned8), `Passenger_Alarm` (Boolean, FALSE) and `Fault_Signals` (a `BACnetLIST` of `LiftFault`: named 0..=16 and proprietary 1024..=65535, no repeats), and `Car_Load_Units` (PERCENT until set), which the table requires alongside `Car_Load`.

`Car_Position` is an Unsigned8 and refuses a write above 255 with VALUE_OUT_OF_RANGE without mutation; `Car_Load` is a REAL that refuses non-finite values; `Car_Door_Status` is a `BACnetARRAY` of `BACnetDoorStatus` and `Landing_Door_Status` a `BACnetARRAY` of `BACnetLandingDoorStatus` (new `bacnet-types` type and `bacnet-encoding` codec), both one element per car door, and `Floor_Text` is a `BACnetARRAY`; all three take an array index.

`Tracking_Value` and `Floor_Number` are not table rows and now fail RP, RPM and WP with UNKNOWN_PROPERTY (breaking, as are the four datatype changes). The membership rows, `Car_Load_Units`, the door arrays and `Floor_Text` are read-only over the network; the application sets them with `LiftObject` setters that refuse another object type, units above 65535, a reserved door status, or a `Landing_Door_Status` size other than `Car_Door_Status`'s, and `set_car_door_status` resizes `Landing_Door_Status` to the door count.

`Car_Position`, `Car_Moving_Direction`, `Car_Load`, `Passenger_Alarm`, `Energy_Meter` and `Fault_Signals` take writes in service and out of service. The door arrays take simulation writes while `Out_Of_Service` is TRUE (#1035).

#1052 adds the optional `Assigned_Landing_Calls`, `Making_Car_Call`, `Registered_Car_Call` and `Car_Door_Command` (per-door `BACnetARRAY`s resized with the door count; new `BACnetAssignedLandingCalls` and `BACnetLiftCarCallList` types and codecs) and `Car_Assigned_Direction`, `Car_Door_Zone`, `Car_Mode`, `Next_Stopping_Floor` and `Car_Drive_Status`, all application-owned in service through `LiftObject` setters and written over the network only while out of service, as items (c) and (d) of the Out_Of_Service description require.

Evidence: `crates/bacnet-objects/src/elevator/{lift.rs,membership.rs,doors.rs,door_values.rs,car_state.rs,metadata.rs,tests/lift_properties.rs,tests/lift_door_simulation.rs,tests/lift_car_calls.rs,tests/lift_car_state.rs,tests/group_membership.rs}`, `crates/bacnet-encoding/src/constructed/tests/{landing_door_status.rs,assigned_landing_calls.rs,lift_car_call_list.rs}`, `crates/bacnet-server/src/handlers/tests/{elevator_properties.rs,elevator_properties/lift_simulation.rs,read_rpm/elevator.rs,property_metadata/elevator.rs}`, `crates/bacnet-server/src/pics/property_metadata_tests/elevator.rs`.

Not covered: the unserved optional rows (`Car_Door_Text` and the deck rows), the `Floor_Text` size rule, `Elevator_Group` consistency with the group's `Group_Members`, intrinsic reporting and dispatching.

rows.standard_anchor: Clause 12.60 and Table 12-78, including Energy_Meter and Energy_Meter_Ref; Clause 21 BACnetDeviceObjectReference; Clause 15.5 ReadProperty, Clause 15.7 ReadPropertyMultiple and Clause 15.9.1.3 WriteProperty errors
rows.requirement_summary: The Escalator serves its Table 12-78 rows with their table datatypes. The required Elevator_Group is a BACnetObjectIdentifier naming Elevator Group instance 4194303 when no group lists the escalator, and the required Group_ID and Installation_ID are Unsigned8. All three read over ReadProperty and ReadPropertyMultiple, and a WriteProperty on any of them is refused with PROPERTY / WRITE_ACCESS_DENIED. Energy_Meter_Ref is a BACnetDeviceObjectReference, read-only over the network (WriteProperty is refused with WRITE_ACCESS_DENIED), and while it names an instance other than 4194303 Energy_Meter reads 0.0 and refuses any other value with VALUE_OUT_OF_RANGE. Property_List, the property metadata, RPM ALL, REQUIRED and OPTIONAL and the PICS rows list exactly the served rows.
notes: Split child of BACNET-12-OBJECT-MODEL (#1022). Breaking pre-1.0 wire changes: the three required rows were missing, Energy_Meter_Ref read as an empty OctetString, and Property_List now lists the rows in table order.

Local policies: the table gives the three membership rows the R code, so they are application-owned and read-only over the network, set through EscalatorObject::set_elevator_group (which refuses any object type but Elevator Group with VALUE_OUT_OF_RANGE), set_group_id and set_installation_id; both identification numbers start at 0.

Energy_Meter_Ref (#1036, shared with the Lift in energy_meter.rs) starts uninitialized, naming Accumulator instance 4194303 with no device. Table 12-78 gives it the O code with no write requirement, and it records how the installation is metered, so it stays read-only over the network and the application sets it with EscalatorObject::set_energy_meter_ref.

That setter takes an Accumulator, Pulse Converter, Analog Input, Analog Value, Large Analog Value, Integer Value, Positive Integer Value or proprietary object type (128-1023, vendor meters), local or with a Device identifier, and refuses other object types or a non-Device device with VALUE_OUT_OF_RANGE; the clause names no types, so this is the set whose Present_Value is a measured number in engineering units.

A reference to instance 4194303 clears it. While a reference is set, Energy_Meter holds 0.0: setting one zeroes the reading, a write of anything but 0.0 (either sign) is refused with VALUE_OUT_OF_RANGE, in service or out, and clearing the reference lets the reading restart from 0.0.

Not covered: that Energy_Meter_Ref names an object that exists, Elevator_Group consistency with the group's Group_Members, the event, intrinsic-reporting, audit, tag and profile rows, and dispatching.
evidence: Split child of `BACNET-12-OBJECT-MODEL` (#1022). The Escalator serves its Table 12-78 rows in table order with their table datatypes. It gains the required `Elevator_Group` (Elevator Group instance 4194303 until set), `Group_ID` and `Installation_ID` (Unsigned8, 0 until set), read over RP and RPM and refused over WP with WRITE_ACCESS_DENIED; the application sets them with `EscalatorObject::set_elevator_group` (refuses any other object type with VALUE_OUT_OF_RANGE), `set_group_id` and `set_installation_id`, shared with the Lift through one membership model.

`Energy_Meter_Ref` is now an uninitialized `BACnetDeviceObjectReference` (Accumulator instance 4194303, no device) instead of an empty OctetString (breaking on the wire). Evidence: `crates/bacnet-objects/src/elevator/{escalator.rs,membership.rs,metadata.rs,tests/group_membership.rs}`, `crates/bacnet-server/src/handlers/tests/{elevator_properties.rs,read_rpm/elevator.rs,property_metadata/elevator.rs}`, `crates/bacnet-server/src/pics/property_metadata_tests/elevator.rs`.

Not covered: an initialized `Energy_Meter_Ref` and its `Energy_Meter` rule, `Elevator_Group` consistency with the group's `Group_Members`, the event, intrinsic-reporting, audit, tag and profile rows, and dispatching.

rows.standard_anchor: Clause 12.26 and Table 12-30 (Present_Value, Priority_Array, Relinquish_Default); Clauses 12.26.4 and 12.26.11; Clause 21 BACnetDoorValue; Clause 19 command prioritization; Clause 15.9.1.3 WriteProperty errors
rows.requirement_summary: The Access Door's commandable Present_Value, the slots of its Priority_Array and its Relinquish_Default are BACnetDoorValue, whose four values are LOCK (0), UNLOCK (1), PULSE_UNLOCK (2) and EXTENDED_PULSE_UNLOCK (3). A Present_Value command carrying one of the four is stored and reads back as that Enumerated, and Present_Value resolves to the highest-priority non-NULL slot, or else to Relinquish_Default. Relinquish_Default takes only LOCK or UNLOCK (Clause 12.26.11). Any other Enumerated is refused with PROPERTY / VALUE_OUT_OF_RANGE and a non-Enumerated value with PROPERTY / INVALID_DATA_TYPE, leaving Present_Value, Priority_Array and Relinquish_Default unchanged.
notes: Split child of BACNET-12-OBJECT-MODEL (#979). The three properties are stored as the DoorValue newtype (the #932 pattern), and AccessDoorObject::set_relinquish_default takes a DoorValue; DoorValue::from_raw can carry any number, so the setter checks the four values too.

Breaking pre-1.0 behaviour change: the Present_Value arm used to store any Enumerated in its priority slot (the follow-up BACNET-12-RELINQUISH-DEFAULT-WRITABILITY recorded) and now shares Relinquish_Default's check through the shared write_priority_array! path.

Values in range read back on the wire exactly as before. The bacnet-types test door_value_values_match_clause_21 pins the four values the check derives from. #1073 narrowed Relinquish_Default from the four values to LOCK and UNLOCK, since Clause 12.26.11 keeps the two pulses out of it (a pulse can't be the resting command); the setter refuses them too.

The pulse timing, the pulse-time rows and Current_Command_Priority are evidenced in BACNET-12-ACCESS-DOOR-PULSE-TIMING. Not covered: Door_Unlock_Delay_Time and the value-source rows, which the object doesn't serve. The footnoted Out_Of_Service writability of Door_Status, Lock_Status and Door_Alarm_State is BACNET-12-ACCESS-DOOR-OUT-OF-SERVICE-SIMULATION (#1131).
evidence: Split child of `BACNET-12-OBJECT-MODEL` (#979, #1073). The Access Door stores `Present_Value`, its `Priority_Array` slots and `Relinquish_Default` as `DoorValue` (#932 pattern), and `AccessDoorObject::set_relinquish_default` takes a `DoorValue`.

A `Present_Value` command accepts LOCK, UNLOCK, PULSE_UNLOCK and EXTENDED_PULSE_UNLOCK (0..=3); `Relinquish_Default` accepts only LOCK and UNLOCK, since Clause 12.26.11 keeps the pulses out of it (#1073).

Any other Enumerated fails with VALUE_OUT_OF_RANGE and a non-Enumerated value with INVALID_DATA_TYPE, leaving the value, the priority array and the default unchanged, over the object API and WP. Breaking: the `Present_Value` arm used to store any Enumerated, and `Relinquish_Default` used to accept the two pulses.

In-range values read the same on the wire. Evidence: `crates/bacnet-objects/src/access_control/{door.rs,typed_value_tests.rs,tests.rs}`, `crates/bacnet-server/src/handlers/tests/{access_typed_values.rs,read_rpm/access_topology.rs,wpm_state_ownership.rs}`.

Pulse timing, the pulse-time rows and `Current_Command_Priority` are `BACNET-12-ACCESS-DOOR-PULSE-TIMING`. Not covered: the unlock-delay row, the value-source rows, and the footnoted Out_Of_Service writability of `Door_Status` and `Lock_Status`.

rows.requirement_summary: The Access Credential's Credential_Status is a BACnetBinaryPV derived from Reason_For_Disable: INACTIVE (0) while the list holds any reason and ACTIVE (1) when it is empty, so it is read-only and every WriteProperty on it fails with PROPERTY / WRITE_ACCESS_DENIED without changing it. Present_Value is not a Table 12-40 row, so it is absent from Property_List, the property metadata, RPM ALL and OPTIONAL, and the PICS rows, and ReadProperty, ReadPropertyMultiple and WriteProperty on it fail with PROPERTY / UNKNOWN_PROPERTY.
notes: Split child of BACNET-12-OBJECT-MODEL (#979, #1073). Breaking pre-1.0 changes. Credential_Status stored any Enumerated; #979 made it the BinaryPV newtype and refused anything but 0 and 1, and ResolvedEnum::from_property names it as a BinaryPV.

#1073 then derived it from Reason_For_Disable as Clause 12.35.8 describes, which made it read-only: a write would break the link to the list, and Credential_Disable (Clause 12.35.13) is the property an operator or outside process writes to disable the credential.

A new credential has no disable reason, so it reads ACTIVE where it used to read INACTIVE. How the list is assembled is evidenced in BACNET-12-ACCESS-CREDENTIAL-REQUIRED-ROWS. Present_Value came with the 0.1.0 import (7efc670a), which described it as the credential's active or inactive state, the meaning Credential_Status carries, but kept it in a separate field nothing synchronised; the #678 metadata migration then recorded it as an implementation-extra Optional writable row.

It is removed, as #984 did for Calendar and #997 for Elevator Group. The object has no COV support, event state or intrinsic reporting, so nothing else read it. The Out_Of_Service it also served, which Table 12-40 doesn't list, went in #1064 (BACNET-12-UNDEFINED-PROPERTY-ROWS).
evidence: Split child of `BACNET-12-OBJECT-MODEL` (#979, #1073). `Credential_Status` is a `BinaryPV` derived from `Reason_For_Disable`: INACTIVE while the list holds a reason, ACTIVE when it is empty (#1073). It is read-only, so WP on it fails with WRITE_ACCESS_DENIED (breaking: #979 let a write store 0 or 1), and a new credential reads ACTIVE (breaking: it read INACTIVE).

`Credential_Disable` is the property an operator writes to disable it. `ResolvedEnum::from_property` names it as a `BinaryPV`. `Present_Value` is not a Table 12-40 row and is removed: it is absent from `Property_List`, the metadata, RPM `ALL`/`OPTIONAL` and PICS, and RP, RPM and WP on it return PROPERTY / UNKNOWN_PROPERTY (breaking).

It came with the 0.1.0 import as a separate, unsynchronised copy of the active/inactive state that `Credential_Status` carries, and #678 recorded it as an implementation-extra optional writable row. Evidence: `crates/bacnet-objects/src/access_control/{credential.rs,credential_tests.rs,metadata_identity.rs,typed_value_tests.rs}`, `crates/bacnet-server/src/handlers/tests/{access_typed_values.rs,read_rpm/access_identity.rs,property_metadata/access_identity.rs}`, `crates/bacnet-server/src/pics/property_metadata_tests/access_identity.rs`, `crates/bacnet-types/src/enums/resolve.rs`.

The other required rows and the array datatypes are `BACNET-12-ACCESS-CREDENTIAL-REQUIRED-ROWS`. The served `Out_Of_Service`, which Table 12-40 doesn't list, went in #1064 (`BACNET-12-UNDEFINED-PROPERTY-ROWS`).

rows.standard_anchor: Clause 12.35 and Table 12-40 (Global_Identifier, Reason_For_Disable, Authentication_Factors, Activation_Time, Expiration_Time, Credential_Disable, Assigned_Access_Rights); Clauses 12.35.5, 12.35.9, 12.35.10, 12.35.11, 12.35.12, 12.35.13 and 12.35.18; Clause 21 BACnetAssignedAccessRights, BACnetCredentialAuthenticationFactor, BACnetAuthenticationFactor, BACnetAuthenticationFactorType, BACnetAccessAuthenticationFactorDisable, BACnetAccessCredentialDisable and BACnetAccessCredentialDisableReason; Clause 15.5 ReadProperty and Clause 15.9.1.3 WriteProperty errors
rows.requirement_summary: The Access Credential serves every Table 12-40 required row. Global_Identifier is a writable Unsigned32; a write past 32 bits fails with PROPERTY / VALUE_OUT_OF_RANGE. Reason_For_Disable is a read-only BACnetLIST holding, sorted and without repeats, the reasons the application raises, the reason the current Credential_Disable stands for (DISABLED, DISABLED_MANUAL or DISABLED_LOCKOUT, and DISABLED for a vendor value), and DISABLED_NOT_YET_ACTIVE before Activation_Time or DISABLED_EXPIRED after Expiration_Time, judged against the database clock on each read; changing Credential_Disable drops the reason its previous value added. Credential_Disable is writable and takes the four named values and 64 to 65535, refusing the rest with VALUE_OUT_OF_RANGE. Activation_Time and Expiration_Time are writable BACnetDateTime values taking a specific moment or all X'FF' (an open end), and refuse a partly specified value with VALUE_OUT_OF_RANGE and any other shape with INVALID_DATA_TYPE. Authentication_Factors and Assigned_Access_Rights are read-only BACnetARRAYs of BACnetCredentialAuthenticationFactor and BACnetAssignedAccessRights: a whole read concatenates the framed elements, index 0 reads the size, index n the element, and an index past the end fails with INVALID_ARRAY_INDEX; the bacnet-encoding codecs round-trip each element and refuse malformed ones.
notes: Split child of BACNET-12-OBJECT-MODEL (#1073). Breaking pre-1.0 wire changes: the five rows were missing, Assigned_Access_Rights read as an Unsigned count and Authentication_Factors as octet strings in a list, which the default array gate refused an index on.

Both identifiers are now identifier-stable arrays in array_property_default, since Table 12-40 is the only table carrying either; an index on an object without them now passes the gate and fails with UNKNOWN_PROPERTY rather than PROPERTY_IS_NOT_AN_ARRAY.

BACnetAssignedAccessRights in bacnet-types held a bare object identifier and had no users; it now holds the BACnetDeviceObjectReference Clause 21 gives it. Local policies: the window is judged lazily on each read, as the Calendar judges its date, so no tick is needed; without a clock frame naming a real moment (no clock, an impossible date, an unspecified time) it adds no reason, so a device with no clock doesn't disable every dated credential.

A partly specified limit names no single moment, so it is refused rather than matched as a pattern; the weekday octet is stored but ignored. The application raises and withdraws its own reasons with add_disable_reason and remove_disable_reason; DISABLED_NOT_YET_ACTIVE and DISABLED_EXPIRED are refused there because they follow the two times.

Which reason a vendor Credential_Disable value adds is a local matter; this implementation adds DISABLED. Global_Identifier, Credential_Disable, Activation_Time and Expiration_Time are network-writable; the two arrays are R rows the application provisions with set_authentication_factors and set_assigned_access_rights, which check each element (a named or vendor disable value, one of the 25 format types, an Access Rights reference or the 4194303 unused marker, a Device for any device identifier).

Not covered: the optional rows (Days_Remaining, Uses_Remaining, Absentee_Limit, Belongs_To, Last_Access_Point, Last_Access_Event, Last_Use_Time, Trace_Flag, Threat_Authority, Extended_Time_Enable, Authorization_Exemptions, Reliability_Evaluation_Inhibit, the audit, tag and profile rows) and the reasons only they drive; resizing the arrays over the network (Clauses 12.35.10.1 and 12.35.18.1); and that a referenced Access Rights object exists.
evidence: Split child of `BACNET-12-OBJECT-MODEL` (#1073). The credential serves every required row. `Global_Identifier` is a writable Unsigned32. `Reason_For_Disable` is a read-only list joining the application's reasons (`add_disable_reason`, `remove_disable_reason`), the reason the current `Credential_Disable` stands for, and DISABLED_NOT_YET_ACTIVE or DISABLED_EXPIRED judged against the database clock on each read (nothing without a usable clock frame).

`Credential_Disable` (named values and 64..=65535), `Activation_Time` and `Expiration_Time` (a specific moment or all X'FF'; a partly specified one is VALUE_OUT_OF_RANGE) are writable. `Assigned_Access_Rights` and `Authentication_Factors` are read-only BACnetARRAYs of the Clause 21 element types, readable whole, by element or by size (breaking: they read as a count and a list of octet strings), and set through checked `set_assigned_access_rights` and `set_authentication_factors`; new `bacnet-encoding` codecs carry the elements.

Evidence: `crates/bacnet-objects/src/access_control/{credential.rs,credential_rules.rs,credential_tests.rs,metadata_identity.rs}`, `crates/bacnet-encoding/src/constructed/{access_credential.rs,tests/access_credential.rs}`, `crates/bacnet-types/src/{constructed/access.rs,enums/access.rs,enums/tests/access_production.rs}`, `crates/bacnet-server/src/handlers/tests/{access_required_rows.rs,read_rpm/access_identity.rs}`. Not covered: the optional rows and the reasons only they drive, resizing the arrays over the network, and that a referenced Access Rights object exists.

rows.standard_anchor: Clause 12.26 and Table 12-30 (Door_Pulse_Time, Door_Extended_Pulse_Time, Door_Open_Too_Long_Time, Current_Command_Priority); Clauses 12.26.4, 12.26.16, 12.26.17, 12.26.19 and 12.26.39; Clause 21 BACnetOptionalUnsigned; Clause 19 command prioritization; Clause 15.9.1.3 WriteProperty errors
rows.requirement_summary: The Access Door serves Door_Pulse_Time, Door_Extended_Pulse_Time and Door_Open_Too_Long_Time as writable Unsigned32 counts of tenths of a second (a write past 32 bits fails with PROPERTY / VALUE_OUT_OF_RANGE, a non-Unsigned value with INVALID_DATA_TYPE) and Current_Command_Priority as a read-only BACnetOptionalUnsigned: the index of the slot Present_Value comes from, or NULL when it comes from Relinquish_Default. A PULSE_UNLOCK or EXTENDED_PULSE_UNLOCK command holds its slot until Door_Pulse_Time or Door_Extended_Pulse_Time has passed and is then relinquished from that slot, so Present_Value falls back to the next command or Relinquish_Default and COV subscribers hear of it. A pulse written while a higher priority is commanded is relinquished at once, as is a pulse with a time of zero; rewriting or relinquishing the slot cancels its deadline.
notes: Split child of BACNET-12-OBJECT-MODEL (#1073). The relock reuses the server's existing monotonic operation task (spawn_binary_lighting_operation_task, which already drives Binary Lighting Output egress): the door records each pulse slot's deadline from the database's monotonic clock when the command is written, reports its earliest deadline through next_monotonic_deadline_internal, relinquishes due slots in advance_monotonic_time_internal and hands the task a snapshot for COV.

No new task, trait method or clock source was added; a door with no bound clock advances a logical clock through advance_time_internal, which the object tests use. Local policies: the clause lets the controller relinquish a pulse early as a local matter; this implementation lets an outranked pulse run to its own deadline.

Changing a pulse time leaves an armed deadline as it was. The defaults are 5 s, 15 s and 30 s. Not covered: Door_Unlock_Delay_Time (an optional row the object doesn't serve, so no unlock delay is applied) and the door-open-too-long alarm, since Door_Open_Too_Long_Time is stored and served but no Door_Alarm_State logic consumes it.

#1131: the relock reads none of Door_Status, Lock_Status or Door_Alarm_State, so values a client simulates while Out_Of_Service is TRUE neither move nor follow it (BACNET-12-ACCESS-DOOR-OUT-OF-SERVICE-SIMULATION).
evidence: Split child of `BACNET-12-OBJECT-MODEL` (#1073). The door serves `Door_Pulse_Time`, `Door_Extended_Pulse_Time` and `Door_Open_Too_Long_Time` as writable Unsigned32 tenths of a second (defaults 5 s, 15 s, 30 s) and `Current_Command_Priority`, NULL on the default.

A PULSE_UNLOCK or EXTENDED_PULSE_UNLOCK slot is relinquished once its pulse time has passed, by the server's existing monotonic operation task (the one Binary Lighting Output egress uses), with COV; a pulse below a live command or with a zero time is relinquished at once, and rewriting or relinquishing the slot cancels it.

Evidence: `crates/bacnet-objects/src/access_control/{door.rs,door_pulse_tests.rs,metadata_topology.rs}`, `crates/bacnet-server/src/server/{binary_lighting_lifecycle.rs,access_door_pulse_task_tests.rs}`, `crates/bacnet-server/src/handlers/tests/{access_required_rows.rs,read_rpm/access_topology.rs}`. Not covered: `Door_Unlock_Delay_Time` and the door-open-too-long alarm.

rows.standard_anchor: Clause 12.26, Table 12-30 footnote 1 and Clauses 12.26.9, 12.26.12, 12.26.13 and 12.26.20 (Access Door Door_Status, Lock_Status, Door_Alarm_State); Clauses 12.26.6 and 12.26.14 (Secured_Status derived from them); Clause 13.1 Table 13-1 (Access Door row); Clause 15.9.1.3 WriteProperty errors; Clause 21 BACnetDoorStatus, BACnetLockStatus and BACnetDoorAlarmState; Clause 23.1 Table 23-1
rows.requirement_summary: While Out_Of_Service is TRUE, an Access Door takes WriteProperty and WritePropertyMultiple of Door_Status, Lock_Status and Door_Alarm_State, the three rows footnote 1 of Table 12-30 makes writable out of service; in service each fails with PROPERTY / WRITE_ACCESS_DENIED. A write must be an Enumerated inside the row's production: a named BACnetDoorStatus or one from the proprietary range 1024..=65535, a named BACnetLockStatus (a closed production that Table 23-1 doesn't list), or a named BACnetDoorAlarmState or one from 256..=65535. Another number is VALUE_OUT_OF_RANGE and another datatype INVALID_DATA_TYPE, with the property unchanged. The three rows are WhenOutOfService in the property metadata and writable in the PICS. Entering out of service sets the door's own three values aside and the return to service serves them again. A simulated Door_Alarm_State sends the Access Door SubscribeCOV report, and so does the restore when it changes the value served. Secured_Status is worked out on every read from what the door serves (Clause 12.26.14, #1148). It reads SECURED for a door that is commanded LOCK, not IN_ALARM, CLOSED or UNUSED at its contact and LOCKED or UNUSED at its lock monitor. Any input that misses makes it UNSECURED, so an UNLOCK or a pulse reads UNSECURED until it is relinquished or relocks. With none missed, a Door_Status or Lock_Status that reads UNKNOWN or a fault makes it UNKNOWN. A simulated Door_Status or Lock_Status moves it the same way, and the return to service moves it back with the device's values.

notes: Split child of BACNET-12-OBJECT-MODEL (#1131, found during #1061). Breaking pre-1.0 wire change: the three rows used to refuse every write. Footnote 1 of Table 12-30 marks exactly Door_Status, Lock_Status and Door_Alarm_State.

Clause 12.26.9 also lists Reliability, but only for a door whose Reliability can leave NO_FAULT_DETECTED; this door applies no fault algorithm and nothing changes its Reliability, so Reliability stays read-only, and Present_Value is commandable in both states already.

Local policies, each recorded in access_control/door_out_of_service.rs: the door holds the three values as one DoorState and sets it aside on the FALSE-to-TRUE edge through common::write_out_of_service_with_restore, the generic form #1131 extracted from write_out_of_service_with_reliability_restore (now a wrapper with its NO_FAULT_DETECTED fallback); the return to service restores it and drops the simulated values.

Meanwhile set_door_alarm_state and the new set_door_status and set_lock_status update the state set aside. A NULL write of one of the three is INVALID_DATA_TYPE, as for the Life Safety Tracking_Value.

Clause 12.26.20 restricts Door_Alarm_State to NORMAL and the members of Alarm_Values and Fault_Values and keeps it out of Masked_Alarm_Values; the door serves none of those lists, so a simulated value is checked against the enumeration only.

The pulse relock (BACNET-12-ACCESS-DOOR-PULSE-TIMING) runs on the timer the command armed and reads none of the three values. The door runs no intrinsic reporting (Event_State stays NORMAL), so a simulated Door_Alarm_State raises no event of its own; an Event Enrollment monitoring the property reads the served value.

COV needed no server change: the Table 13-1 row values are compared around every committed write. Not covered: a runtime application route for the three values once the server holds the door (the setters reach it only before), Alarm_Values, Fault_Values and Masked_Alarm_Values, and the CHANGE_OF_STATE and FAULT_STATE algorithms.

#1148 (wire change): Secured_Status used to read a stored SECURED whatever the door did; AccessDoorObject::secured_status now derives it on each read and nothing stores it, so COV snapshots, ReadProperty, ReadPropertyMultiple and an Event Enrollment monitoring it all see the current value.

Secured_Status is not in the Access Door row of Table 13-1 (#1061), so no COV path needed a change. Local policies, recorded on AccessDoorObject::secured_status: each input is met, failed or undetermined, a failed input gives UNSECURED even when another is undetermined (a door commanded UNLOCK is not secure whatever its contact reports), and UNKNOWN needs every input met or undetermined.

The only undetermined inputs are Door_Status UNKNOWN or DOOR_FAULT and Lock_Status UNKNOWN or LOCK_FAULT: the door's own monitor saying it can't tell. The option of keying UNKNOWN on Reliability was not taken, because this door applies no fault algorithm and nothing moves its Reliability off NO_FAULT_DETECTED; a new door starts CLOSED and LOCKED, so a never-reported Door_Status reads CLOSED, not UNKNOWN.

Door_Status values the clause does not describe for a door (NONE, CLOSING, OPENING, SAFETY_LOCKED, LIMITED_OPENED) and proprietary ones count as not closed. IN_ALARM comes from Event_State (Clause 12.26.6); the door now serves Status_Flags from its own Event_State field so the flag and Secured_Status read the same source, which stays NORMAL until intrinsic reporting is modelled (no wire change).

Masked_Alarm_Values is not served, so that input is treated as met; #1149 adds the list and its input next to the others in secured_status. Door_Alarm_State is not an input: it reaches Secured_Status only through Event_State once an event algorithm runs.

notes: Split child of BACNET-12-OBJECT-MODEL (#1064). Breaking pre-1.0 wire changes. The #1064 sweep listed these as required rows the objects did not serve; each was checked against the 135-2020 table pages before it was added, and all four are R rows.

Local policies: Accepted_Modes starts as every standard LifeSafetyMode, so a standard Mode write that used to succeed still does, and set_accepted_modes replaces it (deduplicated, order kept); a reserved or proprietary mode is accepted only when the application lists it.

The server COV snapshots and the trait default for custom Zones now include it, and the special case that answered NOT_COV_PROPERTY for it is gone. Global Group Event_State reads a fixed NORMAL, as other objects without intrinsic reporting do, so the object's own IN_ALARM stays clear whatever the members report.

Member_Status_Flags is computed on every read from group_members and present_value, the application-filled store Present_Value already reads, so it changes whenever Present_Value does with no second update path: a member counts when its reference names Status_Flags and its stored result is a bit-string value.

Each sets only its own property. Present_Value is taken in or out of service; a Tracking_Value sent while Out_Of_Service is TRUE replaces the value set aside and is served, and notified, from the return to service. public_claims: CHANGELOG.md Unreleased Added entry for #1123 (Life Safety runtime Present_Value and Tracking_Value)
notes: Split child of BACNET-12-OBJECT-MODEL (#1123, found during #1108). Breaking pre-1.0 Rust API: BACnetObject gained set_tracking_value_internal (default OBJECT / OPTIONAL_FUNCTIONALITY_NOT_SUPPORTED), which SourceReporter forwards, and set_present_value_local, which used to refuse these objects with that error, now takes them.

Local policies, recorded in life_safety/application.rs: Clauses 12.15.4 and 12.16.4 leave the derivation of Present_Value and any latching until reset to the implementation, and here the application owns both.

The object never derives one value from the other and neither hook touches Silenced or Operation_Expected, so an application that latches holds Present_Value on the alarm state, reports the live state through Tracking_Value and commits the post-reset Present_Value from its reset executor, whose context carries what the route left; the route takes values whether or not a reset is armed.

Present_Value has no out-of-service footnote, Clauses 12.15.11 and 12.16.11 don't decouple it and clients never write it, so unlike the Inputs the hook takes it while Out_Of_Service is TRUE; Tracking_Value keeps the #1108 set-aside rule (BACNET-12-LIFE-SAFETY-OUT-OF-SERVICE-SIMULATION).

Both routes go through write_local's Life Safety snapshots, so COV reports exact deltas, and through its post-write intrinsic event pass, as every set_present_value_local caller does; the built-in objects run no intrinsic reporting (Event_State fixed NORMAL), so no CHANGE_OF_LIFE_SAFETY event follows.

The out-of-service Tracking_Value write now shares the hooks' decode and range check. Not covered: a runtime route for Silenced, which only LifeSafetyOperation and a reset commit reach once the server holds the object, and intrinsic CHANGE_OF_LIFE_SAFETY reporting (BACNET-13-LIFE-SAFETY-OPERATION).

Each takes an Enumerated `LifeSafetyState`, standard or from 256 to 65535; another number is VALUE_OUT_OF_RANGE, another datatype INVALID_DATA_TYPE, an unknown object UNKNOWN_OBJECT and another object type OPTIONAL_FUNCTIONALITY_NOT_SUPPORTED.

Each sets only its own property: `Silenced` and `Operation_Expected` stay put and neither value is derived from the other, so latching until reset is the application's (its reset executor sees what the route left).

`Present_Value` is taken in or out of service, since clients never write it; a `Tracking_Value` sent out of service replaces the value set aside (`BACNET-12-LIFE-SAFETY-OUT-OF-SERVICE-SIMULATION`). Both run `write_local`'s Life Safety snapshots (Present_Value to SubscribeCOV and Present_Value property subscribers, Tracking_Value to its property subscribers) and its post-write event pass, which raises nothing for the built-in objects.

A member with no acquired result reads PROPERTY / VALUE_NOT_INITIALIZED. Index 0 of Group_Members, Present_Value and Group_Member_Names reads the array size, indexes 1 to N one element, and a larger index PROPERTY / INVALID_ARRAY_INDEX, through ReadProperty and ReadPropertyMultiple, RPM ALL included. public_claims: CHANGELOG.md Unreleased Fixed entry for #1107 (Global Group array encodings)
notes: Split child of BACNET-12-OBJECT-MODEL (#1107, found in #1092). Breaking pre-1.0 wire and Rust API changes. Table 12-57 and the Clause 21 productions were read as page images. A BACnetPropertyAccessResult starts with the same four members, under the same context tags, as a BACnetDeviceObjectPropertyReference, so both share the reference codec; the result follows as the value framed in [4] or the error class and code framed in [5].

Before, Group_Members went out as application-tagged values with NULL standing in for an absent index or device, and Present_Value as the bare stored values, which could neither name the member nor report a failed read; any array index returned the whole array.

Local policies: the application still acquires the member values (polling, COV or both is a local matter in Clause 12.50.7) and stores an AccessResult per member by position in GlobalGroupObject::present_value.

Present_Value is built on each read from Group_Members, so it always has one element per member and each element carries that member's current reference; a member with no stored result reads PROPERTY / VALUE_NOT_INITIALIZED, the result Clause 12.50.7.1 gives an element added by a resize, and stored results past the last member are not served.

Group_Members and Group_Member_Names stay read-only, so no network resize exists, and they are sized by the application. Group_Member_Names gets the same per-index reads. Member_Status_Flags reads the same store: a Status_Flags member counts only when its stored result is a bit-string value.

The decoder returns a one-element value as itself and any other count as a list, and keeps context-tagged content as ApplicationData, so a decoded element re-encodes to the same octets. Not covered: the Global Group intrinsic reporting, COVU and Update_Interval rows; writable Group_Members (with the Clause 12.50.5.1 resizing); acquisition of member values by the server itself.

The application stores an `AccessResult` per member in `GlobalGroupObject::present_value`; a member with none reads PROPERTY / VALUE_NOT_INITIALIZED and results past the last member are not served. Index 0 of `Group_Members`, `Present_Value` and `Group_Member_Names` reads the size, 1 to N one element, and past N PROPERTY / INVALID_ARRAY_INDEX; any index used to return the whole array.

`Member_Status_Flags` counts only bit-string values held for `Status_Flags` members. Present_Value is rebuilt from the members on every ReadProperty, ReadPropertyMultiple (RPM ALL included) and ReadRange: each member is read as ReadPropertyMultiple reads that specification, so selectors expand, a property that fails to read carries its error class and code in [5], and a member naming no object in this device gets OBJECT / UNKNOWN_OBJECT for each reference. public_claims: CHANGELOG.md Unreleased Fixed entry for #1134 (Group List_Of_Group_Members and Present_Value), from changelog.d/1134-group-datatypes.md
notes: Split child of BACNET-12-OBJECT-MODEL (#1134, found in #1107). Breaking pre-1.0 wire and Rust API changes. Table 12-17, Clause 12.14 and the Clause 21 productions were read as page images. Before, List_Of_Group_Members went out as bare application-tagged object identifiers with no properties, and Present_Value as whatever values the application had stored, which named no member and could not report a failed read.

Local policies: the object stores no Present_Value, and a direct read of the object alone returns an empty list; the server builds the list under the database guard the request already holds, through the same planning and per-row reads as ReadPropertyMultiple, so the Device wildcard resolves to this device and a Device member reads the values the executor serves.

A ReadAccessSpecification carries no device, so every member is read from this device's database: an object that isn't there reads OBJECT / UNKNOWN_OBJECT for each of its references, as in ReadPropertyMultiple, and members in other devices belong in a Global Group.

GroupObject::add_member refuses, with PROPERTY / VALUE_OUT_OF_RANGE and the members unchanged, a specification with no property references and one that names a Group or Global Group and selects Present_Value directly or through ALL or REQUIRED, the nesting Clause 12.14.5 rules out; OPTIONAL and named properties of another group are accepted.

Member rows use each object's own reader, so a custom Group object that lists a group's Present_Value gets that object's own answer instead of a recursive rebuild, and a custom Group whose List_Of_Group_Members doesn't decode as ReadAccessSpecifications fails the Present_Value read with PROPERTY / OTHER.

Member reads aren't charged to a ReadPropertyMultiple request's work budget, since the members are local configuration and read-only on the network; the rebuilt octets still count toward its byte budget.

PropertyReference and ReadAccessSpecification moved from bacnet-services into bacnet_types::constructed, with their codecs as free functions in bacnet_encoding::constructed, so the Group stores them the way other objects store their Clause 21 types; the ReadPropertyMultiple, COV and Audit codecs call the same functions.

Not covered: a member naming the Device's Active_COV_Subscriptions or Active_COV_Multiple_Subscriptions reads an empty list, because a request takes its COV snapshot only when it reads those properties directly; writable List_Of_Group_Members; the Audit_Level, Auditable_Operations, Tags and profile rows.
