rows.requirement_summary: Integer Value, Positive Integer Value and Large Analog Value serve the required Units (BACnetEngineeringUnits, NO_UNITS until the application sets it, read-only over the network). The Pulse Converter serves the required Count and Count_Before_Change (Unsigned), Update_Time and Count_Change_Time (BACnetDateTime), all read-only, and COV_Period (Unsigned 0, read-only), which its COV support makes required. In service its Present_Value is Count times Scale_Factor; a write of Adjust_Value stores the value, keeps the old Count in Count_Before_Change, takes the truncated quotient of the value over Scale_Factor off Count and stamps Count_Change_Time, or fails with PROPERTY / VALUE_OUT_OF_RANGE and changes nothing when Count would leave its range. Its SubscribeCOV notifications carry Update_Time after Present_Value and Status_Flags. Lighting Output serves Default_Ramp_Rate and Default_Step_Increment (REAL, writable within 0.1 to 100.0, VALUE_OUT_OF_RANGE outside it), and both lighting objects serve Current_Command_Priority: the Priority_Array slot Present_Value comes from, or NULL on Relinquish_Default, read-only. Each row is in Property_List, the property metadata, RPM ALL and REQUIRED (COV_Period in OPTIONAL) and the PICS.

notes: Split child of BACNET-12-OBJECT-MODEL, from the #1092 tracking list the #1064 property-set sweep produced. Breaking pre-1.0 wire changes: new rows in Property_List, RPM ALL and REQUIRED, and the PICS, and a Pulse Converter whose Present_Value and Adjust_Value now behave as Clause 12.23 describes.

Each row was checked against the 135-2020 table images before it was added. Units: the commandable value macro takes an optional units entry, so only the three numeric types carry the field, with a `units` getter and a `set_units` setter that refuses values above 65535 (the Lift Car_Load_Units precedent); the analog objects likewise keep Units read-only.

Pulse Converter: before, Present_Value was a stored REAL that only an out-of-service write changed and Adjust_Value was stored without effect. Now Count is the state: `add_pulses` accumulates input and stamps Update_Time, and Present_Value is computed from Count and Scale_Factor on each read while in service (the clause leaves the timing to the implementation).

Going out of service freezes Present_Value and decouples it, as item (a) of 12.23.10 requires; Count keeps accumulating, and returning to service makes Present_Value follow Count again. Every change to Count or Scale_Factor is refused with VALUE_OUT_OF_RANGE if the scaled value would not fit a finite REAL, and an Adjust_Value with a zero Scale_Factor is refused because the quotient is undefined.

Timestamps come from the database's Device clock through `clock::stamp_datetime`, shared with the File object's Modification_Date, and are all-unspecified with no clock or before the first change. COV_Period is required by footnote 2 since the object supports COV; it is a constant 0, which Clause 13.1 defines as no periodic notifications, because the server sends none.

Table 13-1 reports Update_Time with the Pulse Converter's Present_Value and Status_Flags, so `cov_reported_properties_default` now lists it (reported, not a trigger). Lighting: Default_Ramp_Rate starts at 100.0 and Default_Step_Increment at 1.0, both inside the 0.1 to 100.0 range Clauses 12.54.17 and 12.54.18 set; they are writable, with matching setters.

Current_Command_Priority reuses `common::current_command_priority`, which the analog, binary and multi-state outputs and values already share; on Binary Lighting Output it stays at the commanding slot through a WARN_RELINQUISH egress, since the slot holds until the egress ends.

Not covered: Lighting Output's Default_Fade_Time still reads a constant 0, below the 100 ms floor of Clause 12.54.16; Current_Command_Priority and COV_Increment on the commandable value types; periodic COV notifications; feeding Count from Input_Reference.

rows.requirement_summary: The Averaging object serves Window_Interval (Unsigned seconds, 900 by default) and Window_Samples (Unsigned, 15 by default), both required and writable, and computes Minimum_Value, Maximum_Value and Average_Value over the valid samples among the most recent Window_Samples attempts. Attempted_Samples counts the attempts in the window and stops at Window_Samples; Valid_Samples counts the valid ones, so their difference is the number of missed samples. With no valid sample in the window, which includes a new object, the three statistics read positive infinity, NaN and negative infinity respectively for minimum, average and maximum, and both counts read zero. A WriteProperty or WritePropertyMultiple of Window_Interval, Window_Samples or Object_Property_Reference, or of zero to Attempted_Samples, empties the window even when the value doesn't change. A zero Window_Interval, a Window_Samples of zero or above 1440 (the buffer bound) and a nonzero Attempted_Samples fail with PROPERTY / VALUE_OUT_OF_RANGE, another datatype with PROPERTY / INVALID_DATA_TYPE, and the object is unchanged. The three rows are in Property_List, RPM ALL and REQUIRED, and writable in the property metadata and the PICS. A property COV subscription on a statistic is notified when the window empties or fills again, whatever its increment, because a non-finite REAL is compared by its bits. In a running server, an Averaging object that holds an Object_Property_Reference is sampled by the server itself every Window_Interval / Window_Samples seconds (never more often than every 100 ms), the first sample one spacing after the server binds its monotonic clock or after any write that empties the window, which also restarts the spacing. A referenced object or property that doesn't exist, an array index on a property that isn't an array, any other read error and a value outside the five datatypes Clause 12.5 averages are recorded as missed attempts. Each server sample reaches property COV subscribers as a write does. An object without a reference is fed by the application only; on one with a reference, an application sample is one more attempt and leaves the spacing alone.

notes: Split child of BACNET-12-OBJECT-MODEL, from the #1092 tracking list. Breaking pre-1.0 wire change: two new rows, Attempted_Samples now writable, statistics that cover a window instead of every sample since creation, and empty-window values of +INF, NaN and -INF where 0.0 used to be read.

Table 12-5 and the clause were read as page images. The window keeps one slot per attempt, oldest first, with a marker for an attempt that produced no value; the statistics are recomputed over the whole window in f64 on every change, so samples leaving the window cause no drift, and the empty-window NaN is always the canonical f32::NAN so COV sees two empty windows as equal.

Window_Samples is capped at 1440 (one sample a minute for a day, eight bytes a slot); the clause sets a floor of 15 and no ceiling. A zero Window_Interval is refused because the clause leaves the minimum to the implementation and a window of no length has no sample spacing. The application feeds samples (#1083) and can report a miss with None.

#1144: the server now samples a referenced property itself, as Clauses 12.5.14 and 12.5.15 have the device do. The object owns the schedule: the database's monotonic clock is bound to it, every reset of the window restarts the spacing from the moment of the reset (so a write of the value already held does too, as does a zero written to Attempted_Samples), and the first sample comes one spacing after a restart, which keeps Clause 12.5.11's relation between Attempted_Samples and elapsed time.

Due times keep a fixed cadence; a pass that falls a whole spacing behind takes one sample and restarts the cadence instead of catching up. The spacing is floored at MIN_SAMPLE_PERIOD (100 ms): one second over 1,440 samples would otherwise take the database lock more than a thousand times a second, so such a window spans more than Window_Interval, a local choice the clause's open minimum for Window_Interval allows.

No new task: the monotonic operation task that already runs Binary Lighting Output egress and Access Door pulse relock calls ObjectDatabase::sample_due_averaging_objects under its database guard before gathering deadlines; the object reports its due time through next_monotonic_deadline_internal and hands over its reference through the new BACnetObject::take_due_averaging_sample_internal hook (SourceReporter forwards it; DeviceReadView keeps the default, as for other mutating hooks).

The read goes through the target's read_property with ReadProperty's array-index gate. The samples fan out as a background commit (BackgroundCommit, then CovFanout::fire once the guard drops), the same COV path schedule writes take; the COV table is locked after the database, and no network work happens under the database guard.

That task also no longer spins when an object leaves its deadline due: the next wake is at least a millisecond away. Remote references stay out of scope: Object_Property_Reference is stored as a local BACnetObjectPropertyReference and a device-qualified write is refused with INVALID_DATA_ENCODING (BACNET-12-REFERENCE-PROPERTY-WRITABILITY), so there is never a remote target to read or count as missed. Not covered: the optional Variance_Value, Minimum_Value_Timestamp and Maximum_Value_Timestamp rows; references to properties in other devices.

rows.requirement_summary: Notification Class Recipient_List reads and writes use the Clause 21 BACnetDestination framing: seven application-tagged members in the order Clause 21 gives (a BACnetDaysOfWeek and a time window first, the recipient fourth) concatenated as a BACnetLIST, with BACnetRecipient discriminated by context tag (device [0] primitive ObjectIdentifier, address [1] constructed BACnetAddress of application Unsigned16 + OCTET STRING). The list holds at most 32 destinations (#1098): a WriteProperty, WritePropertyMultiple or write_local that would leave more fails with RESOURCES / NO_SPACE_TO_WRITE_PROPERTY naming the first destination past the cap, and add_destination refuses the same way. An address recipient carries a MAC of at most 18 octets (BACnetAddress::MAX_MAC_LEN, #1124): a longer one does not decode, so a write fails with PROPERTY / INVALID_DATA_TYPE, AddListElement names that element, and add_destination refuses it with the same code. Routing holds every Notification Class, custom objects included, to the 32-destination cap and routes nothing from a longer list (#1124). Only the framed form is a Recipient_List value: the pre-#152 flat form fails with PROPERTY / INVALID_DATA_TYPE (#1125).
notes: Split child of BACNET-12-OBJECT-MODEL; scope is the modeled NotificationClass path. The generic recipient codec remains interoperability vocabulary and is not Notification Forwarder object support. Golden vectors cover the device, address (nonzero network), and broadcast (zero-length MAC) forms; the 8-entry list round-trip covers the Annex K.2.25 AE-CRL-B minimum-entries posture.

Decode is strict end to end: element sequence, fixed-width bit-string members (exactly one content octet with unused_bits 1 for valid-days / 5 for transitions), and whole-list routing (a malformed stored list fails closed with no prefix delivery).

#1125: the pre-#152 flat application-tagged form (PropertyValue::List of seven-value entries) is gone. A local write of it, an empty flat list included, fails with PROPERTY / INVALID_DATA_TYPE, and routing treats a custom class serving it as an invalid list.

Network writes were always framed, and neither the Python bindings nor the CLI built the flat form. The write path and routing share one capped framed decoder. Indexed writes are rejected (Tranche K / #260 family). Remaining work: interop evidence against a second implementation; Notification Forwarder remains unsupported under BACNET-12-NOTIFICATION-FORWARDER-WITHDRAWAL.

#1098: Recipient_List is capped at 32 destinations (MAX_RECIPIENT_LIST_DESTINATIONS), four times the AE-CRL-B minimum of 8 (Annex K.2.25). A device destination encodes in at most 27 octets and an address destination with a MAC of up to 6 octets in at most 35, so a full list is at most 1,120 octets and a ReadProperty of it fits one 1476-octet B/IP APDU; each event transition fans out to at most 32 notifications per class.

A write checks destinations in order and refuses the first past the cap before decoding it, as Date_List does. The recipient_list field is private: recipient_list() reads it and add_destination returns Result, so nothing local grows the list past the cap. Before, the list was unbounded up to the 10,000-item framed decoder limit, past which a write failed with INVALID_DATA_TYPE.

#1124: an address MAC is at most 18 octets (BACnetAddress::MAX_MAC_LEN). Clause 21 leaves the OCTET STRING unbounded; the longest network-layer address in Table 6-2 is 7 octets (LonTalk Neuron_ID), and the longest link address this stack uses is the 18-octet B/IPv6 form (IPv6 address and UDP port).

A destination's recipient decodes through decode_configured_recipient, which refuses a longer MAC, so a WriteProperty or WritePropertyMultiple fails with PROPERTY / INVALID_DATA_TYPE and an AddListElement with a ChangeList-Error naming the element; add_destination refuses with the same code so a stored list stays decodable.

A destination is then at most 47 octets and a full list at most 1,504. Routing applies MAX_RECIPIENT_LIST_DESTINATIONS to every class: a custom NOTIFICATION_CLASS object serving a longer list yields RecipientListTooLong, the server logs a warning, counts the transition in EventNotificationCounters::recipient_list_too_long (#1142) and sends nothing for that transition (never a prefix), and decoding stops at the first destination past the cap.

GetEnrollmentSummary membership still reads the list as configured. The generic decode_recipient stays unbounded for now: COV subscription lists and audit records report source addresses learned off the network, and the stack must read back what it encodes. Since #1141 the NPDU codec refuses a DLEN or SLEN past the same 18 octets, so those learned addresses fit the bound; holding decode_recipient to it as well is follow-up work (#1156).

rows.requirement_summary: On object types carrying Out_Of_Service and Reliability, Reliability is network-writable exactly when Out_Of_Service is TRUE (the simulation grant quoted in each carrier's Out_Of_Service property text), and the written value is validated against the BACnetReliability production: the named set derived from Reliability::ALL_NAMED (enumerated 0..=25 with 11 reserved for a future addendum) plus the vendor-proprietary range 64..=65535, refusing anything else with PROPERTY / VALUE_OUT_OF_RANGE. In-service writes refuse PROPERTY / WRITE_ACCESS_DENIED (Clause 15.9.1.3 row for a property the requester cannot write at that time). The evaluated value is saved on the FALSE-to-TRUE edge and restored on the TRUE-to-FALSE edge; the internal set_reliability_internal route carries the complementary ownership guard (refused while Out_Of_Service is TRUE). Trend Log and Trend Log Multiple, whose Reliability_Evaluation_Inhibit paragraphs require NO_FAULT_DETECTED while evaluation is inhibited without the out-of-service write provision, refuse all network Reliability writes. Loop Present_Value, which the same footnote covers, follows the same gate: network-writable only while Out_Of_Service is TRUE and refused PROPERTY / WRITE_ACCESS_DENIED in service, with the application route (set_present_value_internal, reached through BACnetServer::set_present_value_local) carrying the complementary guard. Trend Log and Trend Log Multiple serve no Out_Of_Service at all, because Tables 12-29 and 12-35 define none.
notes: Split child of BACNET-12-OBJECT-MODEL (#240, #252). The nine intrinsic-reporting carriers were proven by #218/#239; this tranche added Loop as the tenth reliability_gate_test! carrier and Schedule as the eleventh, extended the predicate from a restated literal to a derivation from Reliability::ALL_NAMED (exhaustive 0..=65536 equivalence sweep; the value past the enum ceiling flips to accepted exactly when its addendum constant lands), and ran the sweep over the remaining OOS+Reliability carriers per #240: Schedule's Reliability_Evaluation_Inhibit text anticipates the out-of-service client write (allowing a client-supplied replacement Reliability value while Out_Of_Service is TRUE) so the gate applies with an internal route reserved for its CONFIGURATION_ERROR evaluation; Trend Log (Reliability O, Table 12-29) and Trend Log Multiple (Reliability O, Table 12-35) carry no writability footnote and no simulation-write provision, so the previously-accepting Trend Log arm now refuses PROPERTY / WRITE_ACCESS_DENIED (behavior change) and Trend Log Multiple's default denial is pinned as deliberate.

Loop and Schedule also gained is_writable_property overrides mirroring their write arms so the PICS and runtime dispatch share one truth source. Residue: carriers that never grew a write arm (Lighting Output family, Escalator/Lift/access-zone family) deny by default; whether each one's Clause 12 Out_Of_Service text obliges the writability half of its footnote is untriaged and tracked separately from this gate.

Binary Lighting Output Relinquish_Default is restricted to BACnetBinaryLightingPV OFF(0) or ON(1), deliberately separate from Present_Value operation inputs; steady Priority_Array storage remains OFF/ON/NULL. WARN, WARN_OFF, WARN_RELINQUISH, and STOP behavior is evidenced in the dedicated Binary Lighting operations row. rows.requirement_summary: Binary Lighting Output Present_Value accepts the named OFF, ON, WARN, WARN_OFF, WARN_RELINQUISH, and STOP inputs plus NULL at priorities 1..=16. Only OFF/ON/NULL are stored: WARN conditionally requests a logical blink without synthesizing ON; WARN_OFF and WARN_RELINQUISH either perform their terminal mutation immediately or retain the existing highest-priority ON command for a snapshotted Egress_Time; STOP cancels only the active same-priority egress. A validated same-or-higher non-STOP Present_Value command completes the old operation before applying the incoming command, lower-priority writes do not halt it, and exactly one monotonic in-memory operation can be active.
notes: Egress state and its arm-relative monotonic deadline are object-owned, process-local, and intentionally not reconstructed after restart. Egress_Time is captured when an operation arms; later Egress_Time or Blink_Warn_Enable writes affect future commands only, and Out_Of_Service does not suspend progress.

A hidden database-bound Tokio monotonic source gives writes and the lifecycle task one time domain; the one-second Delay interval also wakes for an exact known deadline and delayed wakes use actual time without charging pre-arm elapsed.

Expiry freezes COV-readable terminal state with the mutation under the database write lock, then the generic single/multiple path encodes and sends from that immutable snapshot after releasing locks, so later commands cannot rewrite the terminal payload.

Logical blink requests are retained only through a hidden internal observation for deterministic tests; a successful WPM prefix may arm or halt an operation even when a later write fails. There is no Rust/Python host callback, BACnet property, physical output, persistence, or hardware support claim.

#842 removes direct Priority_Array writes: all well-formed values and indices reach read-only denial without completing or advancing an active operation. Valid same/higher Present_Value commands retain the existing halt ordering; lower-priority commands preserve the operation. Explicit elapsed-time tests cover OFF/ON/NULL array refusal without changing slots, blink count or the remaining deadline.
evidence: Binary Lighting Output stores only steady OFF/ON/NULL priority values while interpreting WARN, WARN_OFF, WARN_RELINQUISH, and STOP as operations. The object owns at most one process-local arm-relative monotonic deadline; eligible WARN_OFF/WARN_RELINQUISH retain the existing highest-priority ON slot for snapshotted Egress_Time, zero time mutates synchronously, same-priority STOP cancels without changing the slot, and validated same/higher non-STOP commands complete the prior terminal mutation before the incoming command.

Direct Priority_Array[index] OFF/ON/NULL compatibility follows the same halt-before-incoming ordering, while lower writes leave the operation and deadline intact. A hidden database-bound Tokio monotonic source gives arming and lifecycle expiry one time domain without pre-arm charging; delayed wakes use actual time.

Expiry clones COV-readable terminal state with the mutation under the database lock, then generic single/multiple encoding and network delivery use the immutable snapshot after lock release, so intervening commands cannot rewrite the terminal payload.

A successful WPM prefix that arms, halts, or updates command state remains committed if a later write fails; the failing write itself is mutation-free. notes: Issue #826 adds local latest-successful preparation ordering for whole unconfirmed observations, not a Standard-mandated concurrency tie-break. A checked table-owner counter is reserved after coherent eligible capture and before later awaits; each live reference atomically commits a newer successful marker and complete baseline.

Newer failures/cancellation do not block older success; overlapping Multiple companions have no independent baseline authority. Existing generation, route and lifetime fences remain and same-route expiry refresh retains progress; confirmed completion has drawn from the same counter since #896.

Exhaustion fails unconfirmed candidates closed. Supplied Binary Lighting terminal snapshots follow preparation order even when their object state is older; original-write/event-time, transport-byte and remote-receipt ordering are not claimed.

The public baseline setter is removed in favor of internal completion authority. Issue #840 matches ordinary/Single on original client recipient plus existing process/target/property/index coordinates, independently of immediate router; form remains mutable.

Latest admitted renewal chooses the current route, including permitted ordinary indefinite lifetimes. Canonical cancellation works through either router; cleanup follows only the current route. Existing replacement generations fence stale initial/fanout completion, with normal renewal observation reset and baseline completion timing unchanged (#896 later moved confirmed completion to the Ack); already admitted sends may finish on an old route.

CovRecipient is shared by every family and quota/notification accounting, replacing both prior recipient/peer-key types without aliases. All typed table admissions reject empty routed source MAC before effects; valid full-peer replacements and existing finite-to-indefinite quota refusal are covered.

Refusal preserves the live target and authorization remains before canonical matching. Issue #833 separates Multiple canonical recipient identity (original local MAC or routed SNET/SADR, process, confirmed form) from current immediate delivery route.

Latest successfully admitted finite requests, including empty renewals of existing contexts, retarget every retained reference; empty absent requests create none. Cross-router cancellation matches canonical targets without retargeting survivors.

A request refused as a whole or at its first reference preserves the live target route, terms, references and paired observations, while existing unrelated expired purges/counters may still occur; one refused at a later reference keeps and retargets like an accepted one (#1058).

Private route ownership tokens fence captured old-route snapshots, including A-B-A migrations, without replacing unincluded reference generations or observations, except that a move while a confirmed report is outstanding or owed clears the kept untimestamped observations that report carried (#923); same-route empty renewal preserves authority.

Already admitted sends may complete on their old route, but late completion/ACK cannot advance migrated baselines. Peer cleanup matches current delivery endpoints. Multiple form/context semantics and valid routed quota policies are unchanged.

Claimed BACnet addresses are not authentication; mutation authorization remains before handling. The pre-1.0 API replaces MultipleContextKey.endpoint with recipient: CovRecipient, adds an explicit subscribe_multiple route and moves endpoint() from the key to subscription data.

Issue #817 adds independent applicable Status_Flags triggers and generic property companions, with one generation-fenced delivered selected/flags observation. Effective property_list declares absence; declared-present flags require canonical four-bit encoding.

Local failure policy skips the whole observation on selected or flags read/encoding/cap failure, including ordinary PV failures. Present changes can trigger after delivered absence; disappearance alone cannot, and an unreported absent/same-return cycle is not tracked.

Multiple captures flags once per object per notification context with selected values under the same DB/snapshot borrow, releases before transport, and lets only late-retained references authorize companions/timestamps/baseline updates.

Ordinary nonnumeric/no-increment values report only on change (#889); Life Safety committed deltas remain, and baselines advance on unconfirmed send success or confirmed Ack (#896). Specialized report sets and full service qualification remain outside this claim.

Issue #810 uses one bounded typed selected-property sample for threshold/equality, payload and generation-fenced baseline completion. Read/encoding failure never substitutes Present_Value. Local exact-integer/nonfinite/type-transition policies and immutable shared sample caps (32 List levels,1024 nodes,65536 scalar/raw bytes) are covered by independent arithmetic, shape, wire and retention tests.

Multiple filters each successfully read value independently before choosing its representative, remaining lifetime and Life Safety companions/timestamping.

This row remains below supported status: property-specific COV coverage beyond the selected profile, broader array-index error preservation, empty-spec context materialization, Daylight_Savings_Status adjustment, schema-aware ANY validation, shorter server lock hold for maximum-size requests, Active_COV_Multiple_Subscriptions synchronization, client-mode COV Multiple reception, outbound APDU size/segmentation policy, and fuller BIBB/PICS evidence remain separate work.

Refs #856: timestamped Multiple references capture each qualifying change with the Device clock frame of its commit, under the database write guard of network WriteProperty and WritePropertyMultiple, write_local, Staging target writes and source completion, Binary Lighting terminal transitions, committed intrinsic transitions (write-triggered and periodic), fault-detection reliability changes and schedule writes.

WritePropertyMultiple captures each successful attempt as it commits, including A-B-A within one request and the committed prefix before a failed attempt. Life Safety objects capture the exact properties each mutation changed (WriteProperty, each WritePropertyMultiple attempt, write_local, Operation_Expected arming, background passes), selected as their exact fanout selects; LifeSafetyOperation changes capture the same way on any object.

Since #988 the bundled Staging object supports COV, so its completion capture also reaches its own subscribers (BACNET-13-COV-OBJECT-CRITERIA). The admission clock check and the initial capture share one sample.

Refs #889: those background commits also fan COV out to every subscriber kind once the database guard is dropped, as a network write does; the bundled Event Enrollment objects accept no COV subscriptions, so their evaluation fans nothing out.

The whole-object and property criteria report only an actual change: a missing or non-positive increment means any change, so a repeated fanout of an unchanged value reports nothing. Changes queue per reference until a notification carrying them is delivered, meaning transmitted when unconfirmed and acknowledged when confirmed (#896; §13.16.3.1.2.3).

Any notification to a context also carries that context's other pending timestamped changes (§§13.17.1.1, 13.18.1.1). Each value carries its own Time_Of_Change; earlier changes precede the latest per reference, and explicit untimestamped coordinates are never repeated as history and keep their current row untimestamped even when that selector did not qualify.

An explicit untimestamped selector governs its coordinate outright, while an explicit timestamped selector that conveys no change in a round only fills in a missing time when a sibling carries its field (#987): a value it last saw keeps the commit time of that change, since its captures record the own value even below its increment, an admission or renewal capture included; a value no producer captured takes the preparation time, kept for that value without touching its increment baseline; with no time to give (no valid Device clock, or a producer snapshot that may predate the record) the value is left out of the notification; a reference cancelled since its fanout looked owns nothing, so its field goes out as an ordinary untimestamped value; a companion that already carries a time keeps it.

The header names the newest change whose time a notification carries, so across notifications to a context on several objects it can move back, since it describes each notification alone. A history row is dropped only when the next row for its coordinate repeats it exactly, so a value returning within one clock tick stays.

The initial report after admission uses the admission time as a local convention, and a renewal keeps unconveyed changes. Changes one notification cannot carry go out in several (§13.1, §13.18.1.1; #986), each within the local maximum APDU and within the max-APDU-length-accepted from the header of the subscriber's SubscribeCOVPropertyMultiple request (an unknown one keeps the value advertised before), strictly in capture order with each reference's latest change included (#1008): the oldest changes first, and the untimestamped values with the newest changes that still fit in the last; each envelope names the last change its notification carries.

Untimestamped values that alone exceed one notification follow every timestamped change instead, in as few notifications as fit: runs of whole object items, one object's references apart only where its item alone does not fit (#1038).

Each of those parts completes only the references it carries, and any field a sibling's time stamps there belongs to a change already conveyed. A reference whose latest change went out in an earlier part conveys no change in the last notification, where a sibling carrying its field times it as above, and its observation completes when that part is transmitted, or acknowledged when confirmed.

An unconfirmed report sends every part, each retired once transmitted, one report per context at a time, so another fanout meanwhile leaves its changes queued and gets one follow-up once the report is done (a context without timestamped references holds that turn only while a report of several parts goes out, #1038); a failure, an exhausted budget or communication disabled before a part (Clause 16.1) stops the rest, which the Max_Notification_Delay backstop retries.

The unconfirmed clause expects several notifications; the confirmed clause (13.17) is silent, so splitting a confirmed report is local policy: it sends its oldest part and returns the rest, uncounted and without the bound's eviction, once it holds the context; the Ack's follow-up sends the next part, and a failed part goes out again first after its hold-off.

A change too large for any notification on its own, a reference's latest included, goes out one value per notification instead, in the order its values were captured, each value with the change's Time_Of_Change and each envelope naming the change (#1090); only the part with its last value completes the reference, and parts that fail or are deferred return as one change, which goes out like any other once what is left of it fits.

Several notifications may convey the changes (Clause 13.1) and the COV-multiple clauses (13.16 to 13.18) ask for no grouping of a change's values, so a 50-octet subscriber typically gets Present_Value and Status_Flags in two notifications.

A value too large for any notification even alone is dropped, its change counted once, while the change's other values still go out, so a subscriber whose maximum APDU cannot hold one timestamped value of its references receives none of those values; that subscription is still accepted, as no error the SubscribeCOVPropertyMultiple tables list describes the cause (Clause 13.16; #1039); an untimestamped reference whose values fit no notification alone is left out and logged, not sent over the limit, and is evaluated again at its next fanout (#1038); each report that leaves one out counts it once in untimed_references_oversized, apart from timed_changes_dropped, since nothing of it is lost (#1066).

Untimestamped values have no queue, so a report that began going out owes the untimestamped references of the parts it did not deliver: an unconfirmed report those of the parts left after a stop, a confirmed one those of its deferred parts once it holds the context.

The backstop treats an owed reference as a pending change of its context from when it was first owed (deadline, hold-off, re-enabled communication); the report that next evaluates it takes the mark and reads its value afresh, so a newer change goes in place of the value first prepared, and puts it ahead of newer changes so a split confirmed report cannot defer it for good.

A reference stays owed until a part carrying it is delivered or a report finds nothing left to send for it. A report none of whose parts went out owes nothing new: as before, the next fanout or the failed report's hold-off reports it, though a split confirmed report whose first part fails is brought back at the hold-off's end by the owed references of its deferred parts.

Local bound: one context holds an estimated four notifications of pending history, counting each change's encoding, item framing and a fixed 32-octet overhead, and a per-context reserve, at most one notification's worth, for the most its untimestamped values have taken since it was last admitted or lost a reference; only on overflow is the oldest change dropped, never a reference's latest.

Changes returned by a failed notification wait for an in-flight newer change and are dropped once it is delivered. Those drops are counted in timed_changes_dropped, as is each change that loses a value too large for any notification; each cause (bound overflow, a value too large for any notification, superseded) logs one warning per context until a timestamped reference of it is admitted again or an admission changes its notification size, so the counter is the running signal (#1039).

Changes are reported as soon as they happen; Max_Notification_Delay bounds how long changes left queued by a failed send, an unacknowledged confirmed report, DISABLE_INITIATION or an exhausted budget wait: once the context's delay has passed since its earliest queued change, the context is fanned out again (§13.1, §13.16.1.1.4).

The delay is an upper bound, so overdue changes go out once nothing blocks them: re-enabling communication (DCC request or timer) or admitting a shorter delay retries at once, a confirmed hold-off moves the retry to its end, and an outstanding report's Ack sends what it held back.

Local policy: that backstop acts no sooner than one second after the change and otherwise retries a blocked context at most once per delay (one second at least). The delay and the backstop's wait live only with timestamped histories and owed untimestamped references, so empty-list admissions of unknown contexts keep no state.

WritePropertyMultiple revisits the Life Safety references it captured after its exact fanout, which may not have selected them. Only changes no producer captures (raw database mutation) still use the preparation-time fallback.

Refs #896: a confirmed report completes its references' baselines only on the subscriber's Ack. Each coordinate (an ordinary or SubscribeCOVProperty subscription, or a whole COV-multiple context) has one outstanding confirmed report under one ticket; fanouts skip a busy coordinate, a context's queued timestamped history included, so later changes wait and the next notification to a context still carries every change queued for it (Clauses 13.1, 13.16.3.1.2.3, 13.17.1.1.5).

The Ack fans the coordinate out again, every live reference of a context included even if the carried ones are gone, so held changes follow in one notification and an unchanged value sends nothing; under DCC that follow-up is dropped like any fanout.

Exhausted retries or an Error, Reject or Abort answer return timestamped history, leave the baseline and hold the coordinate off for one full retry cycle (retry timeout times the first attempt plus every retry); fanouts inside the hold-off send nothing and schedule nothing, and the first fanout after it reports again, for a context by re-evaluating every reference whatever object fanned out.

Shutdown and cancellation clear the mark without a hold-off. The retry timeout starts after each send completes and the transport bounds the send, so a report is outstanding for the transport's send bounds plus the retry cycle.

Renewals, route changes and non-empty re-subscriptions of a busy context install a fresh marker: the old incarnation's report stops retrying and can neither complete nor unmark the new one, and initial reports are not held behind it (Clauses 13.14.2, 13.16.2).

A context report fenced while outstanding or owed re-evaluates every context reference, so a relisted reference gets its first report whichever of that follow-up and the initial report goes first; the follow-up may repeat changes the fenced report already delivered.

Because a fenced report may have been delivered although its outcome no longer counts, the same fence first clears the baselines of the kept untimestamped references that report carried (#923), so the follow-up reports their current value even when it went back to the old baseline; this covers a fence during a failed report's hold-off too.

References the report did not carry keep their acknowledged baselines, so the follow-up does not grow to the whole context. Timestamped references keep their baselines, since the fenced history returns to their queue and a change back is captured as another change, and a fence while no report is outstanding or owed clears nothing.

A panicking follow-up batch is caught in unwind builds and logged, and its references wait for their next fanout. The Clause 5.4.4 retry procedure ends delivery, so reporting again after a hold-off is local policy.

Residual gap: without a fence, a failed report keeps its baselines, so if it did arrive and the value goes back during the hold-off it is not re-sent (accepted, #923). Timestamped changes held behind a report that then fails wait for the first natural fanout after the hold-off rather than for any Max_Notification_Delay (13.1), a consequence of not retrying on a timer.

Peer and global in-flight limits, event budgets (one per object or context for follow-ups) and throttling counters are unchanged. Status unchanged. Issues #1058 and #1059 order SubscribeCOVPropertyMultiple admission (Clause 13.16.2): the references are processed in request order, each validated and then checked against the recipient quota and the table capacity, where a renewal or a repeat of an earlier reference takes no slot.

The first that fails ends the request and is named in the first-failed-subscription error, RESOURCES / NO_SPACE_TO_ADD_LIST_ELEMENT at a cap. The references before it are kept as an accepted request's would be (context lifetime, delay and route renewed, timed drop warnings reset) and get their initial notification; those after it are not processed.

A failure of the request itself (inconsistent or out-of-range lifetime and delay, authorization) and a refusal at the first reference keep and report nothing. Issue #1102 makes a missing clock a failure of the reference, not the request: Timestamped is an option each COV reference carries (Clause 13.16.3.1), Clause 13.16.2 keeps the general error for failures before any reference is processed, and the general error table (13.16.3.2.1) covers only context resources, lifetime and delay.

A timestamped reference while the Device has no valid clock is therefore refused itself, after its object and property checks, and named in the first-failed-subscription error with SERVICES / OPTIONAL_FUNCTIONALITY_NOT_SUPPORTED; the references before it are kept and reported and those after it are not processed.

Neither error table has a row for it: Clause 18.5 defines that code for service parameters that would need functionality the device lacks, and Clause 16.1.1.3 pairs it with a device without a clock. The general row for a context that cannot be created never fires and stays documented only (#1102 item 2): a context exists only while it holds references and has no storage or limit of its own, so a new context whose first reference finds no room gets the per-reference RESOURCES / NO_SPACE_TO_ADD_LIST_ELEMENT error.

It ties to the empty-spec context materialization gap below; revisit it if contexts get their own storage or limit. A cancellation validates nothing and removes every listed reference. CovSubscriptionTable::subscribe_multiple returns Err(MultipleRefusal) with the error, the refused position and the kept snapshots.

Issue #1163 keeps a change in delivery out of the local bound's eviction. A change sent one value per notification (#1090) is in delivery from when a part of it is delivered, or sent as a confirmed report's first part with the rest deferred, until its last value is delivered; each reference marks only the change a part last went out ahead of.

Eviction takes neither that change nor a reference's newest, so at a 50-octet subscriber, where the bound holds about one Present_Value and Status_Flags change, a value held back by a failed send or a deferral still goes out after a newer change, and timed_changes_dropped moves only on a real overflow, for a change not yet begun. Beyond the bound a context holds at most two changes per reference. The bound and this exemption are local policy.

notes: Partial RB-21 source READ slice, Refs #727 and #345; broader Audit family status is unchanged. Standard 135-2020 Clause 18.7 pp. 795-799, Tables 19-3/19-4/19-5 pp. 819-828 and Clause 12.63 reviewed; 2024-04-29 errata introduces no source READ field/outcome change.

Direct B/IP IPv4 ClientOnly/Both sessions with one selected private Reporter and a typed built-in Device recipient support both notification modes. Monitored_Objects must be absent for emission, and READ ignores priority filters.

Records preserve actual request invoke ID, one local request-time timestamp, operation-specific target identity (validated Device ACK or direct address including UDP port) and terminal outcome across requester retries/caller waiter cancellation.

A matching ACK omits Result; representable peer Error class/code is preserved; timeout and known Abort/Reject reasons use local COMMUNICATION codes. Reserved/unmapped reasons (including Reject 10), malformed/mismatching ACKs and ambiguous local send errors use COMMUNICATION/OTHER by local policy; an already observed peer terminal takes precedence.

Pre-send rejection is silent. Session-owned tasks begin before egress admission, with 64 whole-operation slots and a separate shared 64-notification pool. One absolute three-second notification deadline, no notification retries/backlog, instance-owned health updates and joined stop bound work without replacing the READ result.

Fair dispatch rotates worker completions, inbound, terminal and policy streams; cancellation remains first. Tests exercise wire fields, both roles/modes, failures, filtering, queue cancellation, capacity/deadline recovery, independent target reporting and shutdown.

Other source operations, selectors, multiple Reporters, batching/send delay, standalone source ownership and other transports are deferred. No durable delivery, full Audit Reporting/BIBB/BTL, PICS/service-bit or whole-product Protocol_Revision claim; #345 remains open.

Refs #732: Clause 19.6.6 / Table 19-5 resource-loss summaries now cover encodable, APDU-fitting eligible source READ records actually dropped by shared audit-permit or confirmed invoke-ID exhaustion, plus known synchronous endpoint egress QueueFull.

One bounded memory-only batch and worker retain a saturating Unsigned count and earliest admission timestamp, despite reversed completion, sequence wrap or clock representation changes. Summary Target_Timestamp is that source record time; Source_Device and Target_Device are local Device; Current_Value is the application Unsigned count and other optional fields are absent.

Non-NONE plus AUDITING_FAILURE-bit gating is local policy. Actual coordinator releases after unlocking wake waiters, including requester-only releases; stale/duplicate cleanup is not capacity. Encoding/size, filtering, pre-send, closed/shutdown, transport/ACK and summary failures do not count or recurse.

Immutable instance/configuration/mode/destination contexts discard incompatible pending counts on mutation and A-to-B-to-A; active Device/Reporter replacement/removal is denied; the latest context survives an empty pending slot and stale contributions cannot supersede it.

The same bounded supersession correction applies to target summaries. Source revalidates DB membership, local Device and generation after waits and before synchronous egress admission; stale delivery health has no authority. No ordinary-record backlog, persistence, restart guarantee, retries or broader Audit status promotion.

Refs #728 source migration: removes StaticSourceAuditRecipient, its builder selector, duplicated copies and ownership-only mode. Source selection requires typed provision even at NONE, one concrete actual Device, absent Monitored_Objects and a client role.

Both requires an explicit Device write authorizer; endpoint WPM stays unsupported. Device choices use immutable direct B/IP bindings, Address choices use network0 six-byte unicast IPv4/nonzero-port without a binding.

Actual post-start broadcast facts are captured before shared locks; resolution is pure. An unresolved Device may start CONFIGURATION_ERROR, suppressing ordinary records without changing READ results or consuming audit sequence/resources.

Local and authorized WP changes use target WRITE semantics: one commit timestamp, actual remote source/invoke or local Device/no invoke, local Device/Object/property, new Target_Value and old Current_Value.

Mandatory old/new attempts bypass NONE/ordinary WRITE filters by the selected property-specific interpretation. NULL/equal are authorized no-ops. Two logical permits, confirmed leases, size checks and owned worker registration precede value/generation/sequence commit; independent bounded egress attempts follow.

Full/closed queue, send or ACK failure never rolls back or retries and cannot cancel the sibling; either failure wins within one generation. Recipient changes retire/wake summaries and fence stale completions.

Device/Reporter/additional-Device membership is protected through quiescence. The public EndpointSession::write_audit_recipient uses the actual Device owner in ClientOnly/Both, treats None as NULL relinquishment and rechecks sealed state after DB acquisition.

Post-ingress profile initialization failure runs joined cleanup and leaves a terminal session; canceled cleanup remains Stopping for stop/Drop completion. Preflight rejection remains retryable. Session and ingress canceled stop retain join ownership for retry.

Source adapters use weak owner projection and become inactive when sealed; dormant external READ futures cannot pin the owner. No broader source operations, Python source API, BIBB or full conformance promotion.

Refs #771 extends this same source READ owner to ReadRange. One attempted request yields one value-free record even for empty/multiple-item ACKs; raw item_data is caller-only. RP/RR share prepared transaction/retry/cancellation and SourceRead filter/typed recipient/64-slot/delivery/failure-summary ownership.

Fallible transactional request encoding rejects ALL/REQUIRED/OPTIONAL, property-array-index0, zero/out-of-INTEGER16 count and nonconcrete ByTime before output/lease/sequence; valid zero position/sequence references remain allowed.

ByTime reuses decoder component bounds without invented weekday/calendar consistency rules. Endpoint ACKs are unsegmented, correlated to request identity and first-sequence semantics; post-attempt segmented response remains a failed READ (local INVALID_APDU_IN_THIS_STATE, peer SEGMENTATION_NOT_SUPPORTED).

Python standalone and EndpointClient share validation and typed dictionary conversion for all-items/position/sequence only, flags tuple and optional first_sequence_number; ByTime is Rust-only. The installed endpoint API does not expose source Reporter configuration.

Direct B/IP Audit scope, recipient generation fencing and stop/Drop ownership remain; source WP and broader Audit families stay open under #345. No row-status/global-pin or service-execution support promotion.

Refs #784: standalone direct/routed and endpoint RP share one decoded ACK identity contract. Property/index match exactly; concrete requests require exact objects, while Device/Network_Port wildcard4194303 requests accept only same-type concrete peer-reported objects.

Unresolved wildcard and wrong-type/object/property/index ACKs return decoding errors. Successful source READ Target_Object uses the validated ACK; a concrete Device ACK also establishes Target_Device for that operation (RP or RR), per Table19-4.

Network_Port/other object successes and failed/no-valid-ACK operations retain direct Address; errors retain the requested object/alias as the attempted identity, an explicit local representation when no actual object was established.

No guessed instance, local source Device substitution or cross-operation discovery cache. Real B/IP Device-server regression, four direct/routed client matrices and source wire tests cover concrete/both-alias bounds, malformed/mismatched failures, both roles/modes, one record across canceled retry and retained recipient snapshot, lease/permit release and value-free fields.

Installed Python validates both client surfaces with bundled-server and independent raw UDP ACKs. Bundled server Network_Port ingress mapping remains #785; broader Audit remains #345, no status/global-pin promotion.

Refs #780 adds Rust/Python endpoint RPM through the same closed requester/source owner:1–64 explicit occurrences across nonempty concrete-object specifications, no ALL/REQUIRED/OPTIONAL/wildcards, index0 valid.

These are endpoint profile restrictions; standalone selectors remain. Shared RPM request encode returns Result and validates nonempty lists before buffer mutation; all callers migrate. Complete ordered ACK object/property occurrence counts/IDs are correlated before projection; values echo requested indexes, inline errors may omit or repeat a requested index but cannot substitute another, and unindexed requests require no index.

Audit retains requested index; indistinguishable duplicate omitted-index errors cannot reveal a peer reorder. Request/raw ACK byte limits use configured unsegmented APDU bounds before decode. One operation/lease/permit/worker/timestamp/invoke/recipient-generation snapshot survives retries and caller cancellation; per-reference filters precede independent bounded value-free records.

Whole-service failures fan out final failure to eligible attempted references as local representation, not remote success inference. Exactly one distinct successful concrete Device object in a complete ACK establishes operation-local Target_Device across records; error-only or conflicting successful Device IDs retain Address.

Typed synchronous egress QueueFull is known local resource loss and joins existing High Volume coalescing; Closed/shutdown and attempted transport/ACK failures are not counted. A summary rejected by QueueFull is restored into the same bounded generation-fenced batch and awaits egress capacity without ordinary retries, recursive counts or unbounded waiters; stop owns its cancellation.

Default16-slot congestion and128-slot full-success fixtures distinguish admission from delivery, while per-permit saturation counts only dropped occurrences. Source remains direct B/IP/Rust-configured, Python conversion matches standalone results, server scalar-error index producer issue remains #789, and broader Audit #345 stays open. No row status/global pin promotion.

Its test reads the method list from the trait's source and runs each method through the adapter against a probe that logs its calls, comparing arguments and answers with the probe's own; only deletion is answered by an active source itself.

python_static_target_reporter.contract: add_audit_reporter remains inert unless configure_audit_reporters is called. Empty/over-64 lists, duplicate identities and reserved instance4194303 are rejected. configure_audit_recipient copies and validates a separate typed initial provision, required before startup even at NONE; it replaces the removed recipient_device_instance keyword. Missing/wrong/duplicate pending identities, local recipient, invalid level, reserved/overflowing operation mask or non-bool confirmation reject without mutation. Full u64 operation mask positions are preserved. Optional monitored_objects dict field accepts None/omission (property absent/catch-all) or an exact list of ObjectIdentifier (exact match), ObjectType (all instances, including extensible values) and ignored None/NULL entries. Empty/all-NULL selects no ordinary targets; duplicate/overlapping selectors never duplicate records. Wrong containers/elements raise TypeError. Optional audit_priority_filter accepts None/omission (all, 0xFFFF) or a strict non-bool u16 mask, including zero: bit 0 is priority 1, bit 15 priority 16, including omitted write priority. Wrong types/bool raise TypeError; negatives/overflow raise ValueError. Commandable-property writes use the mask; non-commandable and non-write operations do not. Enabled Reporter-target writes retain the selection/WRITE/priority bypass. All dict fields validate before mutation; omitted options reset defaults on replacement. Startup revalidates every identity before draining registrations and freezes configuration at ownership transfer, including startup in flight and after stop. Pre-transfer validation/transport preparation failures remain retryable. Binding/configuration order is independent; an unresolved recipient permits startup with CONFIGURATION_ERROR on an enabled Reporter and no ordinary-record growth. Generic read_property exposes RELIABILITY/STATUS_FLAGS.

See target_device_recipient and docs/device-audit-recipient.md. Partial evidence; Refs #345. ConfirmedAuditNotification decodes before policy/storage, requires one explicit Audit Log sink and a fail-closed fast authorizer, keeps immediate/routed transport provenance separate from peer-reported payload identity, and applies each accepted list in wire order.

The built-in Audit Log now commits the resulting records and a complete exact confirmed-request key in one schema-v2 snapshot with a restart-stable Unix UTC completion timestamp. Schema-v1 snapshots load with an empty ledger; unknown future versions and malformed or oversized receipt state fail closed under the existing checksummed two-slot recovery policy.

Retention remains 60 seconds and 256 completed entries with deterministic oldest-completion eviction; age 60 seconds expires, while clock rollback or a future timestamp fails open and is pruned on the next accepted commit.

A retained durable duplicate is checked before authorization and atomically rechecked by the mutation owner, then discarded without record, generation, authorization, or response effects. The general process-local tracker remains the all-service pending/session guard.

Complementary record matching still uses twice Device APDU_Timeout; like Time/DateTime variants compare temporal distance while SequenceNumber requires equality and mixed variants do not match. Receiver payload/list caps of 64 KiB/256 remain repository policy.

Unconfirmed receipt never writes the ledger. Synchronous persistence under the database writer limits availability. Missing/non-Audit identifiers and absent query capability retain their existing errors; malformed payloads retain SERVICES/OTHER mapping.

Raw target/current ANY values receive structural TLV validation only, not property-schema validation. Python exposes typed Audit clients (integer 0..2 success filter with the deprecated Boolean rejected, Unsigned64 cursor) alongside the byte-compatible raw outbound escape hatches.

RB-21a adds only the target-WRITE immediate-send profile described in target_write_immediate. Corrected Device recipient requirement: Clause 12.11 with 135-2020 Errata Summary 2024-04-29 item 25 (PDF page 7), preserving base O and footnotes 19-20; NULL operation semantics in 15.9/15.10/19.2; record shape Table 19-4 and BACnetRecipient in Clause 21.
target_device_recipient.contract: One typed built-in Device value; provision alone stays unexposed. Active runtime exposes required/writable RP/RPM/Property_List metadata while retaining optional base conformance and AuditReporting condition. Local/direct/WP/WPM actual changes prepare both immutable routes, resources and encoding before value/generation/shared-sequence commit and owned worker registration. NULL/equal requests are unchanged successes after normal checks. Dedicated old/new WRITE attempts bypass ordinary WRITE/NONE filters as the selected property-specific interpretation; different values resolving to the same route still consume two attempts. Actual remote source/invoke or local/local context is retained. No duplicate ordinary observer. Independent three-second attempts use new-generation tokens; any failure survives sibling success and cannot roll back committed state. Target historical summary counts retain captured routes across ABA within the bounds in BACNET-12-AUDIT-REPORTER-DELAY; stale completions cannot affect current health.
target_device_recipient.routes: Configured local/routed Device routes remain transport-neutral. Observed-only bindings are ineligible. Unresolved Device provision starts CONFIGURATION_ERROR, but both old/new routes must resolve for a live change; correcting an unavailable old route requires restart. Address support requires explicit IPv4 B/IP, network zero, six-byte unicast IP/nonzero-port, excluding unspecified/broadcast/multicast. Unsupported valid route choices return a semantic error distinct from malformed encoding.
target_device_recipient.lifecycle: Active and sealed ownership protects selected Device/Reporter removal, replacement and adapter callbacks, plus additional Device insertion. Narrow DeviceAuthority replaces raw mutable concrete access. Normal stop seals before close, joins producers/dispatch and drains workers, then uninstalls under DB guard. Canceled stop remains sealed/retryable. Drop aborts owned work and weak membership releases only after retained task frames quiesce.
target_device_recipient.limits: Existing mutation policy remains default Permissive without authorizer; Audit installation is not authentication. No durable outbox, retry, broader Address support or full Audit status promotion.

target_multiple_reporters.scope: Refs #782; target profile only. Standard135-2020 §12.63 and §19.6, including §19.6.2–3 printed819–820/PDF821–822 and Table19-5 printed823/PDF825. Existing row status and global review pins remain unchanged.
target_multiple_reporters.association: One through 64 concrete distinct target Reporters, canonicalized by instance. The cap is local policy. Enabled nominal selector membership determines lowest-instance election before operation/value filters and faults every actual overlap with CONFIGURATION_ERROR. Absent selectors are catch-all; empty/all-NULL select none. Subject add/remove and configuration changes refresh overlap. AV/BV policy inherits the elected Reporter. Source mode stays exactly one.
target_multiple_reporters.mutation: One object-owned configuration authority backs fallible local setters, atomic six-field aggregate configuration (including optional maximum send delay) and Description. Compare BACnet representations and emit each changed property in numeric PID order; equal local configuration is silent. Prepare all records/permits/confirmed leases/encoding/worker ownership before committing any field. Own enable uses post-state, disable/other enabled changes use pre-state. Lowest enabled nominal owner else configured self fallback is local policy, not nominal overlap. A target remaining NONE has no own fallback but can be observed by another eligible Reporter. The selected existing network WRITE attempt policy preserves no-op and execution-failure records for an enabled Reporter independently of WRITE/selector filters; failures include Result. This is local attempt accounting, not a normative failure/no-op mandate. Description sink/observer dedup retains original source/invoke exactly once. No new network configuration execution is added. Reporter Description uses common NULL relinquishment semantics: unchanged success, never stored NULL; any array index rejects before value handling with PROPERTY/PROPERTY_IS_NOT_AN_ARRAY. Standard §15.9.1.1/.1.3 printed752–753/PDF754–755. Direct and WP/WPM regressions distinguish no actual change from the selected network attempt record.
target_multiple_reporters.ownership: Per-Reporter object-owned health, configuration generation and one bounded loss coalescer; one global64 operation budget, not64 per Reporter. Alternating contexts do not erase others. Recipient changes retain one atomic old/new pair, owned by lowest enabled nominal Device match, else lowest enabled configured, else lowest configured; this is local election policy. Fence every Reporter old-recipient context. All configured identities and Device stay protected through sealed/canceled/Drop lifetime until owned frames quiesce.

rows.standard_anchor: Clause 15.9.1.3 (WriteProperty error table) with Clause 21 BACnetNotifyType / BACnetEventTransitionBits / BACnetLimitEnable productions
rows.requirement_summary: WriteProperty validation of the shared intrinsic-reporting event properties matches the Clause 15.9.1.3 error semantics: Notify_Type generally follows the closed BACnetNotifyType {alarm, event, ack-notification} production and refuses out-of-production values with PROPERTY / VALUE_OUT_OF_RANGE; Alert Enrollment narrows its configurable property to ALARM/EVENT because ACK_NOTIFICATION belongs to acknowledgement-flow output. Event_Enable / Limit_Enable (BACnetEventTransitionBits = 3 bits, BACnetLimitEnable = 2 bits) require the canonical encoding of their fixed-width production - exactly one content octet with 8-N declared unused bits, the form the read path emits - refusing any other shape with PROPERTY / INVALID_DATA_ENCODING. A previously-silent normalization of an over-long bit string is now a refusal, as is empty content.
notes: Split child of BACNET-12-OBJECT-MODEL (#255; behavior change - previously-accepted invalid writes now fail). The generic macro arms cover AI/AO/AV/BI/BO/BV/MSI/MSO/MSV, the analog macro arm adds Limit_Enable, and Event Enrollment carries its own full BACnetNotifyType arm.

Alert Enrollment's PR-0808 arm deliberately accepts only configurable ALARM/EVENT and rejects ACK_NOTIFICATION, which belongs to acknowledgement-flow output; its wire tests also pin wrong-type and overwide refusal before mutation.

EventEnrollment and AlertEnrollment retain their own fixed-width Event_Enable arms. A shared objects-layer helper shapes the bit-string PROPERTY error. Related unaddressed family: the Notification Class recipient-list decoder still masks transition/day bit strings without consulting declared counts.
evidence: Split child of `BACNET-12-OBJECT-MODEL` (#255; behavior change — previously-accepted invalid writes now fail). WriteProperty validation of the shared intrinsic-reporting event properties matches the Clause 15.9.1.3 error table: `Notify_Type` (BACnetNotifyType, a closed {alarm, event, ack-notification} production, Clause 21) refuses out-of-production values with PROPERTY / VALUE_OUT_OF_RANGE (a value outside the property's permitted range) instead of storing them — an accepted `Enumerated(99)` previously read back as 99 and could reach the wire as the notification's notifyType; membership derives from `NotifyType::ALL_NAMED` so a future addendum constant widens the gate without a second edit.

`Event_Enable` / `Limit_Enable` (BACnetEventTransitionBits = 3 bits, BACnetLimitEnable = 2 bits, Clause 21) require the canonical encoding of their fixed-width production — exactly one content octet with 8−N declared unused bits, the form the read path emits — refusing any other declared shape (an 8-bit string where fewer bits are defined, extra or missing content octets, a half-octet string; for Limit_Enable even Event_Enable's valid 3-bit shape) with PROPERTY / INVALID_DATA_ENCODING (an encoding incompatible with the property's datatype) instead of silent mask-and-normalize; an empty content now reports INVALID_DATA_ENCODING rather than INVALID_DATA_TYPE.

Applies to the generic macro arms (AI/AO/AV/BI/BO/BV/MSI/MSO/MSV), the analog macro's Limit_Enable, and the own arms on EventEnrollment and AlertEnrollment, via a shared objects-layer helper (`common::check_fixed_width_bit_string`) that reports protocol errors — the decoding-layer sibling in `bacnet-encoding` is intentionally not reused across layers.

Evidence: object-level probes across `crates/bacnet-objects/src/{analog/tests/input.rs,binary/tests/generic_event_properties.rs,multistate/tests/generic_event_properties.rs,event_enrollment/tests/enrollment.rs}` and wire-level `crates/bacnet-server/src/handlers/tests/write_validation.rs`. Follow-up family: the Notification Class recipient-list decoder still masks transition/day bit strings without consulting declared counts.

rows.standard_anchor: Clause 15.9 WriteProperty (15.9.1.2 Result(+), 15.9.1.3 Result(-)), Clause 15.10 WritePropertyMultiple, Clause 20.2.1 (concatenated elements)
rows.requirement_summary: WriteProperty and WritePropertyMultiple decode the entire propertyValue payload: elements are decoded with decode_application_value until the input is exhausted - the mirror of encode_property_value's List flattening - so one element yields the scalar PropertyValue and more than one yields PropertyValue::List. Full consumption is required: a partial or undecodable trailing element is PROPERTY / INVALID_DATA_ENCODING per Clause 15.9.1.3 (an encoding incompatible with the property's datatype) - never a silent drop - with the stored value proven unchanged; a well-formed extra element reaches a scalar arm and fails its shape as INVALID_DATA_TYPE. Empty payloads are also INVALID_DATA_ENCODING except for Fault_Signals (Clause 12.60) and Calendar Date_List (Clause 12.9), BACnetLISTs that may be empty, which are delivered as an empty PropertyValue::List. The RECIPIENT_LIST verbatim special-case keeps its precedence and the context-tagged ApplicationData widening of the single-element decoder is preserved (framed CHOICE properties, Clause 12.17 reference members).
notes: Split child of BACNET-12-OBJECT-MODEL (#182; behavior change - trailing bytes previously dropped between the single-element decoder and the arm now decide the write, and malformed value payloads map to PROPERTY / INVALID_DATA_ENCODING instead of the SERVICES/OTHER a propagated raw decoding error produced).

A value TLV-truncated so far that framing breaks is refused by the shared incremental service grammar before that write is attempted. Unlocks covered here: MSI Alarm_Values whole-list writes (the pin in handlers/list.rs flipped from pinned failure to per-element-validated success) and the datetime-paired value properties completing #270 (DateTime Value PV / Priority_Array entries, Relinquish_Default on DateTime Value + DateTime Pattern Value; see BACNET-12-RELINQUISH-DEFAULT-WRITABILITY).

#401 adds the narrow zero-element exception for Fault_Signals and #996 one for Calendar Date_List; other empty propertyValue payloads remain refused. WPM decodes and commits each complete attempt in order and stops at the first failure.

AddListElement/RemoveListElement now validate all elements before mutation and reject malformed tails atomically (#279). Remaining separate residues: Enumerated contents wider than four octets still truncate to u32 (#277, explicitly untouched); and properties declared SEQUENCE OF beyond the four reference arms (e.g. LIST_OF_OBJECT_PROPERTY_REFERENCES) keep their pre-existing arm-level behavior.
evidence: Split child of `BACNET-12-OBJECT-MODEL` (#182; behavior change — previously-dropped trailing bytes now decide the write). The WriteProperty/WritePropertyMultiple value decoder consumed exactly one application-tagged primitive and silently discarded the rest, so no structured or `BACnetLIST` property value could reach an object arm whole.

`decode_write_property_value` (`crates/bacnet-server/src/handlers/write_property.rs`) now loop-decodes until the payload is exhausted — the exact mirror of `encode_property_value`'s `List` flattening: one element → scalar `PropertyValue`, more than one → `PropertyValue::List`, and full consumption is REQUIRED — a partial or undecodable trailing element is PROPERTY / INVALID_DATA_ENCODING (Clause 15.9.1.3) and an empty payload is refused, while a well-formed extra element reaches a scalar arm and fails its shape as INVALID_DATA_TYPE; in every case the stored value is proven unchanged.

The RECIPIENT_LIST verbatim special-case keeps its precedence (the object layer owns its framed `BACnetLIST` codec), and the context-tagged behavior is preserved: framed CHOICE properties (Event_Parameters/Fault_Parameters) still arrive as a single `ApplicationData`, and context-tagged member productions (the Clause 12.17 references) arrive as one `ApplicationData` element per member — see `BACNET-12-REFERENCE-PROPERTY-WRITABILITY`.

A value TLV-truncated so far that framing breaks is refused earlier by the service request's own [3]/[4] walk (a framing error, never silent). Unlocks: MSI `Alarm_Values` whole-list writes (`whole_list_write_property_decodes_all_elements`, was a pinned failure) and the datetime-paired value properties (DateTime Value PV / priority-array entries / Relinquish_Default, completing #270 — see `BACNET-12-RELINQUISH-DEFAULT-WRITABILITY`).

WPM ordered-prefix execution covers structured values (`wpm_reference_write_commits_in_order_and_keeps_prefix_on_failure`). Evidence: `crates/bacnet-server/src/handlers/write_property.rs` + `handlers/tests/multi_element_writes.rs` + `handlers/tests/reference_writes.rs`, `handlers/list.rs` tests.

Known residues (follow-ups): AddListElement/RemoveListElement still break their `listOfElements` loop on an undecodable element instead of erroring (#182's wider scope); Enumerated contents wider than four octets truncate to u32 (#277, untouched here); and properties declared `SEQUENCE OF` beyond the four reference arms (e.g. `LIST_OF_OBJECT_PROPERTY_REFERENCES`) keep their pre-existing arm-level behavior.

notes: Refs #999. BACnetObject::is_list_property is a provided method beside is_array_property; its default classifies by Clause 12 datatype, including the type-dependent Alarm_Values / Fault_Values, List_Of_Object_Property_References, Present_Value (a list only on Group) and Member_Of (a single reference on Audit Log).

The 2020 tables define no BACnetARRAY of BACnetLIST, so an indexed array element is never a list. An index on a non-array is refused as PROPERTY / PROPERTY_IS_NOT_AN_ARRAY after a whole-property read, so absence keeps its UNKNOWN_PROPERTY precedence.

Recipient_List of Notification Class and Notification Forwarder alone takes the destination codec; a list held framed with no element codec (the standalone Device COV subscription lists, read-only, and Schedule List_Of_Object_Property_References until #1121 gave it the reference codec) returns PROPERTY / WRITE_ACCESS_DENIED instead of being decoded as destinations.

Before, a RemoveListElement naming absent members of a value that reads as several members (DateTime Value Present_Value) was acknowledged and wrote a priority-16 command; it is now refused with nothing written.

Audit observation is unchanged in kind: a target refusal with well-formed elements reports the response error and the readable pre-image. Since #1026 every target refusal goes out as a ChangeList-Error with First Failed Element Number 0; element rules and element numbers are in BACNET-15-LIST-ELEMENT-SEMANTICS. ReadRange applies the same classification and target order (BACNET-15-READ-RANGE-TARGET-KIND, #1025). No broader list-property or complete service conformance claim.

rows.requirement_summary: Inbound AddListElement and RemoveListElement compare whole elements (no served list narrows the comparison) and apply all of a request or none of it. AddListElement leaves an element already present, a repeat within the request included, and that is not a failure. RemoveListElement refuses the request at the first element, in request order, whose datatype differs from the stored elements' (PROPERTY / INVALID_DATA_TYPE) or that is absent (SERVICES / LIST_ELEMENT_NOT_FOUND), and removes nothing. This holds for the values, destination, calendar-entry and reference codecs. Both services answer every error with a ChangeList-Error: the class and code in [0] and, in [1], the First Failed Element Number, which is the 1-based position of the refused element for decode, datatype, not-found and object element refusals, and 0 for refusals of the request or target. Other services keep the plain class/code Error PDU. The APDU codec recognizes the body for services 8 and 9 in both directions, the client surfaces it as Error::Structured with ErrorDetail::FirstFailedElementNumber, and Python's BacnetProtocolError carries first_failed_element_number.

notes: Refs #1026 and #1027; builds on BACNET-15-LIST-ELEMENT-TARGET-KIND (#999) and the calendar-entry codec (#996). Breaking on the wire: both services used to answer with the plain class/code Error PDU, which a peer expecting the ChangeList production misreads, and the client could not decode the ChangeList form at all.

Elements compare by canonical encoding, which equals value equality for every codec and keeps the comparison linear. Neither Recipient_List description (Notification Class, Notification Forwarder) narrows the comparison, so a destination differing in any field is another element.

Notification Forwarder Subscribed_Recipients, whose description matches on recipient and process identifier only, is not served. The values codec takes the datatype a removal must match from the stored elements; an empty list shows none, so there any element is LIST_ELEMENT_NOT_FOUND. Decode errors are found in a first pass over every element, before the target's stored list is read; the remaining checks run in request order.

Refs #1048: the object validates the edited list (stored elements, then the new ones in request order) and may name the element it refuses, as Error::Structured with FirstFailedElementNumber holding its position in that list; the handler records where each added element came from in the request and reports that position, with no trial writes.

The built-in Multi-state Alarm_Values, Lift and Escalator Fault_Signals and Calendar Date_List writers name their datatype, encoding, range and space refusals (since #1121 so does the Schedule's List_Of_Object_Property_References writer, for its datatype, encoding, space and remote-device refusals), and the Notification Class Recipient_List writer names the first destination past its 32-destination cap (#1098), which AddListElement reports as NO_SPACE_TO_ADD_LIST_ELEMENT at the request element that brought it, so the handler's own Date_List range pre-check (#1029) is gone.

A named element the list already held, or a refusal of what a removal leaves, is no element of the request and reports 0 (Clause 15.1.1.3.2). A refusal that names no element, from a custom object, keeps the earlier estimate: the first element the list would gain, exact for a request adding one new element.

Before #1048 a named refusal passed through unmapped, so a custom object's list position went out as the request's element number. WriteProperty and WritePropertyMultiple keep the plain class/code on the wire; their Rust results now carry the detail.

A pure-duplicate AddListElement still writes the unchanged list, so the object's write-access check applies. Audit observation is unchanged in kind: an executable request that fails (not found, datatype, object refusal) is recorded with its error and pre-image, and malformed elements stay silent. CreateObject-Error, which has the same shape, and the other structured error bodies are BACNET-21-STRUCTURED-ERROR-BODIES (#1047), which generalized Error::ChangeList into Error::Structured.
