rows.requirement_summary: The Clause 21 error productions that replace the plain class/code pair are recognized by service in both APDU directions: CreateObject-Error ([0] Error, [1] first failed element number), SubscribeCOVPropertyMultiple-Error (a CHOICE of the [0] Error alone or the [1] failed subscription with its [0] object identifier, [1] property reference and [2] Error), ConfirmedPrivateTransfer-Error ([0] Error, [1] vendor identifier, [2] service number, optional [3] error parameters) and VTClose-Error ([0] Error, optional [1] list of Unsigned8 session identifiers), with ChangeList-Error and WritePropertyMultiple-Error. A conformant peer's body decodes instead of failing APDU decode and timing out. The client reports the body's fields as Error::Structured with an ErrorDetail (element number, first failed write attempt, first failed subscription, vendor/service/parameters, sessions not closed); a body with nothing beyond the error is Error::Protocol. Python's BacnetProtocolError carries the fields as attributes that default to None. The server answers every CreateObject error with a CreateObject-Error naming the initial value it could not apply, or 0 when the request or the object is refused; an undecodable initial value is PROPERTY / INVALID_DATA_ENCODING at its position. It answers every SubscribeCOVPropertyMultiple error with the failed-subscription choice for a refused COV reference and with the general choice for a failure before the references are processed. ConfirmedPrivateTransfer and VT-Close are not served.
notes: Refs #1047, following #1026 (BACNET-15-LIST-ELEMENT-SEMANTICS), whose Error::ChangeList became the general Error::Structured; TsmResponse::Error carries detail: Option<ErrorDetail>. Breaking on the wire: CreateObject and SubscribeCOVPropertyMultiple errors used to be the plain class/code pair.

The detail is boxed so Error stays 32 bytes. Since #1058 the SubscribeCOVPropertyMultiple server keeps the references processed before a refused one, as the service procedure does, and sends their initial notifications.

A refusal of a whole subscription specification (unknown object, object without COV) names its first COV reference. COV table capacity is checked one reference at a time (#1059), so the reference past the recipient quota or the table capacity is named, as an oversized sample is.

A timestamped reference while the Device has no valid clock is named the same way, with SERVICES / OPTIONAL_FUNCTIONALITY_NOT_SUPPORTED (#1102). CreateObject keeps its refusal codes (an Object_Name in use is OBJECT / DUPLICATE_NAME); only the undecodable initial value changed from SERVICES / OTHER to PROPERTY / INVALID_DATA_ENCODING, and it is still a malformed request, not an audited execution.

ConfirmedPrivateTransfer-Error decodes the vendor identifier as u32, like the request and ACK types, where the production narrows it to Unsigned16. A VTClose-Error list that is present but empty decodes as an empty list.

rows.requirement_summary: Inbound ReadRange decides from the target property's datatype, before any range selection, whether it is a BACnetLIST, and refuses every other target (scalar, constructed single value, whole array or indexed array element) with SERVICES / PROPERTY_IS_NOT_A_LIST. Unknown object, unknown property and array-index errors take precedence, and LIST_ITEM_NOT_NUMBERED / LIST_ITEM_NOT_TIMESTAMPED follow. A list held framed in one ApplicationData is split into its elements with the element codec its datatype names (BACnetDestination for Recipient_List, BACnetDeviceObjectPropertyReference for Schedule and Timer List_Of_Object_Property_References, BACnetCOVSubscription and BACnetCOVMultipleSubscription for the Device's Active_COV_Subscriptions and Active_COV_Multiple_Subscriptions), so By Position addresses elements. A running server reads the two Device COV lists through the same Device view and one request-local COV table snapshot as ReadProperty, so a page's items joined in order are a run of the ReadProperty value; a list the server cannot split is refused with SERVICES / OPTIONAL_FUNCTIONALITY_NOT_SUPPORTED.
notes: Refs #1025, following #999: ReadRange uses BACnetObject::is_list_property and the same target order as the list services. The 2020 tables define no BACnetARRAY of BACnetLIST, so an indexed array element is never a list: an index on a non-array is PROPERTY / PROPERTY_IS_NOT_AN_ARRAY after a whole-property read (absence keeps UNKNOWN_PROPERTY), and an index on an array is SERVICES / PROPERTY_IS_NOT_A_LIST.

Before, ReadRange went by the value's shape: it paged whole arrays (Object_List, Priority_Array, State_Text, Property_List, Weekly_Schedule), array elements that read as several values and BACnetDateTime values, and it refused the framed Recipient_List and Schedule List_Of_Object_Property_References as not lists. Calendar Date_List (#996) and Elevator Group Landing_Calls already hold one encoded element per item.

Refs #1046: a running server's ReadRange reads through the same request-local Device view as ReadProperty. For the selected Device's Active_COV_Subscriptions or Active_COV_Multiple_Subscriptions it samples the COV table once per request while it holds the database read guard (database before COV table), and splits the live frame with the new BACnetCOVSubscription and BACnetCOVMultipleSubscription element decoders.

Wire tests compare every whole-list, By Position and byte-capped page with the ReadProperty value cut by the suite's independent decoders, cover empty and cancelled lists, and check that pages read during concurrent subscribe/cancel traffic are whole, contiguous runs whose flags match.

#1046 found the Device view answering is_list_property and the log-record identities with the trait defaults; since #1076 it forwards every read-only BACnetObject query to the object it wraps, and answers itself only the Device's executor-owned rows (Property_List, the metadata and required set it derives them from, and no frozen COV copy).

A test reads the trait's source and fails when a query lacks a forwarding check, and a probe object answers every query unlike its default. Before #1046 ReadRange read the Device object's empty placeholder and refused both lists with SERVICES / OPTIONAL_FUNCTIONALITY_NOT_SUPPORTED.

Standalone handle_read_range has no executor context and pages the Device object's empty lists as zero items, as standalone handle_read_property reads them. Vendor lists held framed, stored frames that do not decode and list values of any other shape are still refused with SERVICES / OPTIONAL_FUNCTIONALITY_NOT_SUPPORTED.

The Python ReadRange tests moved from Device Object_List, an array, to Calendar Date_List. No complete ReadRange conformance claim. Since #1097 the rows and the probe live in bacnet-objects/tests/support/forwarding, shared with the source Reporter adapter's test, and the view's forwarded calls are compared argument for argument as well as by answer.

rows.requirement_summary: Typed outbound WPM validates the complete nonempty request and each nonempty property-write list, excludes ALL/REQUIRED/OPTIONAL targets, and accepts supplied priorities only in 1..16. Encoding is transactional; standalone direct and device-directed clients reject before request admission or discovery, and both Python entrypoints validate synchronously before future creation.
notes: Refs #793. This is an outbound typed service contract, not remote property metadata or commandability validation. Omitted priority, 1..16, index zero, proprietary identifiers, NULL and legal empty-list value payloads remain valid.

The outer nonempty constraint follows the service procedure; no absent ASN.1 SIZE restriction is inferred. BACnetPropertyValue encoding shared with other services is unchanged. Inbound empty request/list no-ops, malformed-wire cursor classifications and ordered-prefix/formal-error behavior remain separate and retain raw fixture coverage.

Python propagates property-value encoding errors; no practical small-input encoding failure is claimed. Priorities outside native u8 extraction raise OverflowError, while invalid u8 priorities and structure raise ValueError synchronously.

Semantic failures return the formal service-16 Error body with Error plus the complete first-failed BACnetObjectPropertyReference. notes: Refs #741: syntactically valid Unsigned priorities outside 1..16 retain a typed PriorityOutOfRange cursor failure and return formal SERVICES / PARAMETER_OUT_OF_RANGE both before writes and after a committed prefix.

The public cursor error kind replaces its former reject-only field; whole-request decode still returns Error::Decoding. Bounded service-procedure correction (Refs #242), not full BACnet, object, PICS, or BIBB conformance.

Inbound empty requests and empty property lists retain the existing SimpleACK/no-op behavior; outbound typed requests reject them before encoding (#793).

evidence: Service 16 parses and executes complete write attempts in wire order, retains the successful prefix, stops on the first failure, and emits the formal `[0] Error` plus `[1] BACnetObjectPropertyReference` Result(-) body for semantic or post-prefix syntax failures.

Pre-write malformed bodies use the narrow classified Reject reason; post-prefix malformed bodies use SERVICES / INVALID_TAG and an exact completed reference or the documented DEVICE:4194303 / ALL / no-index local sentinel.

Response emission precedes committed-prefix generic and exact Life Safety COV. Low-level `ErrorPdu.error_data` retains provenance; legacy generic WPM errors and high-level class/code projections remain compatible. Empty requests/property lists remain no-op. This is a bounded service correction (`Refs #242`), not a broad PICS/BIBB or Acked_Transitions claim.

rows.requirement_summary: A SubscribeCOV notification for a Loop carries Present_Value, Status_Flags, Setpoint and Controlled_Variable_Value, in that order, and is sent when Present_Value moves by at least COV_Increment or Status_Flags changes. For a Staging object it carries Present_Value, Status_Flags and Present_Stage and is sent on such a Present_Value move, a Status_Flags change (including a target-plan completion that changes Reliability) or any Present_Stage change. Both objects serve a writable COV_Increment REAL that refuses negative or non-finite values with PROPERTY / VALUE_OUT_OF_RANGE. Loop serves the required read-only Controlled_Variable_Value. A running server's application feeds it with BACnetServer::set_controlled_variable_value_local (Python: set_controlled_variable_value_local), a finite REAL refused on other objects with OBJECT / OPTIONAL_FUNCTIONALITY_NOT_SUPPORTED and accepted while Out_Of_Service is TRUE; a SubscribeCOVProperty on it is notified of the change, and a SubscribeCOV report carries the new value the next time it fires. SubscribeCOVProperty reports the selected property with Status_Flags; Present_Value inherits COV_Increment. An Averaging object, which Table 13-1 doesn't list, refuses SubscribeCOV with OBJECT / OPTIONAL_FUNCTIONALITY_NOT_SUPPORTED and admits SubscribeCOVProperty and SubscribeCOVPropertyMultiple; a numeric property is reported when it moves by the subscription's COV increment, or on any change without one, with no Status_Flags. A running server's application feeds it samples with BACnetServer::add_averaging_sample_local (Python: add_averaging_sample_local): a BOOLEAN (0 or 1), Signed, Unsigned, Enumerated or finite REAL converted to REAL, other datatypes refused with PROPERTY / INVALID_DATA_TYPE, non-finite REALs with PROPERTY / VALUE_OUT_OF_RANGE and other objects with OBJECT / OPTIONAL_FUNCTIONALITY_NOT_SUPPORTED. Minimum_Value, Maximum_Value, Average_Value, Attempted_Samples and Valid_Samples change together, and a property subscription on one of them is notified. None in place of a value records a missed attempt (Attempted_Samples moves, Valid_Samples doesn't), refused on the same targets. The positive infinity, negative infinity and NaN an empty sample window reads are compared by their bits, so a move to or from one is always reported, whatever the subscription's increment, and staying at one never is. #1061: every object type Table 13-1 lists that the stack builds takes SubscribeCOV, including Access Point, Credential Data Input and Load Control, which refused it before. An Access Door report carries Present_Value, Status_Flags and Door_Alarm_State, and a Door_Alarm_State change sends one. An Access Point report leads with Access_Event instead of Present_Value, then Status_Flags, Access_Event_Tag and Access_Event_Time, and only an Access_Event_Time or Status_Flags change sends one. A Credential Data Input report carries Present_Value, Status_Flags and Update_Time, and an Update_Time change sends one. A Load Control report carries Present_Value, Status_Flags, Requested_Shed_Level, Start_Time and Shed_Duration, and a change of any of them sends one. A Pulse Converter report carries Update_Time, whose change alone sends none.
notes: Split child of BACNET-13-COV-SUBSCRIPTIONS (#985, #988). The server takes the extra values from BACnetObject::cov_reported_properties (a default keyed by object type that custom objects may override) under the same object borrow as Present_Value and Status_Flags, leaves out a declared property the object's Property_List lacks, and sends nothing when a listed one fails to read, as for an unreadable Present_Value.

Only trigger values (Present_Stage) are kept in the delivered observation; Setpoint and Controlled_Variable_Value are carried at their current value. A WriteProperty runs a Staging plan before its own fanout, so a stage change and the completion's Status_Flags can arrive in one notification; write_local reports the stage first.

Local reading of Table 13-1a: a SubscribeCOVProperty on Present_Value reports Present_Value and Status_Flags only, and a Staging Present_Value property subscription does not fire on a Present_Stage change alone.

#1061 lists the remaining rows in the cov_reported_properties default: Access Door Door_Alarm_State (trigger); Access Point Access_Event_Tag, Access_Event_Time (trigger), Access_Event_Credential and Access_Event_Authentication_Factor; Credential Data Input Update_Time (trigger); and Load Control Requested_Shed_Level, Start_Time, Shed_Duration and Duty_Window (all triggers).

The server picks the leading value by object type (cov/reported.rs lead): Present_Value as a trigger, or on an Access Point Access_Event, which doesn't trigger; Active_COV_Subscriptions names the same property.

Credential Data Input's Present_Value stays a trigger although its row's criteria name only Update_Time and Status_Flags: Clause 12.36 has Update_Time change on every Present_Value update, so this sends no report the row wouldn't.

Load Control has no COV_Increment, so its Present_Value reports on any change. Door_Alarm_State, Update_Time and the Access Point event rows have no runtime application route yet: the new setters AccessDoorObject::set_door_alarm_state, AccessPointObject::set_access_event and CredentialDataInputObject::set_update_time reach the object only before the server holds it, so the wire tests replace the stored object and run the fanout.

#1131 made Door_Alarm_State, Door_Status and Lock_Status writable while Out_Of_Service is TRUE (BACNET-12-ACCESS-DOOR-OUT-OF-SERVICE-SIMULATION), and table_13_1_cov_tests.rs::access_door_simulated_door_alarm_state_reports_and_restores shows a simulated Door_Alarm_State and its restore on the return to service each sending the report.

Not claimed for #1061: Access_Event_Credential, Access_Event_Authentication_Factor and Duty_Window, which the objects don't serve and the reports leave out (#1092); a Load Control Start_Time write route; and the datatypes of Credential Data Input Present_Value, the BACnetTimeStamp rows (Update_Time, Access_Event_Time) and the BACnetShedLevel rows, which the reports carry exactly as ReadProperty serves them.

#1063 gave Controlled_Variable_Value an application route through the BACnetObject::set_controlled_variable_value_internal hook and the existing local-write path, which runs the COV capture under the database lock and fires after the guard drops; the server doesn't follow Controlled_Variable_Reference.

Loop's other required rows are BACNET-12-LOOP-PROPERTY-SET (#1062). #1083 gave the Averaging object an application route through the BACnetObject::add_averaging_sample_internal hook and the same local-write path.

Since #1144 the server also samples Object_Property_Reference itself (BACNET-12-AVERAGING-WINDOW), and those samples fan out to property subscribers as a background commit. Local reading of Clause 13.1: Averaging has no Present_Value and no Table 13-1 row, so it has no whole-object COV criteria and SubscribeCOV stays refused, while Table 13-1a covers its properties.

BACnetObject::supports_subscribe_cov_property (default supports_cov) admits the property forms, and the default supports_cov_property follows it. AveragingObject::add_sample now refuses NaN and infinities. The sliding window, its empty-window INF / NaN / -INF values (#1092) and the server's own sampling (#1144) are BACNET-12-AVERAGING-WINDOW. evidence: Split child of `BACNET-13-COV-SUBSCRIPTIONS` (#985, #988). A Loop's SubscribeCOV notification carries Present_Value, Status_Flags, Setpoint and Controlled_Variable_Value and is sent when Present_Value moves by at least COV_Increment or Status_Flags changes; a Staging object's carries Present_Value, Status_Flags and Present_Stage and is also sent on any Present_Stage change, including the Status_Flags change of a target-plan completion that changes Reliability. Both serve a writable COV_Increment (non-negative finite REAL); Loop serves the required read-only Controlled_Variable_Value.

#1063: a running server's application feeds it with `BACnetServer::set_controlled_variable_value_local` (also in Python), a finite REAL that other objects refuse with OPTIONAL_FUNCTIONALITY_NOT_SUPPORTED and that Out_Of_Service doesn't block, through the `set_controlled_variable_value_internal` hook and the local-write COV path; a SubscribeCOVProperty on it is notified, and a SubscribeCOV report carries the new value the next time it fires (`server/loop_controlled_variable_tests.rs`).

#1083: an Averaging object, which Table 13-1 doesn't list, refuses SubscribeCOV but admits SubscribeCOVProperty and SubscribeCOVPropertyMultiple through the new `BACnetObject::supports_subscribe_cov_property` (default `supports_cov`, which the default `supports_cov_property` now follows); its properties report by Table 13-1a without Status_Flags.

A running server's application feeds it samples with `BACnetServer::add_averaging_sample_local` (also in Python) through the `add_averaging_sample_internal` hook: a BOOLEAN (0 or 1), Signed, Unsigned, Enumerated or finite REAL, converted to REAL; other datatypes fail with INVALID_DATA_TYPE, non-finite REALs with VALUE_OUT_OF_RANGE and other objects with OPTIONAL_FUNCTIONALITY_NOT_SUPPORTED.

The statistics and sample counts change together and notify property subscriptions (`server/averaging_sample_tests.rs`, `averaging/sample_tests.rs`). The server reads the extra values through `BACnetObject::cov_reported_properties` (default keyed by object type) under the Present_Value borrow, omits a declared property missing from Property_List, keeps only trigger values (Present_Stage) in the delivered observation, and sends nothing when a listed value fails to read.

A WriteProperty runs a Staging plan before its own fanout, so a stage change and the completion's flags can share one notification. Local reading of Table 13-1a: SubscribeCOVProperty reports the selected property with Status_Flags, so a Present_Value property subscription carries neither Setpoint nor Present_Stage.

Evidence: `crates/bacnet-objects/src/{traits.rs,traits/defaults.rs,loop_obj.rs,staging.rs}`, `crates/bacnet-server/src/cov/{reported.rs,observation.rs}`, `crates/bacnet-server/src/server/cov_notifications.rs`, `crates/bacnet-server/src/server/{loop_cov_tests.rs,staging_cov_tests.rs}`, `crates/bacnet-objects/src/loop_obj/tests.rs`, `crates/bacnet-objects/src/staging/tests.rs`.

#1061: every type Table 13-1 lists that the stack builds takes SubscribeCOV; Access Point, Credential Data Input and Load Control refused it before. The `cov_reported_properties` default now covers every row with extra values: Access Door Door_Alarm_State (trigger); Access Point Access_Event_Tag, Access_Event_Time (trigger), Access_Event_Credential and Access_Event_Authentication_Factor; Credential Data Input Update_Time (trigger); Load Control Requested_Shed_Level, Start_Time, Shed_Duration and Duty_Window (all triggers); Pulse Converter Update_Time (reported only, #1092).

An Access Point report leads with Access_Event, which doesn't trigger, instead of Present_Value; the server picks that leading value by type (`cov/reported.rs` `lead`), the same property Active_COV_Subscriptions names.

Credential Data Input's Present_Value stays a trigger, which adds no report since Clause 12.36 moves Update_Time on every Present_Value update. Unserved rows (Access_Event_Credential, Access_Event_Authentication_Factor, Duty_Window; #1092) are left out of the reports.

Door_Alarm_State, Update_Time and the Access Point event rows have no runtime route yet; the new setters (`AccessDoorObject::set_door_alarm_state`, `AccessPointObject::set_access_event`, `CredentialDataInputObject::set_update_time`) work before the server holds the object, so the wire tests (`server/table_13_1_cov_tests.rs`, `server/pulse_converter_cov_tests.rs`) replace the stored object and run the fanout; `cov_criteria_tests.rs` pins admission and the reported rows per type.

Not claimed: the Access Door rows Table 12-30 makes writable while Out_Of_Service, a Load Control Start_Time write route, the datatypes of Credential Data Input Present_Value and of the BACnetTimeStamp and BACnetShedLevel rows (reported as ReadProperty serves them), and the server following Loop's Controlled_Variable_Reference.

Averaging's sliding window and no-sample INF / NaN / -INF values (#1092) and the server's own sampling of its Object_Property_Reference (#1144) are `BACNET-12-AVERAGING-WINDOW`; the server samples fan out to property subscribers as a background commit (`server/averaging_sampling_tests.rs`). Loop's other required rows are `BACNET-12-LOOP-PROPERTY-SET` (#1062).

rows.requirement_summary: Single and Multiple commandable Value_Source subscriptions on AO/AV/BO/BV/MSO/MSV report PV, Status_Flags, Value_Source, Last_Command_Time and Current_Command_Priority from one bounded capture. Object PV criteria, flags, source and priority trigger reports; command time alone does not.
notes: Refs #823. Uses #824 producer state without changing source ownership or codecs. Analog PV uses the object increment, not the Value_Source reference increment; binary/multistate use any PV change. Complete constructed CHOICE and companion shape/retention validation precede admission.

Initial/renewal force bypasses only the trigger. Overlapping Multiple fields reuse one capture; only qualified references complete baselines and contribute per-reference timestamps. A qualified explicit selector controls its field timestamp, including false; otherwise implicit companion timestamp intent is ORed as a local overlap policy, not a Standard tie-break claim.

An explicit untimestamped selector keeps its field untimestamped even when it did not qualify (#856); an unqualified explicit timestamped selector adds no companion timestamp and only fills in a time for its own field carried untimestamped by a sibling: the commit time of the value it last saw, a value below its increment included, or the preparation time for a value no producer captured; with no time to give (no valid Device clock) the field is left out (#987).

Failed specialized references do not block independent healthy siblings. Existing route, generation, lifetime, budget and confirmed/unconfirmed completion rules remain. Issue #826 adds same-generation successful preparation ordering through the shared completion owner; its local policy and limits are recorded in BACNET-13-COV-SUBSCRIPTIONS. Other object families and broader product conformance are not claimed.

rows.standard_anchor: Clause 21 (BACnetTimeStamp), Clause 20.2.1.5
rows.requirement_summary: All BACnetTimeStamp producers and consumers share one codec: time [0] as a primitive context tag 0 of length 4 holding raw Time octets, sequence-number [1] constrained to Unsigned (0..65535) and enforced on encode and decode, datetime [2] as an opening/closing tag 2 pair around application-tagged Date and Time, in both bare-CHOICE (SEQUENCE OF member) and field-wrapped forms.
notes: Split child of BACNET-21-FORMAL-APDUS. Resolves the divergent dual-codec defect from #259 per the Clause 20.2.1 tag-form rules: time [0] tags the primitive base type Time, so the primitives codec's primitive-tag form is conformant and the GetEventInformationAck opening-tag-0 form was removed. Golden vectors, 0/65535 boundary acceptance, 65536 and 3-octet overflow rejection, and a cross-call-site primitives<->GetEventInformationAck matrix all run in-tree.
evidence: Split child of `BACNET-21-FORMAL-APDUS`. Resolves the #259 dual-codec defect per the Clause 20.2.1 tag-form rules: `time [0]` tags the primitive base type `Time`, so every producer/consumer now shares one codec — `time [0]` as a primitive context tag 0 of length 4 (raw Time octets), `sequence-number [1]` constrained to Unsigned (0..65535) by its public representation and hostile-wire validation, `datetime [2]` as an opening/closing tag 2 pair around application-tagged Date/Time.

The bare CHOICE form serves `SEQUENCE OF` contexts (GetEventInformation-ACK `eventTimeStamps`); the field-wrapped form serves BACnetTimeStamp-tagged fields (audit, alarm acknowledgment, and event notification) byte-identically to before.

COVNotificationMultiple instead carries independent request DateTime and per-value Time fields. Golden vectors, 0/65535 boundary acceptance, 65536 and 3-octet overflow rejection, wrong-outer-tag / wrong-class-bit / truncated negatives, and a cross-call-site primitives↔GetEventInformationAck matrix run in-tree.

Evidence: `crates/bacnet-encoding/src/primitives/mod.rs` + `primitives/tests.rs`, `crates/bacnet-services/src/alarm_event/get_event_information.rs` + `alarm_event/tests/get_event_information_timestamps.rs`.

rows.standard_anchor: Clause 21 BACnetCalendarEntry, BACnetDateRange, BACnetWeekNDay, BACnetSpecialEvent, BACnetDailySchedule and BACnetTimeValue; Clauses 20.2.1.3.2 and 20.2.1.5; Clause 12.9 Date_List; Clause 12.24 Effective_Period, Weekly_Schedule and Exception_Schedule; Clauses 15.1.1.3, 15.2, 15.8 and 15.9.1.3
rows.requirement_summary: Every BACnetCalendarEntry goes on the wire under its CHOICE tag: date [0] as a four-octet context primitive, date-range [1] as an opening/closing pair around two application-tagged Dates, weekNDay [2] as a three-octet context primitive. Calendar Date_List is the concatenation of its entries. Schedule Exception_Schedule elements are whole BACnetSpecialEvents: the period as the calendar-entry [0] frame around an entry or the calendar-reference [1] object identifier, the [2] time-value frame, and event-priority [3], which decodes as any Unsigned while the Schedule object checks its 1..16 range (VALUE_OUT_OF_RANGE, #1087). Weekly_Schedule elements are BACnetDailySchedule [0] frames of application Time plus primitive value (held typed, so a time-value decodes to and encodes from its own datatype, and a constructed value is refused at encode), and Effective_Period is two application Dates. One codec in bacnet-encoding serves objects, services and tests. Date_List is network-writable: WriteProperty and WritePropertyMultiple replace it (an empty list included) and AddListElement and RemoveListElement edit it. A written value that is not calendar entries is refused with PROPERTY / INVALID_DATA_TYPE, an undecodable entry with INVALID_DATA_ENCODING, a well-formed entry with an octet outside its Clause 21 range (date month 1-14, day 1-34, weekday 1-7; week-n-day month 1-14, week-of-month 1-9, weekday 1-7; date-range ends that are each a specific date or wholly unspecified, per the Clause 12 note on unspecified dates) with PROPERTY / VALUE_OUT_OF_RANGE on WriteProperty and WritePropertyMultiple, and on AddListElement as a ChangeList-Error whose First Failed Element Number is that entry's position (checked in the list handler, since the object judges the edited list as a whole), and more than 1024 entries with RESOURCES / NO_SPACE_TO_WRITE_PROPERTY (NO_SPACE_TO_ADD_LIST_ELEMENT for AddListElement), leaving the list unchanged. The list services decode their elements with the same calendar-entry codec (its own ElementCodec, beside the destination codec of BACNET-15-LIST-ELEMENT-TARGET-KIND), so RemoveListElement matches entries by value and either service refuses an element that is not a well-formed entry with INVALID_DATA_TYPE. Each entry is one list element, so ReadRange addresses entries by position.
public_claims: CHANGELOG.md Unreleased Fixed entry for #1029 and #1028
notes: Split child of BACNET-21-FORMAL-APDUS (#996). Breaking on the wire: Date_List entries went out as an application Date or Octet String, Exception_Schedule dropped each event's period and sent the priority as an application Unsigned, Weekly_Schedule days were lists of Time and Octet String pairs, and Effective_Period was an eight-octet Octet String, NULL until set (it now defaults to the range with both dates unspecified). The codecs moved from bacnet-services::schedule, which is removed, to bacnet-encoding::constructed, and the raw eight-octet BACnetDateRange::encode/decode are removed.

#1029 added the value checks: a date-range end may leave its weekday octet unspecified or inconsistent (Clause 20.2.12 makes the weekday a local matter), and a reversed range is accepted and matches no day.

RemoveListElement has no VALUE_OUT_OF_RANGE in Clause 15.2.1.3.1; since no stored entry is out of range, such an element is absent and the request fails LIST_ELEMENT_NOT_FOUND at its position. #1028 made time-values typed. Present_Value evaluation is BACNET-12-CALENDAR-PROPERTY-SET and BACNET-12-SCHEDULE-EVALUATION. Network writes of the Schedule properties decode with these codecs (BACNET-12-SCHEDULE-WRITES, #1057).

#1087: the special-event codec no longer range-checks event-priority, and BACnetSpecialEvent::event_priority is a u64 so any Unsigned decodes whole; the Schedule object, the codec's only consumer, refuses a priority outside 1..16 with VALUE_OUT_OF_RANGE. The shared list-service element rules (#1027), under which a present entry is left on AddListElement and an absent one refuses RemoveListElement, are in BACNET-15-LIST-ELEMENT-SEMANTICS.
evidence: Split child of `BACNET-21-FORMAL-APDUS` (#996). Each `BACnetCalendarEntry` travels under its CHOICE tag: date [0] (four-octet primitive), date-range [1] (frame around two application Dates) or weekNDay [2] (three-octet primitive).

Calendar `Date_List` is the concatenation of its entries; Schedule `Exception_Schedule` elements are whole special events (calendar-entry [0] frame or calendar-reference [1], the [2] time-value frame, event-priority [3] decoded as any Unsigned and range-checked 1..16 by the Schedule object, #1087), `Weekly_Schedule` elements are [0] daily-schedule frames, and `Effective_Period` is two application Dates.

One codec in `bacnet-encoding::constructed` (`calendar.rs`, `schedule.rs`) serves objects and services; `bacnet-services::schedule` and the raw eight-octet `BACnetDateRange::encode`/`decode` are removed.

`Date_List` is network-writable: WP/WPM replace it (empty included), AddListElement/RemoveListElement edit it, and written non-entries are INVALID_DATA_TYPE, undecodable entries INVALID_DATA_ENCODING and more than 1024 entries NO_SPACE_TO_WRITE_PROPERTY (NO_SPACE_TO_ADD_LIST_ELEMENT for AddListElement), atomically.

The list services use a calendar-entry element codec, so RemoveListElement matches by value and a malformed element is INVALID_DATA_TYPE on either service. One list element per entry lets ReadRange address entries by position.

Breaking on the wire: entries were an application Date or Octet String, `Exception_Schedule` dropped the period and sent the priority as an application Unsigned, `Weekly_Schedule` days were Time/Octet String pairs, and `Effective_Period` was an Octet String, NULL until set (now the range with both dates unspecified).

Evidence: `crates/bacnet-encoding/src/constructed/tests/{calendar,schedule}.rs`, `crates/bacnet-objects/src/schedule/{calendar_tests,tests}.rs`, `crates/bacnet-server/src/handlers/tests/calendar_date_list.rs`, `crates/bacnet-server/src/handlers/tests/read_rpm/{calendar,schedule}.rs`.

#1029: a well-formed entry with an octet out of its Clause 21 range (month 1-14, day 1-34, weekday 1-7, week-of-month 1-9, date-range ends each a specific date or wholly unspecified) is VALUE_OUT_OF_RANGE on WP and WPM, and on AddListElement a ChangeList-Error naming that entry's position, atomically; RemoveListElement has no such error, and since no stored entry can be out of range it fails LIST_ELEMENT_NOT_FOUND at that position.

#1028: time-values are typed `PropertyValue`s; the encoders refuse a constructed value. Present_Value evaluation is `BACNET-12-CALENDAR-PROPERTY-SET` and `BACNET-12-SCHEDULE-EVALUATION`. Network writes of the Schedule properties decode with these codecs (`BACNET-12-SCHEDULE-WRITES`, #1057). The shared list-service element rules are `BACNET-15-LIST-ELEMENT-SEMANTICS` (#1027).

rows.standard_anchor: Annex A
rows.requirement_summary: PICS output is generated as draft internal support evidence until formal BTL/PICS evidence exists.
notes: Issue #838 generalizes the Audit Reporter property fold to every configured instance of each object type. Presence and readable/writable capability are unions; optional is AND across present rows, so a required declaration wins and missing rows do not vote.

Ascending property-ID order applies even to single-instance output. Text and Markdown explain instance-dependent availability/access. Each served Device uses the #834 execution view before folding; standalone object declarations stay raw.

Type-level factory/deletion flags and runtime File behavior are unchanged. This is draft internal capability evidence, not per-row instance counts or a certification claim. WP, WPM and network-equivalent write_local reject assignment to executor-owned Device PSS, both COV lists and Property_List before custom writers, preserving existing validation/authorization and WPM successful-prefix/offending-coordinate semantics; direct object/database mutation remains raw.

Issue #834 makes served Device reads executor-owned for their complete PSS, COV presence/values, Property_List and selector/index definitions. Full-server wire RP, budgeted RPM, read_local and generate_pics use fixed EXECUTED_SERVICES with existing clock filtering, even after public Device profile mutation, same-OID replacement or opaque custom readers/metadata.

Both COV lists are present on every served Device; only the selected minimum instance gets live values and other Devices get empty lists. Endpoint server roles execute exactly RP or RP+WP and expose neither COV list; incompatible identity declarations fail before ingress even without WP, while WP profile commit remains after all validation.

ClientOnly has no responder and retains a local declaration. Standalone built-in Device metadata/direct reads follow declared services: 152 iff SubscribeCOV or SubscribeCOVProperty, 481 iff Multiple; present raw lists are empty.

Context-free RP/RPM and standalone PicsGenerator retain raw declarations. No runtime service-disable switch, general database guard, discovery rebinding, or conformance-status promotion is claimed. This ledger does not claim certification.

rows.standard_anchor: Annex J
rows.requirement_summary: Original-Broadcast-NPDU frames are encoded, decoded, and routed according to BACnet/IP broadcast semantics.
notes: Generic BVLL envelope coverage exists. J-04 Original-NPDU evidence covers BBMD handling of Original-Broadcast-NPDU: local delivery uses sender B/IP MAC, remote BDT peer and registered FDT targets receive Forwarded-NPDU with the original sender encoded, and the BBMD does not echo the already-local broadcast back onto the local subnet as Forwarded-NPDU.

J-09 adds platform socket evidence for Annex J local broadcast prerequisites: the B/IP socket binds INADDR_ANY for subnet/limited-broadcast reception while retaining the configured interface in the local B/IP MAC, and SO_BROADCAST is enabled for Original-Broadcast-NPDU sends.

J-10 adds B/IP send-path evidence that Clause 6 global-broadcast and remote-broadcast NPDUs preserve DNET, DLEN 0 broadcast DADR, Hop Count, and APDU bytes unchanged inside Annex J Original-Broadcast-NPDU. Additional malformed/unsupported-path coverage remains open.
evidence: J-04 Original-NPDU evidence covers BBMD Original-Broadcast local delivery, BDT/FDT Forwarded-NPDU fanout with original sender preservation, and no local Forwarded-NPDU echo. rows.standard_anchor: Annex J
rows.requirement_summary: Forwarded-NPDU includes a valid originating BACnet/IP MAC and preserves source-address semantics.
notes: J-04 covers generic originating-address parsing, truncated-address rejection, BBMD delivery with originating B/IP source MAC, FDT fanout preserving the origin, local rebroadcast for unicast peer arrivals, directed-broadcast peer local-rebroadcast suppression, and no onward forwarding to other BDT peers.

Original-Broadcast fanout covers BDT/FDT Forwarded-NPDU emission with original sender preservation and no local echoed Forwarded-NPDU. Non-BDT Forwarded-NPDU evidence verifies rejection before local delivery, local rebroadcast, BDT fanout, or FDT fanout.

DBTN evidence covers registered foreign-device fanout to local broadcast, BDT peer, and non-origin FDT peer while preserving the origin, excluding origin echo, checking for no extra duplicate frames, and returning X'0060' when deterministic local Forwarded-NPDU forwarding fails.

#937 adds the BBMD's own broadcasts: besides the local Original-Broadcast-NPDU, the BBMD sends a Forwarded-NPDU whose originating address is its own B/IP address to its BDT peers and registered foreign devices, after a fresh start and after a restart; a server-level test shows a remote-subnet client discovering the BBMD's own device from that I-Am.

Fanout throttling and queue overflow are counted and never fail the local send, and plain and foreign-device modes do not forward. A Forwarded-NPDU that arrived by broadcast, to the configured broadcast address or 255.255.255.255, already reached the local subnet, so it is never rebroadcast locally even from a full-mask BDT peer; it is still delivered and sent to foreign devices, while the same frame by unicast is rebroadcast. This also stops echo loops through a BDT row that is the BBMD under another address.

rows.standard_anchor: Annex J.4/J.5
rows.requirement_summary: BBMD Broadcast Distribution Table write/read/ACK behavior and peer broadcast fanout are validated.
notes: J-03 covers read/write BDT caller paths, replacement semantics, malformed Write-BDT NAK without table mutation, self-entry insertion without overflow, and directed-broadcast forwarding target calculation.

J-04 adds Forwarded-NPDU BDT mask behavior: full-mask peers require local rebroadcast, directed-broadcast and unknown peers skip it, Forwarded-NPDUs are not forwarded onward to other BDT peers, and non-BDT senders are rejected before BDT fanout.

Original-Broadcast fanout covers one remote BDT target and verifies no local Forwarded-NPDU echo. DBTN fanout covers a registered foreign-device request forwarded to a BDT peer plus local broadcast and FDT targets without extra duplicate frames.

J-07 adds project ACL evidence: Write-BDT is answered with the standard NAK whatever the sender, listed or not, and the table is unchanged; a listed management sender may delete an FDT entry, while unlisted senders get the Delete-FDT-Entry NAK with the BDT and FDT unchanged.

J-08 adds BDT persistence evidence: an externally provisioned wire-format BDT file is loaded at startup in preference to the configured BDT, inbound Write-BDT (valid or malformed) changes neither the table nor the file, and invalid persisted bytes fall back to the configured BDT without accepting malformed state.

J-11 adds client-side Read-Broadcast-Distribution-Table-Ack validation that rejects malformed payload lengths not divisible by the Annex J.2.4 N*10 BDT entry size. J-12 adds raw BBMD Read-Broadcast-Distribution-Table-Ack wire evidence for ACK function code and N*10 BDT entry bytes.

J-13 adds reproducible BBMD stress benchmark A/B runner evidence with ignored raw artifacts and a machine-readable result-row schema. #937 extends BDT fanout to the BBMD's own broadcasts: its Forwarded-NPDU goes to every BDT entry except its own, as the directed broadcast of a one-hop peer's subnet or by unicast to a two-hop peer, and to each registered foreign device, under the same fanout budgets and counters as forwarded input.

A BBMD bound to 0.0.0.0 takes its own address, and so its self row, from the BDT it starts with: the single row at a local IPv4 address and the bound port, else a default-route address that is local and not loopback.

Several such rows or no usable address fail start without consuming the configuration. A persisted BDT that loads is authoritative, so a failure to choose from it fails start instead of falling back to the configured BDT.

#952 lists local IPv4 addresses on Windows with GetAdaptersAddresses, as getifaddrs does on Unix, so the same rules apply on every platform, and a 0.0.0.0 start fails if the addresses cannot be listed.

Each start of a wildcard BBMD chooses again; the appended self row follows the new address while listed rows stay, a failed restart (ambiguous rows, or a new self row that would overflow the 128-entry BDT) leaves the BDT and FDT as they were, and an explicit-interface restart keeps its address without choosing.

A wildcard BBMD broadcasting to 255.255.255.255 from an own address other than the default-route address warns that its echo may come back from another interface. As a backstop against echo loops whatever the own address, a Forwarded-NPDU that arrived by broadcast (the configured broadcast address or 255.255.255.255) is never rebroadcast locally, even from a full-mask peer, and still goes to foreign devices.

Final encoded BVLC limits only, not Max-NPDU; ingress5705 unchanged. Every nonforwardable ACK is silent. Local/preregistered eligible Request retains 7/150 UNEXPECTED_DATA, original ResultFor2/ID, marker zero, no options/detail, destination=valid origin or absent, same socket only; no origin lookup or preregistration transit/commit. Broadcast/reserved origins and registered explicit-origin transit are silent. This unsupported-local policy is not AB.3.3 node behavior or full field-validation/diagnostic-priority conformance. ResultFor2 and ResultFor3 ACK/NAK join the guarded return path under destination-match unicast with stamped origin and no self echo (AB.5.1/AB.5.3.2); 0x03 answers the AR initiator as a unicast response (AB.2.7) via the hub (AB.4.1); Result-for-Result stays dropped, no Result-on-Result. Rejection has no activity/probe/identity/limits/registry/deadline effects. Accepted transit follows existing NPDU/Unknown activity including missing/capped targets; self drops before activity. Pending ACK timeout was already independent, not an ACK-evasion fix. Existing source/target retirement/replacement, absolute preregistration 5s deadline, cleanup and immediate-send-error policy remain, no new timers or write budgets. Fresh two-variant semantic fixtures, held-sink cancellation/stop/capacity evidence and installed native public hub/raw A-B Request-ACK-Result plus healthy real native third-peer ReadProperty qualify transit only; raw B owns AR semantics. NODE production/fatal ResultFor2 policy unchanged. Connector freshness is a caller contract. Only current/retained-initial-primary ownership is tracked, not an unbounded poisoned-Arc history. Buffered bytes and already-admitted application sends are not rolled back; logical retirement is not immediate OS closure. Strict pre/post-poll checks and chunked timer registration avoid accepting expired ready sends or new overflow panics for huge accepted u64 settings. Base 135-2020 AB.3.1.4/.5 NAK rules and remaining-parts qualification remain; AB.6.1/.2 and AB.6.3 do not prescribe this local budget/retirement policy. Real-clock Rust and production TLS write-lock gates cover expiry, not OS backpressure; installed-native smoke covers NAK/ReadProperty and explicit fresh starts, not 60-second expiry or automatic native reconnect. Cooperative timer-enabled runtime and available state locks are assumed, not hard real-time scheduling. Other write paths, general forwarding/Address-Resolution-ACK and graceful shutdown are excluded. See standard-135-2020-ledger.md#rejection-nak-budget-and-fresh-only-recovery. No full Annex AB claim, support promotion, historical/status change or reopening of #513/#517.

notes: AB-03 adds native Connect-Accept message-id matching evidence, preserves the Connecting state when a pure state-machine response does not match the pending Connect-Request, and makes the async native handshake fail/disconnect on a mismatched response.

Native Connect-Accept handling now requires the fixed AB.2.11.1 26-byte payload before entering Connected, stores peer Max-BVLC-Length and Max-NPDU-Length, advertises local Max-BVLC-Length, rejects outbound NPDUs or encoded BVLC frames that exceed peer limits, and discards oversized inbound WebSocket payloads before BVLC processing.

The hub stores client Max-BVLC-Length and Max-NPDU-Length from Connect-Request, advertises its own limits in Connect-Accept, rejects non-26-byte Connect-Request payloads, drops inbound frames above the hub limit before decode, and filters unicast/broadcast relay targets by each recipient's negotiated NPDU and encoded BVLC limits.

The hub BVLC-Result NAK builder now takes typed BACnet ErrorClass/ErrorCode values; duplicate client or hub VMAC collisions are encoded as COMMUNICATION/NODE_DUPLICATE_VMAC (7/151) instead of raw 1/1, and known-but-invalid functions are no longer classified as BVLC_FUNCTION_UNKNOWN.

AB-07 stores each hub client's Device UUID, accepts known-UUID Connect-Request replacements, sends a WebSocket Close to the superseded connection, wakes the superseded handler, keeps superseded sinks from relaying or removing the replacement entry, and revalidates both source and recipient closed tokens immediately before relay writes so marked-superseded sinks are not written after replacement wins.

It also preserves NODE_DUPLICATE_VMAC NAK behavior for a new UUID that collides with an existing client or hub VMAC. Live generated-certificate WebSocket evidence now requires the superseded connection to receive a Close frame, rejects a second Connect-Request from an already connected client without replacing a peer that it claims, verifies the closed client's original VMAC is no longer reachable, verifies peer reachability after that invalid connected-state transition, and decodes duplicate-VMAC BVLC-Result NAK values at the WebSocket boundary.

Transport receive-loop evidence now covers WebSocket close/error receive paths transitioning the native connection to Disconnected before exit, heartbeat send failures disconnecting before retry/exit, reconnect exhaustion leaving Disconnected, and oversized frame discard.

Existing transport tests also cover connect timeout to Disconnected, Disconnect-Request construction, Disconnect-ACK transition from Disconnecting, and hub Device UUID payload parsing. This tranche adds Annex H.7.3 Random-48 VMAC generation, native Connect-Request BVLC-Result handling that detects COMMUNICATION/NODE_DUPLICATE_VMAC (7/151), requires the BVLC-Result message ID to match the pending Connect-Request before reseeding, disconnects, clears the pending connect, and installs a new Random-48 VMAC before later attempts.

Native duplicate-VMAC reseed failure now blocks failover/retry eligibility so a stale duplicate VMAC is not sent on a subsequent failover Connect-Request. Failed primary-restore probes now copy a successful Random-48 reseed or fail-closed retry-block state back to the active connection before the probe is discarded, preventing later primary-restore or reconnect attempts from reusing a stale duplicate VMAC.

Native connect-time failures now clear the pending Connect-Request on timeouts, invalid Connect-Accept responses, malformed BVLC-Result wires, generic SC decode errors, and WebSocket send/receive I/O errors.

It also adds failover and primary-restore evidence that retry Connect-Requests use the reselected VMAC, primary-restore reseed-failure evidence that no stale-VMAC retry is sent, generic and wrong-message-id Connect-Request NAK evidence that does not reseed.

Remaining AB.6.2 gaps include explicit AWAITING_WEBSOCKET modeling at the WebSocket adapter boundary, accepting-peer connect-wait timeout, Disconnect wait behavior in ScTransport::stop, and reserved VMAC error signaling.

Hub handshake-deadline evidence addresses #520 under Standard 135-2020 AB.6/AB.6.2 and AB.6.2.3. ScHubHandshakeTimeouts exposes checked private Duration fields and independent TLS, HTTP upgrade, and accepting-peer Connect-Request budgets.

Existing start/start_with_uuid methods retain their signatures and delegate to all-10-second defaults; start_with_uuid_and_timeouts accepts explicit checked budgets. TLS/HTTP ranges greater than zero through 300 seconds are local resource policy.

Connect-Request uses the AB.6.2.3 range 5 through 300 seconds and recommended 10-second default. Invalid, zero, below-minimum, above-maximum, and overflow-prone durations are rejected before socket creation.

Absolute phase deadlines begin at TCP admission, TLS success, and WebSocket acceptance respectively. The Connect budget covers all pre-registration message processing, registry/sink lock waits, and responses; ignored, malformed, oversized, Ping, and nonqualifying traffic do not restart it.

An explicit per-message expiry check also prevents continuously ready input from starving the timer. Expiry wins readiness ties, with a clock check under the registry lock immediately before the first irreversible removal, closed marking, or insertion.

A valid admission before expiry retires the timer and commits registry/client_vmac synchronously without an await; a commit notification permanently switches to awaiting the established handler without deadline cancellation.

Connect-Accept transmission after commit and ordinary sink-identity cleanup retain existing behavior. Expired upgraded peers receive no timeout-specific NAK; the hub attempts Close within a separate one-second local grace that includes sink lock and send, then releases its owned resources.

This bounded best-effort close is a local fallback under AB.7.5.5, not full reciprocal-close-handshake conformance. TLS/HTTP timeout drops the owned stream. The existing cap is 512 total active accepted connections, including established clients.

Its RAII guard now exists at admission and is carried into the task, so abort before first poll, mid-TLS abort, errors, and timeout release the slot. Generated-certificate mTLS/TLS/WebSocket tests cover silent and partial TLS, silent and partial HTTP after successful TLS, observable Connect-timeout Close, held registry/NAK/heartbeat/Text-Close sinks, no late insertion or incumbent UUID eviction, exact expiry, and valid admission just before expiry.

The blocked-Accept test makes timer and commit notification ready together, verifies the established handler survives, receives the correct Accept, and completes ordinary identity cleanup. Timer-wakeup tests allow two millisecond ticks for Tokio Sleep granularity; exact admission tests use the exact Instant boundary.

The resource test exercises the actual production 512-slot cap with explicit admission-count barriers, rejects the 513th stalled connection, expires all slots, then completes a legitimate mTLS BVLC Connect session and verifies established-slot retention and cleanup.

No reduced-cap substitute is used. Omitting commit-time deadline retirement defeats the blocked-Accept wire regression; the temporary mutation was restored. Dispatch/cleanup moved intact to a private handler module for file-size maintenance, apart from the deadline checks and test barriers.

Broader connection lifecycle audit (#476), reciprocal close completion, detached-task shutdown/drain, established send bounds, replacement rollback or Accept-send-failure cleanup (#525), WebSocket frame allocation (#516), UUID/advertised-capacity validation, and Python/CLI timeout options remain outside this evidence.

Public support status, global source pins, and other ledger rows are unchanged; no addenda-wide conformance claim is introduced. Subsequent #516 resource evidence supersedes the prior WebSocket-allocation exclusion and prior 1476-byte full-message defaults.

Base 135-2020 AB.5.1 requires the hub workload of 1497 NPDU bytes plus 4192 combined encoded Destination/Data Option bytes, including their marker/length overhead. AB.2.1-AB.2.3 envelope arithmetic yields a supported full receive capacity of 5705 (16+4192+1497); valid source-free hub ingress is 5699 and broadcast forwarding adds six source-VMAC bytes under AB.5.3.3.

The hub advertises 5705/1497, preserves option bytes and payload exactly for unicast/broadcast, and drops its own 1498-byte NPDU before activity updates or relay construction, even for willing recipients.

Node ConnectRequest defaults now advertise full BVLC 5705 while retaining NPDU 1476; negotiated outbound peer limits remain separate. Both production WebSocket creation paths use explicit tungstenite 0.29.0 frame and aggregate-message limits: hub 5705, initiating adapter 65535.

The initiating adapter retains its public Vec receive contract and mutable u16 local-capacity domain: its first Vec copy is bounded by 65535, while existing handshake/established protocol checks apply current lower full-message limits before decoder allocation.

Post-start mutation and independent NPDU rejection are tested. Existing active-retry reset still restores defaults before the reconnect probe; this slice adds no capacity-persistence promise. Both configurations use 4096-byte read/write targets and a 131098-byte maximum write queue, allowing independently larger outbound peer capacities and framing.

A WouldBlock sink proves two full u16-sized messages fit and a third fails with WriteBufferFull. The hub retains Binary Bytes through its initial full-length check. RFC 6455 sections 5.2, 5.4 and 10.4 framing tests cover declared max+1 headers with no body through real mTLS production constructors, cumulative fragment overflow, inclusive maxima, Ping interleaving, registered/unregistered cleanup and healthy-peer service.

The exact 65535-byte node fixture uses NPDU 61327 plus 4192 encoded options and both VMACs, consistent with Table 6-1. Removing the cumulative-message cap defeats the fragmentation regression; mutation restored before gates.

The opt-in release memory harness uses identical baseline/candidate source, isolated actual ScHub or TlsWebSocket receiver children with two Tokio workers, parent-owned attackers and PID-only sysinfo sampling after mTLS/Connect/heartbeat warmup.

On Apple M5 macOS 27 with Rust 1.97.1 and sysinfo 0.39.6, all eight N1 calibrations and forty alternating N16 trials completed without failures; every candidate peer had positive read EOF/error rejection, while baseline peers remained open after full offered traffic.

With at most 8MiB offered per peer and one-second residence, candidate N16 attack-peak minus established-idle median RSS was at most 0.25MiB, below the predeclared 32MiB envelope; all N1 trials met 17MiB.

Baseline N16 deltas ranged 109.656-133.672MiB. Sampling was nominally 10ms (actual N16 median 11.937ms, maximum 34.332ms), not continuous heap-peak observation. Zero-clamped RSS deltas do not mean zero allocation; buffers may overallocate and no total-memory, throughput, latency, or other-platform bound is claimed.

Timeouts and nonterminal writes are incomplete trials, never rejection success. The ignored harness records all phase samples, per-peer actual written bytes, rejection evidence and trial outcomes; local artifacts are retained for PR evidence.

Existing TLS/mTLS/subprotocol rules, handshake deadlines, identity cleanup, peer relay limits, and public support status remain unchanged. Full close/shutdown/send lifecycle, replacement rollback, UUID/option semantics, new dependencies/CI and public configuration APIs remain outside this slice.

Subsequent owned-hub shutdown evidence supersedes only the detached-task shutdown/drain exclusion. ScHub.stop seals synchronous task admission, cancels and joins listener-owned heartbeat, accepted-connection and replacement-close work, then clears the registry.

Its retained join survives cancellation; Drop sends a sticky eventual-cleanup request under a live runtime. Real TLS/WebSocket tests cover every handshake stage, established peers, held Accept/ACK/unicast/heartbeat/replacement sinks, zero admissions and no hub-owned sink references at stop completion, listener reuse, and completed-task reaping.

Spawn/seal races and unpolled/rejected captures are covered; restoring a detached helper or prematurely taking the join defeats regressions. Shutdown is forceful local resource policy, without a hard realtime bound or graceful Annex AB.6.2 Disconnect/AB.7.5.5 reciprocal Close claim.

Broader per-client blocked-send/replacement lifecycle (#525) and public lifecycle audit (#476) remain open; row status and source pins are unchanged. Subsequent partial #525 evidence moves the registration lease outside cancellable dispatch and updates it at the existing locked commit.

Externally signaled retirement interrupts the entire Accept/ACK/relay wait; a monotonic closed predicate plus registered multi-waiter notification also releases senders targeting that identity. Replacement signals immediately and the old owner performs same-sink registry cleanup and a separate five-second local Close/flush attempt, superseding the separate replacement helper.

Admission remains owned through cleanup; global stop still cancels and joins all workers. NPDU unicast/broadcast and forwarded Result retire only the captured target on tungstenite 0.29 ConnectionClosed, AlreadyClosed, Protocol(SendAfterClosing), or Io except WouldBlock; capacity/buffer failures and existing timeout policy remain unchanged.

Tests cover stale target failure queued behind replacement, nonterminal target usability, spurious/late/multiple waiters, actual heartbeat timeout sweep and send_request completion failure, and in-flight target-send cancellation.

Real mTLS acceptance repeats each of six included paths 513 times (3,078 cases), checking admission/task/registry recovery each iteration and fresh healthy recovery; repeated heartbeat retirement signals are distinguished from separate detector-boundary tests.

Corrected named heartbeat fixtures and restored cancellation/terminal/identity mutations provide failure-sensitive evidence. This remains partial #525: the sole blocked reader cannot observe a new peer EOF/Close without external retirement, ordinary task-panic cleanup and send-timeout policy outside the bounded relay attempts remain deferred; #525 and #476 stay open.

Five seconds is local cleanup policy, not a hard realtime or graceful Annex AB Disconnect/reciprocal Close guarantee. Buffered frames can outlive cancellation and heartbeat snapshot clones can retain sockets; no rollback, retry, no-more-bytes, or synchronous destruction of external references is claimed.

Refs #762: NPDU unicast and addressed opaque transit now use the caller-local attempt policy (default five seconds; configurable under #769), covering sink acquisition and WebSocket send. Timeout releases the source reader without retry, fabricated Result or timeout-only target retirement.

Captured-generation terminal-error retirement remains unchanged. Real mutual-TLS ControlledPeer tests use paused Tokio time to prove a queued healthy-destination frame proceeds after the deadline, the blocked destination stays registered, no timed-out pre-lock frame replays after release, no spurious Result appears, and stop drains admissions/registry/tasks/sinks.

No cancellation rollback or guarantee about already buffered bytes is claimed. Broadcast and forwarded Result bounds remain unchanged. This is local resource policy, not a new Annex AB timing requirement or broader status promotion; #476 remains open.

Refs #767 under #476: one registration decision is computed before the existing operator policy under the same clients lock, then supplies a fixed ScHubRegistrationKind to ScHubAdmissionInput. Initial includes a new UUID at capacity; same-UUID same/moved-VMAC replacement and different-UUID VMAC conflict have distinct labels with no incumbent identifiers.

Conflict takes precedence if a known UUID moves onto another UUID's VMAC. Python replaces its private deny-all boolean with a static allow_all/deny_all/deny_uuid_replacement mode evaluated through this native authority, never a Python callback or duplicate registry.

Default Annex AB.6.2.3 (PDF1406/printed1404) known-UUID acceptance and incumbent close remain; opt-in refusal is local security policy before protocol acceptance, not certificate-principal authentication.

Denial preserves the incumbent and existing RESOURCES/OTHER/admin-denial accounting. Allow still applies standard collision/capacity limits; existing deadline commit, panic-deny and generation/shutdown ownership remain.

Real mTLS tests cover classifications, concurrent same/moved UUID first-winner refusal, live incumbent preservation, collision precedence, full-capacity behavior, policy panic and expired registry wait.

Installed Python tests cover default replacement versus refusal, standard collision NAK, redacted status and constructor-only validation before I/O. No row-status/global-pin or broader support promotion. Fixed-shape outcome evidence is recorded in the #770 scope below.

Refs #769: ScHubProbePolicy replaces wall-clock whole seconds with a single per-Hub monotonic millisecond origin and positive whole-ms checked settings. Defaults remain scan30s/idle60s/ACK-age5s/send5s.

Both ages use strict-exceeds comparisons; ACK age starts at reservation and is only enforced on later serial scans, so it is not a hard closure deadline. Missed ticks use Skip. Only a matching valid ACK refreshes activity and clears pending under the registry lock.

Wrong/invalid ACK, generation/replacement, held-sink and forceful/graceful cleanup evidence is retained. Public TLS config separately controls the transit relay acquisition-plus-send budget (default5s); no timeout-only retirement, retry or fabricated Result is added.

#774 extends this one budget to each concurrent NPDU/opaque broadcast recipient and forwarded Result. Python validates probe/relay timing and existing native sender/global rate policies before credential I/O/bind; installed TLS tests observe configured probes and reconcile delivered broadcasts with sender/global counters. These are local Hub resource/liveness policies, not the initiating-node AB.6.3 configurable3–300s range or a broader conformance promotion. Outcome evidence follows; #476 remains open.

Refs #770: fixed-shape ScHubOutcomeCounts and Python typed outcomes report saturating per-start committed UUID replacement, selected VMAC/capacity refusals, ordered accept-limit drops, TLS/WebSocket/Connect timeout, eligible NPDU/opaque unicast no-target/length-limit/send-timeout/send-error, and actual matching-generation heartbeat retirement including generation exhaustion.

Refusals count decisions, not delivered NAKs; later phase expiry can also count. Malformed, pre-registration, stale-source, self/local, broadcast and forwarded Result traffic are excluded from unicast counts; retired-sink skips do not imply success.

Counters do not control policy and snapshots are not transactional. Tests cover saturation, independent instance ownership, cancellation/stale/ACK-winner negatives, real TLS outcomes and actual established-peer graceful shutdown/restart on the same address/config.

Rust post-stop status and explicit graceful/forced outcomes remain; Python status still errors before start/after stop. Existing admin/broadcast semantics, row status and global pins remain unchanged. #476 acceptance is reconciled separately, with no broad conformance claim.

Refs #774: replace the pre-1.0 unicast-only API with relay_send_budget (Rust checked setter/getter/validator) and relay_send_budget_ms (Python), no aliases. One validated value bounds acquisition plus send for NPDU/opaque unicast, each concurrent broadcast recipient and forwarded BVLC-Result.

Probe/control/cleanup/graceful policies remain distinct; unicast-only outcome counters preserve their exclusions. Real TLS paused-clock tests show healthy broadcast progress with two held sinks, one concurrent budget, source progress, no replay, retained peer/later delivery, Result forwarding and captured-identity replacement safety.

A concurrent real-TLS peer-close wave verifies resource/capacity recovery and joined shutdown without a throughput/timing claim. Installed Python signature/stub, invalid-before-I/O and all-transit-family tests use the final name. Global evidence pins/status remain unchanged; parent acceptance is reviewed separately.
evidence: AB-03 adds native Connect-Accept message-id matching evidence, strict 26-byte Connect-Accept payload handling, negotiated Max-BVLC/Max-NPDU limits, and native async handshake failure/disconnect evidence.

AB-07 adds Device UUID replacement, superseded WebSocket close, duplicate-VMAC NAK signaling for new-UUID collisions, and live generated-certificate evidence around replacement and invalid connected-state transitions.

This tranche adds Annex H.7.3 Random-48 VMAC generation, initiating-peer Connect-Request BVLC-Result NAK COMMUNICATION/NODE_DUPLICATE_VMAC (7/151) detection, native failover retry evidence using the reselected VMAC, generic Connect-Request NAK no-reseed evidence. notes: AB-06 adds hub connector/forwarding evidence for Annex AB.5.3.2, AB.5.3.3, and AB.5.4. Hub-bound Encapsulated-NPDU messages now carry Destination Virtual Address and omit Originating Virtual Address; local receive logic accepts hub-relayed unicast with no Destination Virtual Address and drops non-broadcast Destination Virtual Address from hub relay.

The hub rejects forwarding attempts with an Originating Virtual Address or missing Destination Virtual Address, selects only the matching VMAC for unicast, discards unknown unicast destinations by producing no recipient, fans broadcast to all current hub connections except the origin, preserves Message ID/payload/destination options/data options, adds the sender Originating Virtual Address, strips Destination Virtual Address for unicast forwarding, and preserves broadcast Destination Virtual Address for broadcast forwarding.

Live generated-certificate WebSocket evidence covers three connected clients: A-to-B unicast reaches only B with the required VMAC transformation and option preservation, A-to-unknown unicast reaches no client, and A broadcast reaches B and C but not A while preserving the broadcast Destination Virtual Address.

AB-07 adds live generated-certificate WebSocket evidence that a known Device UUID replacement moves hub reachability to the replacement VMAC, prevents old-VMAC unicast delivery, requires a Close frame for the superseded connection, prevents marked-superseded source or recipient sinks from relaying after replacement wins, and preserves peer reachability after rejecting a connected client's second Connect-Request.

Transport connector evidence now covers initial primary timeout to failover, established primary loss with reconnect exhaustion, failover Connect-Request/Connect-Accept, connection state update, active unicast send-path swap to the failover hub, and primary restoration while failover is active.

Primary restoration uses a separate probe connection, sends a best-effort Disconnect-Request to the failover hub after the primary Connect-Accept succeeds, swaps the active transport path back to the primary hub, and verifies subsequent unicast traffic is sent to the restored primary.

AB.5.1 live generated-certificate WebSocket evidence in `sc_hub::ws_capacity_tests` covers a 1497-octet NPDU plus 4192 octets of encoded Destination Options and Data Options through both unicast (5699-octet relayed BVLC) and broadcast (5705-octet relayed BVLC), preserving options and payload.

The hub advertises 5705-octet Max-BVLC and 1497-octet Max-NPDU capacities and drops a 1498-octet NPDU before relay or activity refresh. Recipient-limit decision tests cover independent NPDU and final encoded BVLC bounds; unicast and broadcast relay apply each recipient's negotiated limits, so the node's historical 1476-octet NPDU default (1478 after #893) is not a hub capacity limit.

Existing 31 minimum-size Destination Options plus 31 minimum-size Data Options remain covered by relay-helper and live WebSocket unicast tests, with helper broadcast preservation. This slice also adds explicit unsupported direct-connection classification evidence: the hub WebSocket subprotocol selection rejects `dc.bsc.bacnet.org`, and a connected hub client sending Address-Resolution receives a BVLC-Result NAK with COMMUNICATION/UNEXPECTED_DATA rather than BVLC_FUNCTION_UNKNOWN.

Configured hub URI evidence covers the production TlsWebSocket::connect parse boundary preserving the configured wss authority, port, path, and query before dialing; malformed or hostless configured hub URIs are rejected before any WebSocket/TLS dial.

ASHRAE Addendum cc to 135-2020 changes AB.5.3.1 hub-connection metadata and Network Port properties but does not change these forwarding, replacement, reconnect-failover, option-preservation, configured/malformed hub URI, or direct-connection unsupported-classification behaviors. No remaining hub connector gaps are tracked in this row.
evidence: AB-06 adds hub connector/forwarding evidence: hub-bound Encapsulated-NPDU uses Destination VMAC present and Originating VMAC absent; local receive drops hub-relayed non-broadcast Destination VMAC; hub rejects Originating-VMAC-present or missing-Destination forwarding attempts; unicast selects only the matching VMAC and unknown unicast has no recipient; broadcast targets all current hub connections except origin; relay preserves Message ID/payload/destination options/data options, adds sender Originating VMAC, strips Destination VMAC for unicast, and preserves broadcast Destination VMAC.

Live three-client WebSocket evidence covers A-to-B unicast, A-to-unknown discard, and A broadcast to B/C but not A. AB-07 adds live WebSocket evidence that known Device UUID replacement moves hub reachability to the replacement VMAC, prevents old-VMAC unicast delivery, requires a Close frame for the superseded connection, prevents marked-superseded source or recipient sinks from relaying after replacement wins, and preserves peer reachability after rejecting a connected client's second Connect-Request.

rows.requirement_summary: The Event Enrollment evaluator honors both delays and executes transition actions for every indicated transition. pTimeDelay (Event_Parameters.Time_Delay per Table 12-15) gates transitions into OFFNORMAL states; pTimeDelayNormal - the EE object's new optional Time_Delay_Normal property (Unsigned, Table 12-14 O, writable under the Clause 12.1.2 option, read-back falling back to Time_Delay per Clause 13.3's use of pTimeDelay for an absent pTimeDelayNormal) - gates transitions to NORMAL. The pending countdown is owned by the EE object in-memory behind a guarded internal trait channel (mirroring set_event_state_internal, #130) and advances once per evaluation pass of the event_enrollment_task interval (#133): condition-revert cancels, a redundant qualifying observation never re-seeds (Clause 13.3: the delay runs from when the condition began to hold), a changed target re-seeds with the new target's direction delay, and a parameter change mid-pending (parameters and the effective TDN are fingerprinted per pass) cancels and re-gates. Per Clause 13.2.2.1.4 the actions run for transitions with identical source and destination states too: the SPECIFIC returned state is stored (a HIGH_LIMIT result cannot be replaced with OFFNORMAL in Event_State), the Acked_Transitions bit is maintained per Clause 13.2.3 (cleared when the referenced Notification Class's Ack_Required marks the transition ack-owed, otherwise set; an unresolvable class is not-required), and the transition is emitted with its Event_Enable-scoped distribute flag (Clause 12.12 / 13.2.5). Committed Event Enrollment results select their model EventType through the shared EventStateChange selector: FAULT entry, changed-Reliability FAULT re-entry, and recovery select CHANGE_OF_RELIABILITY, while non-FAULT transitions retain the configured algorithm. This slice does not route or emit Event Notifications; that remains #127 / PR-0305. CHANGE_OF_STATE condition (c) (Optional:) is implemented via the retained last-offnormal-causing value so OFFNORMAL->OFFNORMAL re-indicates; CHANGE_OF_BITSTRING condition (c) (Optional:) is deliberately unimplemented and documented. CHANGE_OF_VALUE tracks the Clause 13.3.3 detection baseline (the value at the last indicated NORMAL transition): both criteria compare against it (REAL: |current - baseline| >= a positive pIncrement; BIT STRING: significant masked-bit change), the only indication is NORMAL->NORMAL (Figure 13-10), the baseline advances at each indicated NORMAL transition, and the first observed sample initializes the baseline without indicating (the clause's explicit local matter).
