crates/bacnet-server/src/event_enrollment/tests/delays.rs (manual mutant: pending countdown forced to re-seed every pass is killed by eleven tests across delays.rs, same_state.rs and change_of_value.rs)
notes: Split child of BACNET-12-OBJECT-MODEL (issues #163 delay honoring, #166 same-state transition actions, #137 COV baseline; branch codex/ee-evaluator-delays, tranche C2). Extract verification: Time_Delay_Normal's Table 12-14 row read in the two-column interleave as name/type/conformance triples adjacent to Event_Algorithm_Inhibit O1 and Status_Flags R (16444-16446), its property text located at 16887-16889, and Table 12-15's per-algorithm Time_Delay -> pTimeDelay mapping confirmed for all five evaluated algorithms (16530-16679); Clause 13.2.3 and Clause 13.2.2.1.4 checked against the full clause text (not reproduced here).

Tick semantics: Clause 13.3's delays measure condition persistence in seconds and are honored in wall time: the countdown is seeded with ceil(delay_secs / interval_secs) - never-fire-early ceiling semantics against the actual (>=1s-clamped) event_enrollment_interval_secs (#133), so at the 10s default a 5s delay fires on the ~10s tick, a 15s delay on the ~20s tick, a 25s delay on the ~30s tick, all pinned by start_paused lifecycle tests - and decrements once per evaluation pass.

The interval is builder configuration and the countdown is in-memory, so no runtime rescale exists; a restart re-evaluates with a fresh conversion (the per-pass misreading this supersedes was issue #163's original suggested direction, caught in the PR-#290 review).

Ownership: the pending countdown, the COS last-offnormal value, and the COV baseline live in the EE object (in-memory only, matching the intrinsic detectors' restart semantics) instead of evaluator-side maps, so they survive evaluation cycles and stay object-owned behind guards that refuse writes while detection is disabled; the Clause 13.2.2.1 detection-disabled reset clears all three.

Struct discipline: the EE pending type does NOT reuse the intrinsic PendingTransition - the mechanisms are structurally similar but do not share code across the objects/server boundary (per-cycle vs probe/tick cadence) - and the condition identity additionally discriminates by matched alarm value (COS) or masked monitored bytes (COBS), stricter than the intrinsic detectors' target-only identity.

Fences honored: no notification emission (#127, tranche E - the lifecycle task still only logs), no Event_Time_Stamps/Event_Message_Texts on the EE object (tranche E, #264), no Status_Flags algorithm input (Table 12-15.1) - CHANGE_OF_STATE/COBS conditions here take pStatusFlags as all-FALSE per the standard's own absent-parameter fallback; flagged as tranche-E follow-up.

No intrinsic-detector changes. Deliberately-remained gaps: CHANGE_OF_BITSTRING condition (c) (Optional:, no bitstring baseline retained); OUT_OF_RANGE 13.3.6 (c)/(f) no-delay returns when a limit is disabled (also deferred by BACNET-12-TIME-DELAY-NORMAL); fault-precedence for EE (the evaluator evaluates no reliability term) unchanged and out of scope.

Behavior-change note: two pre-#137 COV tests pinned absolute-magnitude OFFNORMAL indications the standard's Figure 13-10 cannot produce; they were rewritten to the conformant baseline semantics. Custom downstream EE-typed objects that skip the new internal channel degrade fail-closed: evaluation runs, TD=0 transitions fire as before, but nonzero delays never fire and COV never indicates (documented in the trait docs).

PR-#290 review round (runtime+adversary+dataflow lanes): (B1) the countdown originally counted evaluation PASSES while Clause 13.3's delays are seconds - fixed by threading the actual interval in (evaluate_event_enrollments now takes interval_secs; lifecycle passes the clamped period) and seeding remaining = ceil(delay_secs / interval_secs), never-fire-early ceiling semantics; residual behavior documented (builder-config interval + in-memory pending => no runtime rescale; restart re-evaluates with a fresh conversion).

(B2) foreign Event_State wedge: params rewritten to a different algorithm left states the new arm's conditions never name, and the keyed conditions matched nothing forever - each arm now names its reachable set (OOR/FL {NORMAL,HIGH_LIMIT,LOW_LIMIT}; COS/COBS {NORMAL,OFFNORMAL}; COV {NORMAL}) and, outside it, evaluates as from NORMAL and indicates the computed state through the ordinary actions path (delay-gated; COV's recovery installs the sample as the 13.3.3 baseline).

(B3) AcknowledgeAlarm on EE previously failed via the trait default - EventEnrollmentObject now implements the 13.2.3 acknowledgment indication (unconditional idempotent set), refusing OBJECT/NO_ALARM_CONFIGURED per Table 13-10 while detection is disabled; OOS does not gate ack.

(F4) the fingerprint-cancellation is flushed before any later exit (an A->B->A params round-trip can no longer resume a stale countdown; the unreadable-reference exit deliberately precedes the check).

(F5) monitored object+property folded into params_fingerprint. (F2) structured COBS matcher compares over max(mask,value) with zero-filled bytes (was min-width truncation: false OFFNORMAL on prefix match).

(N2) pending value-identity strictness re-anchored on 13.3.2 (c)'s requirement to retain the particular matched value, with (a)'s set-membership condition called out as the stricter deliberate choice.

Added while in the file: TO_NORMAL ack-required coverage and the Event_Enable-vs-ack independence pin. Out of scope per the review: #179 (EE Status_Flags IN_ALARM) stays tranche E. PR-0303 policy gate (#305/D4; repository-local policy, not a normative BACnet requirement): any valid but unavailable monitored observation clears pending delay, the COV baseline, last-offnormal carryover, and monitored-source ownership; restoration or retargeting requires a fresh baseline and the full applicable delay.

Invalid configuration remains on the PR-0302 CONFIGURATION_ERROR path. A transient gap remains ObservationUnavailable and causes no Reliability, Event_State, Acked_Transitions, event-history, or timestamp transition.

Implementation evidence is `crates/bacnet-server/src/event_enrollment/{mod.rs,support.rs,commit.rs}`; exact executable coverage is recorded in this row's PR-0303 continuity and legacy-report test entries.
evidence: Split child of `BACNET-12-OBJECT-MODEL` (tranche C2: #163, #166, #137). The Event Enrollment evaluator honors both delays: `Event_Parameters.Time_Delay` gates OFFNORMAL-directed transitions and the EE object's new optional `Time_Delay_Normal` property gates NORMAL-directed ones (read-back falling back to `Time_Delay` exactly as Clause 13.3 requires; writable as Unsigned per the Clause 12.1.2 option; in `Property_List` and PICS).

The object-owned (in-memory, internal-channel, reset by `Event_Detection_Enable` FALSE) pending countdown advances once per `event_enrollment_task` interval: revert cancels, redundant observations never re-seed, a changed target re-seeds with the new direction's delay, and a mid-pending parameter change (per-pass fingerprint over framed parameters + effective TDN + event type) cancels and re-gates.

rows.standard_anchor: Clause 12.13 (Table 12-16 File_Access_Method), Clauses 14.1 and 14.2 (Incorrect File access method), Clauses 14.1.4.1 and 14.2.4.1 (non-File Object Identifier), Clause 14.2.4.1 (Write to a read-only File), Clause 18 (INVALID_FILE_ACCESS_METHOD, FILE_ACCESS_DENIED, and INCONSISTENT_OBJECT_TYPE), Clause 21 (BACnetFileAccessMethod production; AtomicReadFile/AtomicWriteFile access-method CHOICE)
rows.requirement_summary: The bundled server cross-checks each AtomicReadFile and AtomicWriteFile request's access method against the target File object's declared File_Access_Method before any ACK is encoded or object state is mutated. The request CHOICE maps semantically to the property enumeration (stream request -> STREAM_ACCESS, record request -> RECORD_ACCESS), never by CHOICE tag number (stream is CHOICE [0] but enumeration value 1; record is CHOICE [1] but enumeration value 0). A mismatch, an unreadable property, a wrong property datatype, or an out-of-production raw value fails closed with SERVICES / INVALID_FILE_ACCESS_METHOD for a File object that exposes storage; a File-typed object without storage is refused SERVICES / FILE_ACCESS_DENIED directly after the lookup (see BACNET-14-FILE-STORAGE). AtomicWriteFile refuses a matching-method File whose Read_Only property is TRUE before access-method validation, mutation, or ACK encoding with SERVICES / FILE_ACCESS_DENIED. Both services classify a non-File object identifier as SERVICES / INCONSISTENT_OBJECT_TYPE before the object lookup, so an absent non-File identifier is classified by its type while a missing File object remains OBJECT / UNKNOWN_OBJECT. This row covers only access-method cross-checking, non-File identifier classification, and the read-only AtomicWriteFile refusal; no broader File service support (stream/record storage completeness, append semantics, ReadRange) is claimed.
notes: Narrow row added with #287. The four-way mismatch matrix pins the exact SERVICES / INVALID_FILE_ACCESS_METHOD pairing, response-buffer atomicity, and no-mutation on refused writes. Matching-method stream and record tests pin the Clause 14.2.4.1 SERVICES / FILE_ACCESS_DENIED read-only refusal, byte-identical sentinel response buffers, and unchanged FILE_SIZE and RECORD_COUNT state.

Storage behaviour (stream/record persistence, append, start-position validation, growth cap) is covered by BACNET-14-FILE-STORAGE (#397). Non-File identifier tests (#398) pin SERVICES / INCONSISTENT_OBJECT_TYPE for both present and absent non-File identifiers, OBJECT / UNKNOWN_OBJECT for a missing File object, byte-identical sentinel response buffers, and unchanged read-only precedence for File identifiers. The standard does not sequence the non-File type check against the existence check, so classifying an absent non-File identifier by type is a deliberate choice recorded with #398.

rows.standard_anchor: Clause 12.13 / Table 12-16 and footnotes 1-2 (File object property model; File_Size stream-only conditional writability; Record_Count record-only presence and conditional writability; truncate, clear, local-matter expansion fill; Modification_Date events and Archive reset), Clause 14.1 (AtomicReadFile parameters, End Of File, Service Procedure), Clause 14.2 (AtomicWriteFile parameters, -1 append, Service Procedure, Result(+) position), Clauses 14.1.4.1 and 14.2.4.1 (INVALID_FILE_START_POSITION), Clause 14.2.4.1 (FILE_FULL), Clause 18 (INVALID_FILE_START_POSITION, FILE_FULL, FILE_ACCESS_DENIED), Clause 19.1.3.3 (restore context writes File_Size=0 before rewriting a differently-sized stream configuration file), Clause 21 (Date, Time, and BACnetDateTime), Annex F (AtomicWriteFile append example)
rows.requirement_summary: The bundled server's AtomicReadFile and AtomicWriteFile service handlers reach a File object's contents through the internal FileStorage channel exposed by the BACnetObject file_storage_internal hooks, never through a property. Stream and record reads return the stored octets and records for the requested window, short reads return what remains, and End Of File is authoritative: an empty window at the end of a non-empty file reports FALSE, while a valid built-in empty stream or record read at its only position returns an empty payload with TRUE. Stream and record writes persist, extend the file when the start is past its end (zero octets and empty records as the local-matter fill), keep File_Size and Record_Count coherent, honour -1 as append, and acknowledge the position actually written. Built-in FileObject property resize follows Table 12-16: File_Size is writable only for an exact STREAM_ACCESS instance whose Read_Only is FALSE, and Record_Count is present and writable only for an exact RECORD_ACCESS instance whose Read_Only is FALSE. Wrong access mode, an unknown raw access method, or Read_Only TRUE is refused PROPERTY / WRITE_ACCESS_DENIED before datatype validation; an eligible non-Unsigned value is refused PROPERTY / INVALID_DATA_TYPE. A smaller target preserves the stream or record prefix, zero clears the active data without deleting the object, stream expansion appends zero octets, and record expansion appends empty records. Growth is preflighted against the existing per-object caps and conversion limits before mutation; preloaded contents above a cap may no-op or shrink but may not grow beyond the larger of the cap and current length/count, and a refusal is OBJECT / FILE_FULL. An exact target no-op changes no payload, accounting, clock sample, Modification_Date, or Archive. Every actual property resize commits through set_data or set_records, keeping File_Size and Record_Count coherent before sampling its bound ClockReader once and clearing Archive; adding or removing empty records is a data change even when File_Size remains zero. Built-in FileObject property resizes validate a candidate before committing bytes or records and metadata. A successful resize in a WPM prefix remains committed when a later property fails, and the unprocessed suffix does not modify it. Every successful built-in FileObject set_data or set_records mutation, including equal-content and empty writes reached through those direct APIs or AtomicWriteFile, commits payload and size/count accounting before sampling its bound ClockReader once, stores the exact local Date and Time only for a valid actual datetime, falls back to a fully unspecified Date and Time when clockless or invalid, and clears Archive. A changed direct Modification_Date assignment clears Archive, while an identical assignment preserves it; changing File_Access_Method invokes the same authority only when recomputation changes effective File_Size. Clock binding and rebinding do not timestamp creation or otherwise mutate metadata. A read start that is negative or past the end, or a write start that is negative other than -1, is refused SERVICES / INVALID_FILE_START_POSITION; an AtomicWriteFile growth past the designed limit (1 MiB of octets and 10,000 records by default, the record cap being the workspace decoder's own SEQUENCE OF ceiling so a read-back at the cap stays decodable) is refused OBJECT / FILE_FULL; a File-typed object without storage is refused SERVICES / FILE_ACCESS_DENIED directly after the lookup, as is an AtomicWriteFile request to a File whose Read_Only property is TRUE, unreadable, or not a BOOLEAN (the gate fails closed); a record write whose payload list is shorter than its Record Count is rejected MISSING_REQUIRED_PARAMETER. Every built-in refusal leaves payload, File_Size, Record_Count, Modification_Date, Archive, and the response buffer unchanged. A custom FileStorage implementation owns its metadata contract; a write position outside the ACK's INTEGER range can leave a custom object mutated and still draw DEVICE / INTERNAL_ERROR. A record read returns at most MAX_DECODED_ITEMS (10,000) records in one ACK, the workspace decoder's SEQUENCE OF ceiling; a larger file reads back in windows, with Returned Record Count below the request and End Of File FALSE until the last window. This row covers built-in FileObject storage and conditional property resize behind the BACNET-14-FILE-ACCESS-METHOD gates; custom-backend property resize, restore orchestration, and ReadRange remain outside the storage claim. Mixed-instance PICS capability evidence is tracked separately under BACNET-A-PICS.
notes: Row added with #397, extended for built-in FileObject mutation metadata with #416, and extended for conditional built-in resize properties with #417. AtomicReadFile/AtomicWriteFile gate order remains object type, lookup, storage presence, read-only for writes, access method, then storage start-position and capacity checks.

End Of File is authoritative: an empty window at the end of a non-empty built-in file, including a zero-count read, reports FALSE; a valid read at the only position of a built-in empty stream or record file returns empty data with TRUE.

The growth caps (1 MiB of octets, 10,000 records by default, per object, growth-only so preloaded contents past the cap remain valid) are the designed limit Clause 18 defines FILE_FULL for; the caps are not BACnet properties and never appear in Property_List.

AtomicWriteFile record decoding requires file-record-data cardinality to equal Record Count (#418): a short list is rejected MISSING_REQUIRED_PARAMETER and an extra element is rejected TOO_MANY_ARGUMENTS.

The handler's access-method gate is pinned independently with lax custom storage; FileStorage defaults report FILE_ACCESS_DENIED, never a method mismatch. Built-in mutation metadata is object-owned: ObjectDatabase binds the ClockReader, and FileObject samples only after successful payload/accounting commit.

Custom FileStorage implementations still own their Modification_Date and Archive maintenance; no generic callback or custom-backend resize contract is claimed. Property resize has a separate PROPERTY-class policy: exact access method and Read_Only eligibility precede Unsigned datatype validation, actual changes reuse set_data/set_records, and exact no-ops bypass the clock and metadata.

The retained compatibility snapshot hook directly restores truncated bytes, records, and metadata in object-local tests; bundled-server Service 16 does not invoke it and retains successful file-resize prefix writes.

File PICS tests cover single-instance metadata and mixed writable/read-only stream/record capability unions (#838). Rows sort by raw property ID, including single-instance output; access flags describe at least one configured instance, with concrete-object availability and authorization still checked at runtime.

This draft PICS evidence does not change File storage or resize behavior. Clause 19.1.3.3 explains the File_Size=0 restore use case, but restore orchestration is not implemented here. Other deferrals are custom FileStorage/custom-backend property resize, host filesystem storage, locking beyond the object-database guard, Python/CLI exposure, ReadRange, and unbounded allocation.

The read handler clamps a record window to MAX_DECODED_ITEMS so one ACK never exceeds what the workspace decoder accepts, including files preloaded past the record cap. This is a recorded departure from the Clause 14.1 Service Procedure, which short-reads only when fewer records remain; the clamp adds a second local reason.

Clause 14.1.3.1 makes End Of File data-independent, so a client that continues from start + Returned Record Count still reads the whole file. FileObject::set_data and set_records update File_Size and Record_Count only for the selected channel (any raw value other than RECORD_ACCESS is the stream channel for those local setters), while network property resize requires an exact named access method and set_file_access_method recomputes both on a switch; Record_Count remains present only under RECORD_ACCESS (Table 12-16 footnote 2).
